Check the connection before running Forge operations: Codex users can run codex mcp list , while Claude Code users can run claude mcp list ; /mcp is also available in either client's TUI. Scene queries and edits require the Blender-side Bridge. Reading Skills and searching local documentation do not. mcp-server and addon/Forge are independent components. The former provides agent-side stdio MCP; the latter runs in the Blender instance that owns the scene. See Installation Forge for Blender version requirements. Operating scenes through an agent requires both components. When distributing only mcp-server , keep the source directories forge_mcp/skills and forge_mcp/docs and create the environment with the installation scripts above. Use FORGE_BLENDER_DOCS_DIR to override the default Blender documentation directory. For cross-machine connections, configure the bridge in the add-on preferences or with the background command's --host , --port , and --token options; set FORGE_MCP_HOST , FORGE_MCP_PORT , and FORGE_MCP_TOKEN in the client process. Both sides must use the same token. Non-localhost listeners must use a token and should be protected by a firewall or VPN. The Bridge requires Blender's online-access permission. Without it, the port does not listen. Use --online-mode for background launches, or allow online access in Preferences for GUI sessions. If startup fails, check the Debug error message in Forge preferences. For the complete configuration and environment-variable reference, see mcp-server/README.md .

Global Properties ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_global The dialog contains: Compiler Properties Compiler settings. The Autolimits switch controls automatic range inference. Visual Properties ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_visual The dialog contains Global, Headlight, Map, RGBA, Quality, SSGI, and Tonemapping : Global Properties Global miscellaneous parameters. MJCF reference Headlight Properties Headlight parameters. When Active is disabled, the Headlight sub-parameters cannot be edited. Export writes the Active state to the headlight active attribute as 1/0; import accepts both 1/0 and true/false. MJCF reference Map Properties View-distance and fog settings. MJCF reference SSGI Properties SSGI settings. When Active is disabled, SSGI sub-parameters cannot be edited. MJCF reference Tonemapping Properties Tonemapping settings. The available Forge types depend on the Blender object type: Blender object type Forge types available Additional behavior Empty Link Move to the Link or World Collection and use the LNK_ prefix. Mesh Visual, Collider Initialize as Mesh; Visual uses Group 2 with contact disabled, Collider uses Group 3; use the GEO_ or COL_ prefix. Light Light Area Light is unsupported; initialize a Forge Light and use the LIT_ prefix. Camera Camera Perspective and Orthographic only; use the CAM_ prefix. Enter a numbering placeholder in Numerate ; the number of characters determines the zero padding. Confirm. Names are generated as prefix_number . For example, with New Name arm and Numerate ### , the results are arm_000 , arm_001 , and so on.

docs.text: Chapter 3: Model Define — Geometry and Material ¶ 3.1 Geometry group layout ¶ The Geometry group contains, from top to bottom: Create geometry(s) / Create collider(s) Define geometry(s) / Define collider(s) Create height field / Create plane Check Mesh(s) 3.2 Create Visual Geometry ¶ Button: Create geometry(s) Operator ID: forge.create_geometry Dialog: Available when no object is selected, or when every selected object is a Link , Frame , or Replicate . With no selection, create one Visual in World . With a selection, create one Visual for every selected parent object. Types: Box , Capsule , Cylinder , and Sphere . Dimensions: Box uses the three-axis Size ; Sphere uses Radius ; Capsule/Cylinder use Radius and Height . After creation, the new Visual objects become the current selection. 3.3 Create Collider ¶ Button: Create collider(s) Operator ID: forge.create_collider Dialog: With no object selected: choose Collider type manually Use the selected object's Geometry type Choose Collider type manually Available when: no object is selected; all selected objects are Link/Frame ; or all selected objects are Visual . When Visual objects are selected, there are two Method options: Geometry type: each Collider follows the type of its corresponding Visual . Collider type: every Collider uses one explicitly selected type. Auto size can automatically calculate dimensions for non- Mesh types. For Capsule / Cylinder , Use Min As Height takes the height from the visual's smallest bounding-box axis (and orients the shape along it) instead of the largest; it has no effect without Auto size . With no selection or with Link/Frame selected, creation uses the specified Collider Type and Size . 3.4 Change Geometry / Collider type ¶ Dialogs: Visual Define Collider Define Button Operator ID Applies to Types Define geometry(s) forge.define_geometry_type Visual Box, Capsule, Cylinder, Sphere, Mesh, Sdf Define collider(s) forge.define_collider_type Collider Box, Capsule, Cylinder, Sphere, Mesh, Sdf The dialog starts with the active object's current type and modifies only the active object by default. Enable Apply to all selected to modify the whole selection. Changing type also switches or rebuilds the corresponding shape. SDF uses an existing mesh: define a Visual as Sdf to export type="sdf" with a mesh asset reference. Switching between Mesh and SDF preserves the mesh; switching from a primitive first applies its shape modifier. Converting a primitive to Mesh or Sdf preserves its material slots, material assignments, and active material slot, without changing other objects sharing the original mesh. Colliders also support Sdf . Select a Visual and choose Sdf in Create collider(s) to share its Mesh Data as a linked duplicate, preserving its parent and transform. Vertex edits affect both objects. Use Define collider(s) to change an existing collider. SDF colliders use mesh inertia computation and export as type="sdf" , reusing the visual's mesh asset when shared or an STL asset when exported alone. 3.5 Height Field and Plane ¶ These two buttons are available only when no object is selected, and create the result in World. They currently have no dialog. Button Operator ID Result Create height field forge.create_height_field Create a Height Field; edit detailed parameters in Properties. Create plane forge.create_plane Create a Plane; edit detailed parameters in Properties. 3.6 Mesh Check ¶ Button: Check Mesh(s) Operator ID: forge.mesh_check Available only when every selected object is a Visual . It checks whether the meshes satisfy the requirements of later operations such as inertial calculation and displays errors and elapsed time in the status/report area. Check whether the Visual model is manifold. Check whether Visual models intersect. Compute Inertial validates geometry only when Check Geometry is enabled (off by default), using its chosen Visual / Collider source. If validation fails, repair open, degenerate, or otherwise invalid meshes first. 3.7 Material group ¶ Button: Common Material Operator ID: forge.create_material Dialog: Available when all selected objects are Visual , Height Field , or Plane . It creates a parameter-only material: Choose a Category from the Forge PBR Library . Choose a Material . When Use Existing is enabled, an existing Blender material with the same name is reused first. On confirmation, assign the reused or newly created material to the first Material Slot of every selected object. Reusing preserves existing material settings; creating uses the library parameters. Visual , Height Field , and Plane all use an object-level material slot. A suffix at the end of the material name selects the exported MJCF alpha_mode : Name suffix Exported alpha_mode _blend blend _mask mask _multiply multiply The suffix is part of the material name, so the exported <material name> keeps it as well. Without one of these suffixes the MJCF default opaque mode is used. • Assign an existing material ¶ Button: Assign Material Operator ID: forge.assign_material Dialog: Select one or more Visual , Height Field , or Plane objects. Click Assign Material in the Material group. Choose an existing Blender material from the searchable Material dropdown and confirm. The dialog initially selects the active object's material when available. The selected material is assigned to the first object-level Material Slot of every selected object, creating the slot if needed. Other slots are preserved. This reuses the existing material, including its shader nodes and settings, without creating a copy. Unselected objects keep their assignments, including objects sharing the same mesh. Create or import a material first if none are available. • Create a checker material ¶ Button: Checker Material Operator ID: forge.create_checker_material Dialog: Select one or more Visual , Height Field , or Plane objects, then click Checker Material in the Material group. Every selected object must be one of these types. Parameter Meaning Default Color 1 First checker color Black Color 2 Second checker color White Repeat Integer repeat count along both UV axes, from 1 to 128 4 Confirm to create a new material and assign it to the first object-level Material Slot of every selected object. Each invocation creates a new material; selected objects share that material. The generated shader uses Texture Coordinate (UV) → Mapping → Checker Texture → Principled BSDF (Base Color) . Repeat sets Mapping Scale X and Y; Z remains 1. The Checker Texture node's Scale is 2. Keep this node layout and Scale when editing a checker for MJCF export; adjust tiling with Mapping instead. Export writes a native MJCF <texture type="2d" builtin="checker"> and an RGB texture layer on the material, without baking or writing an image file. Color 1 / Color 2 become rgb1 / rgb2 , with linear Blender colors converted to sRGB. Mapping Scale X/Y becomes the material's texrepeat ; matching values produce texuniform="true" , otherwise false . The texture is written before the material that references it. With Import material enabled, importing an MJCF 2D builtin checker restores the UV, Mapping, and Checker Texture nodes, colors, and texrepeat . Both a material's texture attribute and RGB/RGBA <layer> references are supported. Imported U/V repeat values may differ; the creation dialog's Repeat sets both axes together. • Create a custom material ¶ The image below shows a complete custom material with texture maps. Each of the four framed sections can be disconnected from the BSDF node and replaced with the BSDF's direct parameter. The scene exports either parameters or textures depending on whether a node is connected to the BSDF input. For image textures, follow the node layout above. For procedural checkers, use the checker layout described in the previous section. A parameter-only material does not need any node connected to the BSDF node. If tiling is not required, the Mapping node does not need to be connected to the texture node.

docs.text: Chapter 4: Model Define — Kinematics and Instance ¶ 4.1 Kinematics group layout ¶ Button Operator ID Available when Create link(s) forge.create_link Nothing is selected; all selected objects are Link/Frame/Replicate; or all are Visual/Collider Create joint(s) forge.create_joint All selected objects are Link Mark root forge.mark_root_link All selected objects are Link, Frame, or Replicate Define joint(s) forge.define_joint_type All selected objects are Joint Link Parent forge.define_parent The active object and other selected objects form a valid parent-child relationship Compute Inertial forge.create_inertial All selected objects are Link Mark Instance Link forge.mark_instance_link All selected objects are Link (see 4.7 ) Set instance idname forge.set_instance_idname Selected objects are Link, Frame, or Visual; only unmarked Links are changed 4.2 Create Link ¶ Create link(s) ¶ With no selection, create a top-level Link. With Link/Frame/Replicate selected, create a child Link for each object. With Visual/Collider selected, create a Link from each selected geometry object. Shift + click : reverse the parent relationship — create a new parent Link at each selected Link/Frame/Replicate object's position and orientation, then make that object a child of the new Link, matching Shift + click on Create frame(s) . After creation, the new Links become the current selection. There is no dialog. 4.3 Create and define Joint ¶ Create joint(s) ¶ Create a Joint for every selected Link . Types are Free , Ball , Slide , and Hinge ; the default is Hinge . Define joint(s) ¶ The dialog starts with the active Joint type and modifies only the active object by default. Enable Apply to all selected to modify all selected Joints. Changing type also updates the displayed Joint shape. 4.4 Link Parent ¶ Link Parent always uses the active object as the parent and has no dialog: When the active object is a Link , Frame , or Replicate , every other selected object must be an allowed child: Link , Frame , Replicate , Visual , Collider , Joint , Site , Light , Camera , or Attach . When the active object is a Visual the operator is unavailable: a Collider belongs under the Link , next to its Visual . A Collider inside a Visual is not exported. Existing children of a moved Visual (for example Colliders still bound to it) are reparented under the new active parent first, which repairs a legacy Collider-inside-Visual nesting. Every reparented object also moves into the collection named after its model type — a Visual into Visual , a Collider into Collider , and so on. Objects created at the world root live in World ; parenting them is what moves them out. Procedure: Select the child objects to move. Select the destination parent last, making it active. Click Link Parent . 4.5 Compute Inertial ¶ Select one or more Links and click Compute Inertial . The dialog contains: Parameter Default Behavior Inertial Model Type Visual Use either Visual or Collider geometry Check Geometry Off Validate the collected geometry before calculation; skip the Link if validation fails Collect direct children of the chosen type and recurse through Frame descendants. Child Link hierarchies are excluded; Visual and Collider geometry are not mixed. Box / Sphere / Cylinder / Capsule use solid-shape formulas from their parameters and do not require TetGen. World transforms account for scale (including nonuniform scale), reflections, and shear introduced by parents. Mesh uses evaluated geometry with modifiers applied, then TetGen tetrahedralization. Install TetGen and supply valid geometry suitable for volume calculation. Density comes from each object's Forge_Geometry.density , unless the material in its first material slot has a density custom property, which takes precedence. Mass, center of mass, and inertia are combined across the collected objects. Each successful calculation creates and selects a new Inertial under the Link. Existing Inertial objects are not replaced; remove old ones before recalculating. No new Inertial is created for a Link with no matching geometry, failed validation when enabled, or failed inertia calculation. See the report area for details. Recommended workflow: confirm geometry types, dimensions, and density; select the Link ; choose Visual / Collider in the dialog and enable Check Geometry when validation is needed. The separate Check Mesh(s) button still accepts only Visual objects. Inertial preview ¶ An Inertial is displayed as a box with equivalent mass and diagonal inertia, centered at the center of mass and aligned with the principal axes. Editing mass or inertia updates the display; Gizmo display size does not resize it. Physical position and rotation are stored relative to the parent Link; display scaling does not enter the exported MJCF inertial pose. See Chapter 7 for inertia editing and Chapter 0 for preview toggles. 4.6 Mark root ¶ Writes the Root Link marker to selected Link/Frame/Replicate objects that have no parent. Objects with a parent are disconnected, marked, and accompanied by a warning. There is no dialog. 4.7 Instance rules ¶ Instance reuses one Link subtree (for example, a gripper or wheel) at multiple locations. A marked Instance Link supplies template content; on export, its children are written under every Link that references it. The separate Instance group below Kinematics contains three rows: Mark Instance Link , the Instance field, and Set instance idname . Concepts ¶ Name Marker Description Instance Link (source) INSTANCE_LINK custom property Written by Mark Instance Link and removed by clicking again. It is not exported as a <body> ; if unreferenced, it is not exported at all, including assets. Placeholder Link INSTANCE_IDNAME custom property Written by the Instance field and Set instance idname . The Link itself (name, pose, and properties) is retained; its children are replaced by a copy of the Instance Link subtree. Instance field Forge_Props.instance_body The list contains only marked Instance Links. Procedure ¶ Build a template Link in the scene with its Joints, Visuals, child Links, and so on. Keep it visible at the world root. Select the template Link and click Mark Instance Link . This adds INSTANCE_LINK ; clicking again removes it. Choose the template in the Instance field. Select one or more placeholder Link objects that are not marked as INSTANCE_LINK (normally empty Links created under the destination parent). Click Set instance idname to write INSTANCE_IDNAME . If the Instance field is empty, the references on selected Links are cleared. Export normally; see Chapter 8 . Export rules ¶ The Instance Link itself is not exported as a <body> . When referenced by a placeholder Link, its subtree meshes and material assets are exported with the copies. An Instance Link referenced by no placeholder Link is not exported at all: no <body> and no assets from its subtree are written; a warning is shown. Each placeholder Link exports its own <body> (name, position, quaternion, and properties), while its children are replaced by a complete copy of the template subtree: every copied element name receives the prefix <placeholder Link name>_ (for example, grip_l_finger ); copies do not collide with one another, and an _inst suffix is added if a name still conflicts; Camera and Light target references inside a copy are renamed as well; meshes and material assets from the template subtree are exported once and shared by all copies. Children of the placeholder Link itself are not exported and are not included in asset collection. Global sections ( actuator , sensor , tendon , equality , contact ) are not duplicated per instance and should not refer to element names inside an Instance Link. Notes ¶ INSTANCE_IDNAME stores a reference to the Instance Link object rather than its name, so renaming the template keeps the reference valid. Markers stored as names in older files are still recognized on export. If the object referenced by INSTANCE_IDNAME is deleted or is no longer a Link , the placeholder Link falls back to normal export and shows a warning. A Link already marked as an Instance Link cannot also receive INSTANCE_IDNAME ; it is skipped with a warning. INSTANCE_IDNAME markers inside a template subtree are ignored when copying because the copy is content only. An Instance Link nested inside a template subtree is not copied as a <body> ; its content is exported only through a placeholder Link that references it. If it has no reference, it is not exported. The Instance marker is a Blender-side authoring concept and is not restored when an MJCF file is imported again. MCP calls ¶ forge_mark_instance_link ( select = [ "gripper" ]) # mark / unmark the template forge_set_scene_property ( group = "forge_props" , values = { "instance_body" : "gripper" }) forge_set_instance_idname ( select = [ "arm_l" , "arm_r" ]) # write references on placeholder Links

When the active object is a Visual the operator is unavailable: a Collider belongs under the Link , next to its Visual . A Collider inside a Visual is not exported. Existing children of a moved Visual (for example Colliders still bound to it) are reparented under the new active parent first, which repairs a legacy Collider-inside-Visual nesting. Every reparented object also moves into the collection named after its model type — a Visual into Visual , a Collider into Collider , and so on. Objects created at the world root live in World ; parenting them is what moves them out. Procedure: Select the child objects to move. Select the destination parent last, making it active. Click Link Parent .
docs.title: 4.4 Link Parent

docs.text: Select one or more Links and click Compute Inertial . The dialog contains: Parameter Default Behavior Inertial Model Type Visual Use either Visual or Collider geometry Check Geometry Off Validate the collected geometry before calculation; skip the Link if validation fails Collect direct children of the chosen type and recurse through Frame descendants. Child Link hierarchies are excluded; Visual and Collider geometry are not mixed. Box / Sphere / Cylinder / Capsule use solid-shape formulas from their parameters and do not require TetGen. World transforms account for scale (including nonuniform scale), reflections, and shear introduced by parents. Mesh uses evaluated geometry with modifiers applied, then TetGen tetrahedralization. Install TetGen and supply valid geometry suitable for volume calculation. Density comes from each object's Forge_Geometry.density , unless the material in its first material slot has a density custom property, which takes precedence. Mass, center of mass, and inertia are combined across the collected objects. Each successful calculation creates and selects a new Inertial under the Link. Existing Inertial objects are not replaced; remove old ones before recalculating. No new Inertial is created for a Link with no matching geometry, failed validation when enabled, or failed inertia calculation. See the report area for details. Recommended workflow: confirm geometry types, dimensions, and density; select the Link ; choose Visual / Collider in the dialog and enable Check Geometry when validation is needed. The separate Check Mesh(s) button still accepts only Visual objects.
docs.title: 4.5 Compute Inertial

docs.text: An Inertial is displayed as a box with equivalent mass and diagonal inertia, centered at the center of mass and aligned with the principal axes. Editing mass or inertia updates the display; Gizmo display size does not resize it. Physical position and rotation are stored relative to the parent Link; display scaling does not enter the exported MJCF inertial pose. See Chapter 7 for inertia editing and Chapter 0 for preview toggles.
docs.title: Inertial preview

docs.text: Writes the Root Link marker to selected Link/Frame/Replicate objects that have no parent. Objects with a parent are disconnected, marked, and accompanied by a warning. There is no dialog.
docs.title: 4.6 Mark root

docs.text: Instance reuses one Link subtree (for example, a gripper or wheel) at multiple locations. A marked Instance Link supplies template content; on export, its children are written under every Link that references it. The separate Instance group below Kinematics contains three rows: Mark Instance Link , the Instance field, and Set instance idname .
docs.title: 4.7 Instance rules

docs.text: Name Marker Description Instance Link (source) INSTANCE_LINK custom property Written by Mark Instance Link and removed by clicking again. It is not exported as a <body> ; if unreferenced, it is not exported at all, including assets. Placeholder Link INSTANCE_IDNAME custom property Written by the Instance field and Set instance idname . The Link itself (name, pose, and properties) is retained; its children are replaced by a copy of the Instance Link subtree. Instance field Forge_Props.instance_body The list contains only marked Instance Links.
docs.title: Concepts

docs.text: Build a template Link in the scene with its Joints, Visuals, child Links, and so on. Keep it visible at the world root. Select the template Link and click Mark Instance Link . This adds INSTANCE_LINK ; clicking again removes it. Choose the template in the Instance field. Select one or more placeholder Link objects that are not marked as INSTANCE_LINK (normally empty Links created under the destination parent). Click Set instance idname to write INSTANCE_IDNAME . If the Instance field is empty, the references on selected Links are cleared. Export normally; see Chapter 8 .
docs.title: Procedure

docs.text: The Instance Link itself is not exported as a <body> . When referenced by a placeholder Link, its subtree meshes and material assets are exported with the copies. An Instance Link referenced by no placeholder Link is not exported at all: no <body> and no assets from its subtree are written; a warning is shown. Each placeholder Link exports its own <body> (name, position, quaternion, and properties), while its children are replaced by a complete copy of the template subtree: every copied element name receives the prefix <placeholder Link name>_ (for example, grip_l_finger ); copies do not collide with one another, and an _inst suffix is added if a name still conflicts; Camera and Light target references inside a copy are renamed as well; meshes and material assets from the template subtree are exported once and shared by all copies. Children of the placeholder Link itself are not exported and are not included in asset collection. Global sections ( actuator , sensor , tendon , equality , contact ) are not duplicated per instance and should not refer to element names inside an Instance Link.
docs.title: Export rules

docs.text: INSTANCE_IDNAME stores a reference to the Instance Link object rather than its name, so renaming the template keeps the reference valid. Markers stored as names in older files are still recognized on export. If the object referenced by INSTANCE_IDNAME is deleted or is no longer a Link , the placeholder Link falls back to normal export and shows a warning. A Link already marked as an Instance Link cannot also receive INSTANCE_IDNAME ; it is skipped with a warning. INSTANCE_IDNAME markers inside a template subtree are ignored when copying because the copy is content only. An Instance Link nested inside a template subtree is not copied as a <body> ; its content is exported only through a placeholder Link that references it. If it has no reference, it is not exported. The Instance marker is a Blender-side authoring concept and is not restored when an MJCF file is imported again.
docs.title: Notes

docs.text: forge_mark_instance_link ( select = [ "gripper" ]) # mark / unmark the template forge_set_scene_property ( group = "forge_props" , values = { "instance_body" : "gripper" }) forge_set_instance_idname ( select = [ "arm_l" , "arm_r" ]) # write references on placeholder Links

docs.text: Chapter 5: Model Define — Hardware ¶ 5.1 Hardware group layout ¶ From top to bottom, Hardware contains Create Actuator/Site , Define Actuator/Site , Create Tendon/Equality , Create Sensor/Contact , and Create Light/Camera . 5.2 Actuator ¶ Create actuator(s) ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_actuator All selected objects must be Link , Joint , or Tendon . Forge creates one Actuator for each target. Types are General , Motor , Position , Velocity , and Adhesion ; the default is Position . Define actuator(s) ¶ Operator ID: forge.define_actuator_type All selected objects must be Actuator . Only the active object changes by default; enable Apply to all selected to change the full selection. 5.3 Site ¶ Create site(s) ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_site All selected objects must be Link . Forge creates one Site per Link. The type can be Box , Capsule , Cylinder , or Sphere , with Size , Radius , and Height as applicable. Define site(s) ¶ Operator ID: forge.define_site_type All selected objects must be Site . Change the type to Box , Capsule , Cylinder , or Sphere . Only the active Site changes by default; Apply to all selected enables batch editing. 5.4 Create Tendon ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_tendon Select at least two Joint objects, all of which must be Slide or Hinge . Forge creates one Fixed Tendon from the Joints in selection order. 5.5 Create Equality ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_equality Select exactly two objects of the same category: two Link or two Site objects: choose Connect or Weld ; two Joint objects: only Joint Equality is available. The first selected object is Target 1 and is also the parent of the new Equality object. The second is Target 2 . 5.6 Create Sensor(s) ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_sensor Sensor Type changes dynamically according to the selection: Link: Body Sensor (the Frame family, Contact , Subtreecom/Subtreelinvel/Subtreeangmom ). Use Xbody restricts the choices to the Frame family; Use Subtree restricts them to Contact . Joint: only sensors supported by Joint . A Joint cannot be the Target/Reference of a Frame Sensor . Site , Visual/Collider , and Camera: sensors supported by the corresponding target type. With exactly two compatible objects, Use Reference can be enabled. The first is Target and the second is Reference . Notes: Use Xbody and Use Subtree are mutually exclusive. Switching Reference/Xbody/Subtree resets Sensor Type . A None entry in the dropdown means that the current combination has no valid Sensor . 5.7 Create Contact ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_contact Select at least two Link objects to create an Exclude . Select at least two Visual/Collider/Plane/Height Field objects to create a Pair . With more than two objects selected, create a Contact for every pairwise combination. The first target of each Contact is also its parent. 5.8 Light ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_light Available with no selection or when all selected objects are Link . With no selection, types are Directional , Spot , and Point (default: Directional ). With selected Links, only Spot and Point are available (default: Spot ). With one or two Links all five modes are available (default: Targetbody ); with no selection or at least three Links, only Fixed , Track , and Trackcom are available (default: Fixed ). With no selection, create a World Light at the 3D Cursor . In ordinary tracking modes, create a child Light for every selected Link. With one Link and Targetbody/Targetbodycom , create one World Light at the 3D Cursor targeting that Link. With two Links and Targetbody/Targetbodycom , the first is the Light's position/parent and the second is its target; create one Light . 5.9 Camera ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_camera Available with no selection or when all selected objects are Link . Types are Perspective and Orthographic . With one or two Links all five modes are available (default: Targetbody ); with no selection or at least three Links, only Fixed , Track , and Trackcom are available (default: Fixed ). With no selection, create a World Camera at the 3D Cursor . In ordinary tracking modes, create a child Camera for every selected Link. With one Link and Targetbody/Targetbodycom , create a World Camera at the 3D Cursor targeting that Link; other modes create a child Camera for it. With two Links and Targetbody/Targetbodycom , the first is the Camera's position/parent and the second is its target; create one Camera .

docs.text: Chapter 6: Model Define — Meta Elements ¶ The Meta Elements panel is in the Forge tab and creates organizational and reference elements for a model. 6.1 Create frame(s) ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_frame Available with no selection or when all selected objects are Link , Frame , or Replicate . There is no dialog: Normal click: create a child Frame for each selected object; with no selection, create a World Frame . Shift + click : create a Frame and make the originally selected objects children of that Frame. 6.2 Create replicate ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_replicate All selected objects must be Camera , Light , Visual , Collider , Site , Link , Frame , Attach , or Replicate . Parameters: Count: number of copies. Separator: separator used when generating copy names. Offset: translation increment between adjacent copies. Euler: rotation increment between adjacent copies. After creation, Replicate values can be edited; see the Replicate section in Chapter 7. 6.3 Attach and Include ¶ The Meta Elements group also provides Attach and Include . They are not part of the main Creation, Definition, or Properties operator categories, but reference another scene, model, or MJCF file. During execution, the panel shows an overall progress bar and a sub-progress bar. File selection and prefixes must match the relevant MJCF tag parameters. Attach ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_attach Available with no selection or with exactly one Link , Frame , or Replicate selected; that object becomes the Attach parent. Dialog fields: File: an existing external MJCF XML file; Model: external model name; required; Prefix: prefix for imported object names; required; Link: optional external Body/Link. None means no Body is specified. After confirmation, Forge imports the external model as a modal task and then creates the Attach reference. Do not start another Import, Export, Attach, or Include operation while it is running. The first progress bar represents the overall stage; the second represents the number of elements in the current stage. Include ¶ Operator ID: forge.create_include Include requires no selected objects. Forge imports the collections from the external file for use in the scene, but export writes only an <include file="..."> reference; the external file contents are not merged into the current XML. Include also runs as a modal task and shows overall and sub-progress in the Meta Elements panel. Attach Include Progress:

docs.text: Chapter 7: Properties editing ¶ 7.1 Three property entry points ¶ Model Define → Global ¶ This entry edits scene-level Global Properties and Visual Properties; see Chapter 2. All objects must be deselected first. 3D View property gizmo ¶ In Object Mode , select a Forge object and click the colored Gizmo shown next to the object to open its Properties dialog. Blue Gizmo After clicking the Gizmo Object Properties → Forge Properties ¶ This panel displays the active object's: Local/World Location and Rotation ; Dimensions ; Parent ; Forge Model Type ; and model-property data for the current type. To open the panel: Open the Properties editor . Switch to the Object Properties tab . Expand Forge Properties to show properties for the current Model Type. 7.2 The property gizmo is not visible ¶ Check the following in order: The current area is a 3D View and Blender is in Object Mode . Gizmos are enabled in the 3D View . The active object's Blender type and Forge type are correct. A shape object still has the Geometry Nodes Modifier that Forge added during creation. 7.3 Object property dialogs ¶ All dialogs below are UI-only Operators intended for interaction through the Blender interface. Height Field ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_hfield Main editable values Nrow/Ncol, Elevation, X/Y Radius, Elevation Z, Base Z, Offset, Use Height Map, Height Map, contact/solver properties Dialog: Hfield Properties Model Properties Plane ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_plane Main editable values X/Y Half Size, Infinite, contact/solver properties Plane Properties Model Properties Visual / Collider ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_shape Main editable values Basic shape dimensions; Group, Condim, Contype, Conaffinity, Priority, Friction, Mass, Density, Margin, Gap, Solver Box: edit X/Y/Z Size . Sphere: edit Radius . Capsule/Cylinder: edit Radius and Height . Mesh: there is no Primitive Size input; edit the Mesh itself or the object dimensions. Materials are not edited in this dialog. Use Create Material , or assign a material directly in the Blender object material slots. The Model Properties area stores collision, mass, and Solver parameters for the MJCF Geometry . Visual Properties Collider Properties Link ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_link Main editable values Empty Display Type, Display Size, Mocap, Gravcomp Site ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_shape_site Main editable values Box/Sphere/Capsule/Cylinder dimensions and Group Inertial ¶ Select an Inertial to view mass , diaginertia , and fullinertia under Object Properties → Forge Properties → Inertial Info . This panel is read-only and there is no separate inertia properties dialog. To change values, use the object's Forge_Inertial through Python: import bpy inertial = bpy . context . active_object . Forge_Inertial inertial . mass = 2.0 inertial . fullinertia = ( 0.2 , 0.3 , 0.4 , 0.0 , 0.0 , 0.0 ) diaginertia contains the three diagonal components in the principal inertia frame. The object's rotation relative to its parent Link defines the principal axes; its position is the center of mass. fullinertia is the symmetric tensor about the center of mass, expressed in Link axes , ordered Ixx, Iyy, Izz, Ixy, Ixz, Iyz . It is derived from the current rotation and diagonal inertia. A nonzero fullinertia assignment must be positive definite. Forge decomposes it and updates the principal rotation and diaginertia . Scripts should assign all six components together to avoid incomplete intermediate tensors. Changing mass or inertia updates the equivalent box. Preview requires finite positive mass, finite positive diagonal moments, and the inertia triangle inequalities; otherwise it is not drawn. Joint ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_joint Main editable values Type, Display Size, Springdamper, Solver, Range, Force Range, Stiffness, Ref, Armature, Damping, Frictionloss Actuator ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_actuator Main editable values Type, Target, control/force ranges, Gain/Bias types, type-specific parameters, Gear/Dynamics/Gain/Bias arrays Tendon ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_tendon Tendon uses + and - to add or remove Target list entries. The Operators are forge.add_tendon_target_item and forge.remove_tendon_target_item . They are UI helper entry points; scripts and MCP should maintain the Tendon Target collection directly. Main editable values Type, add/remove Target entries, Range, Solver, Spring Length, Stiffness, Damping Equality ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_equality When Active is disabled, the main Equality parameters cannot be edited. Main editable values Active, Type, Target 1/2, type-specific parameters Contact ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_contact Only Pair contacts display collision and Solver parameters. Main editable values Type, Target 1/2; for Pair: Condim, Friction, Solver, Margin, Gap Exclude Properties Pair Properties Sensor ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_sensor Frame Sensor can set Reference . Contact Sensor shows a Link , Geom , Subtree , or Site name according to Target Type . Main editable values Sensor/Target Type, Target, Reference, Xbody/Subtree, Noise, Cutoff; Contact Sensor Data/Reduce Light ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_light Target is shown only for Targetbody/Targetbodycom modes. Main editable values Type, Mode, Target, Shadow, Color, Energy, Size/Distance/Angle/Spot parameters Camera ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_camera Target is shown only for Targetbody/Targetbodycom modes. Main editable values Type, Mode, Target, FOV or Ortho Scale, Clip Start/End Replicate ¶ Operator ID: forge.properties_replicate Main editable values Count, Offset, Euler, Separator Dynamic fields: Global / Visual: detailed Headlight and SSGI parameters are controlled by their Active switches; disabling them disables the corresponding fields. Height Field: Height Map appears only after Use Height Map is enabled. Plane: Infinite is independent and does not hide Half Size . Visual / Collider: the geometry type determines dimension fields; Box shows three-axis Size , Sphere shows Radius , Capsule/Cylinder show Radius + Height , and Mesh shows no primitive size. Materials are managed through the object's first Material Slot . Site: the geometry type determines whether Size , Radius , or Radius + Height is shown. Link: Display Type / Display Size / Mocap / Gravcomp are always shown; no fields are hidden by type. Joint: Free shows only basic Stiffness / Armature / Damping / Frictionloss . Other types also show Springdamper , Solver, Range, Limited, and related fields. Ball does not show Actuator Force Range/Limited . Actuator: Position shows Kp / Kv / Inheritrange , Velocity shows Kv , and Adhesion shows Gain ; other types show Gear / Dynamics / Gain / Bias arrays. Tendon: the Target field comes from a variable-length Target list controlled by + / - . Equality: disabling Active disables all remaining fields. Target 2 appears only after Target 1 is set; the remaining parameters depend on Equality type. Contact: only Pair shows Condim, Friction, Solver, Margin, Gap ; Exclude does not show them. Sensor: a Contact Sensor labels target fields as Link1/2, Geom1/2, Subtree1/2 , or Site according to Target Type . Frame sensors show Reference and Use Xbody after Target is set; Contact sensors show Reference and Use Subtree when a second target is required. Light: only Targetbody/Targetbodycom shows Target ; Spot/Point show Shadow Soft Size / Cutoff Distance , other types show Angle , and Spot additionally shows Spot Size / Spot Blend . Camera: only Targetbody/Targetbodycom shows Target ; Perspective shows FOV/Angle , while Orthographic shows Ortho Scale . Replicate: Count / Offset / Euler appear only while the object still has a Replicate Modifier; Separator always belongs to Replicate properties. 7.4 How changes take effect ¶ Property dialogs modify Object , Modifier , or Scene data directly and do not have an Apply/Save button. Changes remain after closing the dialog and can be undone with Blender Undo . Prefer changing Size , Radius , and Height in Properties . Several Forge objects lock Object Scale ; shape dimensions are driven by the Geometry Nodes Modifier parameters.

docs.text: Operator ID: forge.properties_replicate Main editable values Count, Offset, Euler, Separator Dynamic fields: Global / Visual: detailed Headlight and SSGI parameters are controlled by their Active switches; disabling them disables the corresponding fields. Height Field: Height Map appears only after Use Height Map is enabled. Plane: Infinite is independent and does not hide Half Size . Visual / Collider: the geometry type determines dimension fields; Box shows three-axis Size , Sphere shows Radius , Capsule/Cylinder show Radius + Height , and Mesh shows no primitive size. Materials are managed through the object's first Material Slot . Site: the geometry type determines whether Size , Radius , or Radius + Height is shown. Link: Display Type / Display Size / Mocap / Gravcomp are always shown; no fields are hidden by type. Joint: Free shows only basic Stiffness / Armature / Damping / Frictionloss . Other types also show Springdamper , Solver, Range, Limited, and related fields. Ball does not show Actuator Force Range/Limited . Actuator: Position shows Kp / Kv / Inheritrange , Velocity shows Kv , and Adhesion shows Gain ; other types show Gear / Dynamics / Gain / Bias arrays. Tendon: the Target field comes from a variable-length Target list controlled by + / - . Equality: disabling Active disables all remaining fields. Target 2 appears only after Target 1 is set; the remaining parameters depend on Equality type. Contact: only Pair shows Condim, Friction, Solver, Margin, Gap ; Exclude does not show them. Sensor: a Contact Sensor labels target fields as Link1/2, Geom1/2, Subtree1/2 , or Site according to Target Type . Frame sensors show Reference and Use Xbody after Target is set; Contact sensors show Reference and Use Subtree when a second target is required. Light: only Targetbody/Targetbodycom shows Target ; Spot/Point show Shadow Soft Size / Cutoff Distance , other types show Angle , and Spot additionally shows Spot Size / Spot Blend . docs.text: Chapter 8: Import and Export ¶ 8.1 Import ¶ GLB import and export require Blender's glTF 2.0 add-on ( io_scene_gltf2 ). If disabled, Forge prompts you to enable it in Edit > Preferences > Add-ons , before clearing the import scene or writing export files and modifying meshes. OBJ/STL import, OBJ export and XML-only updates do not require this add-on. The Import panel rebuilds a Blender scene from an MJCF XML file. Mesh assets can reference OBJ , STL , or GLB files. A GLB asset must contain exactly one Mesh object; other elements such as cameras, lights and empty nodes are discarded. The Mesh node's transform is baked, preserving file-space coordinates and UVs for Forge export/import roundtrips. MJCF mesh scale is applied afterwards; materials come from the MJCF definitions, rather than embedded GLB materials. Missing files, unsupported formats, and GLB files with zero or multiple Mesh objects report an asset-loading error. Operator ID: forge.import_mjcf Procedure: Select an MJCF XML file in File . Enable Import material if needed. Click Import . Import is a modal operation and displays overall progress plus sub-progress for the current stage. Save your current work before importing: Import cleans the current scene objects and collections, non-main scenes, and orphaned data before rebuilding the model. If Forge Library does not exist or its path is invalid, Forge attempts to configure it again from the add-on's lib/assets directory. The operation is cancelled if recovery fails. 8.2 Export ¶ The Export panel writes the current Forge scene as an MJCF XML file. Operator ID: forge.export_mjcf Parameters: Only Update File: update only the MJCF contents and skip rewriting external asset files; Path: export destination. If .xml is omitted, the file selector adds it automatically. When calling forge_export_mjcf through MCP, an existing target file is refused by default. Pass overwrite=True explicitly to confirm replacement. The UI operator forge.export_mjcf writes to the path selected by the current file browser. Export proceeds through these stages: collect assets; write images, Height Field , and Visual/Collider meshes; write each MJCF section; and write the file. Overall and sub-progress are displayed. Empty exported mesh assets are ignored. Export collects model objects from the World , Link , Frame , Visual , and Collider collections, plus Replicate and its child collections: parentless objects in those collections are treated as roots, and their children are collected by walking the hierarchy. A root Link is therefore exported even when it lives in the Link or Frame collection. When World uses an Environment Texture node connected to an environment image, Export writes it as an MJCF <texture type="envhdr"> . Import restores the texture to the main scene's World . Checker materials export as native MJCF 2D builtin checker textures, without external image files. Import restores their colors, repeat values, and Blender shader nodes when Import material is enabled. See Create a checker material for creation parameters and the supported node layout. Instance reuse markers and export rules are described in Section 4.7 : an Instance Link only supplies assets; its children are written under each placeholder Link during export. The export path may be absolute or relative to the current .blend file. Make sure the destination directory exists and is writable before exporting. 8.3 Scripts and MCP ¶ Import , Export , Attach , and Include are all modal Operators . They initially return RUNNING_MODAL ; scripts and MCP clients must wait for the corresponding state to finish: Import: Forge_Props.is_importing ; Export: Forge_Props.is_exporting ; Attach: Forge_Props.is_attaching ; Include: Forge_Props.is_including . Through MCP , prefer forge_import_mjcf , forge_export_mjcf , forge_create_attach , and forge_create_include . These tools set paths, wait for the modal operation to finish, and return the result. 8.4 Inertial import and export ¶ When importing <inertial fullinertia="..."> , Forge decomposes the tensor expressed in Link axes into a principal frame and diagonal inertia. When nonzero diagonal inertia is available, export writes pos , mass , quat , and diaginertia , without also writing fullinertia . An imported fullinertia can therefore export as an equivalent quat + diaginertia representation. Inertial poses use physical transforms relative to the Link; viewport box scaling does not affect export. Imported Mesh Colliders use wireframe display and can show translucent surfaces through Collider Preview .

docs.text: Chapter 9: CoACD convex decomposition ¶ 9.1 Function and prerequisites ¶ CoACD decomposes a mesh into several approximately convex collision meshes, which is useful for generating Collider shapes from a complex Visual . Operator ID: forge.coacds Available in Object Mode when at least one Visual is selected. The operator selection check requires every selected object to be a Visual , and each Visual must contain Mesh data. When calling the MCP tool by name, pass one Visual object. 9.2 Before running ¶ The coacd package must be installed in the Blender Python environment. It can be installed from the Dependencies page in the Forge add-on preferences. Processing can take several minutes, depending on mesh complexity and sampling/MCTS parameters. Logs appear in the system console, not Blender's Python Console editor. On Windows, use Window → Toggle System Console . The current CoACD dialog also calls bpy.ops.wm.console_toggle() , so opening the dialog hides an already visible console; toggle it again if needed. On macOS / Linux, start Blender from a terminal and read logs there. See Blender's command-line launch guide . The operation decomposes evaluated triangle faces. It creates new convex-hull objects, so save the file or create a backup first. Each output hull is a new Mesh object in the source object's first Collection and is initialized as a Forge Collider ( Forge_Model_Type=COLLIDER , Geometry type MESH ). 9.3 Main parameters ¶ Threshold: concavity threshold; a smaller value usually produces a finer decomposition; Max Convex Hull: maximum number of hulls when merging is enabled; Preprocess Mode / Resolution: manifold preprocessing method and resolution; Sample Resolution: Hausdorff-distance sampling resolution; MCTS nodes / Iteration / Max Depth: search size; PCA , Merge , Decimate , Max Convex Hull vertex ; Extrude , Extrude Margin ; Seed: random-sampling seed. After completion, use Select Hulls to select hull objects generated from coacd_name_template . The hulls are already Forge Collider objects and do not need to be defined again; continue by adjusting hierarchy or properties.
docs.title: Chapter 9: CoACD convex decomposition

docs.text: Chapter 10: Troubleshooting and scripting ¶ 10.1 Why did Definition change only one object? ¶ Definition for Geometry , Collider , Site , Joint , and Actuator changes only the active object by default. To batch-edit, enable Apply to all selected in the dialog. 10.2 Target or Reference order is reversed ¶ Deselect everything, then select again in the correct order: Equality: the first is Target 1/parent; the second is Target 2. Sensor Reference: the first is Target; the second is Reference. Targetbody Light: with one Link, that Link is the target; with two Links, the first is the Light position/parent and the second is the tracking target. Targetbody Camera: with one Link, that Link is the target; with two Links, the first is the Camera position/parent and the second is the tracking target. Tendon: Joints are added to the target list in selection order. Link Parent: the exception; the active object is always the parent and must be activated last. 10.3 Compute Inertial finds no geometry or fails ¶ Ensure Inertial Model Type matches the intended Visual / Collider source and that geometry is a direct child of the selected Link , or inside its Frame descendants. Child Links are not searched. Mesh calculation requires TetGen ; enable Check Geometry for validation and repair failures reported for the mesh. Box, Sphere, Cylinder, and Capsule use shape parameters directly and do not require TetGen. See 4.5 . 10.4 The original object is no longer selected after creation ¶ Most Creation Operators clear the original selection and select the newly created objects. This is expected. To continue creating child elements on the original Link , select the Link again. 10.5 Shape Size and Object Scale ¶ Prefer editing Size , Radius , and Height in Shape Properties . Primitive shapes are normally controlled by Geometry Nodes Modifier parameters and lock Object Scale . After changing to Mesh , the geometry is baked into the mesh and Object Scale may become editable again. 10.6 Operator ID quick reference ¶ Creation ¶ Function Operator ID Geometry / Collider / Site forge.create_geometry / forge.create_collider / forge.create_site Height Field / Plane forge.create_height_field / forge.create_plane Link / Joint / Inertial forge.create_link / forge.create_joint / forge.create_inertial Actuator / Tendon / Equality forge.create_actuator / forge.create_tendon / forge.create_equality Sensor / Contact forge.create_sensor / forge.create_contact Light / Camera forge.create_light / forge.create_camera Frame / Replicate forge.create_frame / forge.create_replicate Material forge.create_material Definition ¶ Function Operator ID Model forge.define_model_type Geometry / Collider / Site forge.define_geometry_type / forge.define_collider_type / forge.define_site_type Joint / Actuator forge.define_joint_type / forge.define_actuator_type Parent / Root forge.define_parent / forge.mark_root_link Instance Link forge.mark_instance_link Mesh / Gizmo forge.mesh_check / forge.scale_gizmo_size Utility, IO, and CoACD ¶ Function Operator ID Batch Rename / Tag Select forge.batch_rename / forge.select_by_tag Model Type Select forge.select_by_model_type Select Hulls / Instance ID forge.select_hulls / forge.set_instance_idname Instance Link marker forge.mark_instance_link (see 4.7 ) Import / Export forge.import_mjcf / forge.export_mjcf Attach / Include forge.create_attach / forge.create_include CoACD forge.coacds Properties ¶ Properties operators use the common forge.properties_* naming scheme, including global , visual , hfield , plane , shape , shape_site , link , joint , actuator , tendon , equality , contact , sensor , light , camera , and replicate . 10.7 Blender Python example ¶ import bpy # Ensure Object Mode and deselect every object first. if bpy . context . mode != "OBJECT" : raise RuntimeError ( "Forge operators require Object Mode" ) bpy . ops . object . select_all ( action = "DESELECT" ) bpy . ops . forge . create_geometry ( geometry_type = "BOX" , size_box = ( 1.0 , 2.0 , 0.5 ), ) Operator calls are constrained by the current Blender Context and poll conditions. Before batch operations, set explicitly: Object Mode ; the selected objects; the active object; and the Forge selection order when two targets are required.

docs.text: Forge MCP Setup and Connection ¶ 中文 | English This page covers the path from preparing a workspace to a working client connection. Full environment-variable definitions, server operation, Skills and document discovery, and development are maintained in the server reference . The agent-side stdio MCP server lives in mcp-server/ . Client configuration is provided in .mcp.json (Claude Code and similar clients) and .codex/config.toml (Codex). You can clone or copy the following four items into an empty workspace and start the agent from there: .claude/ .codex/ .mcp.json mcp-server/ A minimal MCP workspace needs only the items above; no Blender test project is required. Scene queries and edits require Blender with addon/Forge installed and enabled and the add-on's MCP Bridge running (default localhost:9876 ). Reading Skills and searching local documentation do not require Blender to be running. Check Blender before connecting ¶ Complete the Forge add-on installation , enable Forge in the Blender instance that owns the scene, and allow Blender online access. Click Start MCP Bridge in the Forge sidebar and confirm it is running. Listener, token, startup, and polling controls are documented in Config Forge . 1. Prepare a workspace ¶ Clone the repository to obtain the complete layout: git clone <repository-url> forge-mcp-workspace cd forge-mcp-workspace If you copy an existing checkout, include the hidden directories and .mcp.json listed above; do not copy only mcp-server/ . Check that the configuration items beginning with . are included in the copy. 2. Install MCP dependencies ¶ Install uv first. In a full checkout containing the root pyproject.toml , run uv sync from the repository root to prepare the root .venv used by the client. See the development environment instructions for details. For a minimal MCP workspace containing only the items listed above, run the installer below from that workspace. It creates a Python 3.11 environment in mcp-server/.venv and installs mcp and forge-mcp without modifying the system Python. Windows PowerShell: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 macOS / Linux / WSL: bash mcp-server/install.sh The installer can launch a client after installation: .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 -Launch claude .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 -Launch codex bash mcp-server/install.sh claude bash mcp-server/install.sh codex These installers prepare a workspace for using the server. To modify source and run tests, use the development environment in the server reference . 3. Start an agent in the workspace ¶ Open a new terminal and change to the workspace: cd C :\ path \ to \ forge-mcp-workspace claude # Claude Code cd C :\ path \ to \ forge-mcp-workspace $env:CODEX_HOME = ( Join-Path ( Get-Location ) '.codex' ) codex # Codex CLI On macOS / Linux, use export CODEX_HOME="$PWD/.codex" . With CODEX_HOME set, Codex reads the copied .codex/config.toml ; Claude Code reads .mcp.json from the workspace root. The client automatically starts the MCP server over stdio using its configuration. A minimal MCP workspace uses the installer's mcp-server/.venv ; the full repository's uv workspace uses the root .venv , which must first be prepared using the development environment instructions . The --no-sync option only skips dependency synchronization; it does not create or repair the environment. 4. Verify the connection ¶ Codex: run codex mcp list , or enter /mcp in the TUI; Claude Code: run claude mcp list , or enter /mcp and confirm that forge is connected; The default port is 9876 . For a non-default or remote endpoint, set FORGE_MCP_HOST and FORGE_MCP_PORT consistently in the env sections of .mcp.json and .codex/config.toml . Cross-machine connections must also use the same non-empty FORGE_MCP_TOKEN on both sides; restrict the bridge port with a firewall or VPN. Connection troubleshooting ¶ Symptom Check first No forge entry in the client Workspace location, client configuration, and whether the client was restarted Server process fails to start Installer results, availability of uv , and tool filters or directory overrides in runtime configuration MCP connects, but scene operations fail or time out Blender is running, Forge is enabled, the Bridge is started, and host, port, and token match Bridge fails to start Blender online access and port availability; see Config Forge Once connected, use the server reference for runtime configuration and MCP Skills for authoring rules. Configuration files ¶ .mcp.json : MCP configuration read by Claude Code, Cursor, and similar clients; .claude/settings.local.json : enables the project's forge MCP entry; .codex/config.toml : project-level MCP configuration for Codex; the project must be trusted by Codex; OpenAI's documentation explains that Codex CLI, IDE extensions, and the desktop app share MCP configuration. Project-level configuration is stored in .codex/config.toml for trusted projects; use codex mcp list or the TUI /mcp command to inspect the connection: https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/ . 中文 | English
docs.title: Forge MCP Setup and Connection

You can clone or copy the following four items into an empty workspace and start the agent from there: .claude/ .codex/ .mcp.json mcp-server/ A minimal MCP workspace needs only the items above; no Blender test project is required. Scene queries and edits require Blender with addon/Forge installed and enabled and the add-on's MCP Bridge running (default localhost:9876 ). Reading Skills and searching local documentation do not require Blender to be running.
docs.title: Forge MCP Setup and Connection

docs.text: Complete the Forge add-on installation , enable Forge in the Blender instance that owns the scene, and allow Blender online access. Click Start MCP Bridge in the Forge sidebar and confirm it is running. Listener, token, startup, and polling controls are documented in Config Forge .
docs.title: Check Blender before connecting

docs.text: Clone the repository to obtain the complete layout: git clone <repository-url> forge-mcp-workspace cd forge-mcp-workspace If you copy an existing checkout, include the hidden directories and .mcp.json listed above; do not copy only mcp-server/ . Check that the configuration items beginning with . are included in the copy.
docs.title: 1. Prepare a workspace

docs.text: Install uv first. In a full checkout containing the root pyproject.toml , run uv sync from the repository root to prepare the root .venv used by the client. See the development environment instructions for details. For a minimal MCP workspace containing only the items listed above, run the installer below from that workspace. It creates a Python 3.11 environment in mcp-server/.venv and installs mcp and forge-mcp without modifying the system Python. Windows PowerShell: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 macOS / Linux / WSL: bash mcp-server/install.sh The installer can launch a client after installation: .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 -Launch claude .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 -Launch codex bash mcp-server/install.sh claude bash mcp-server/install.sh codex These installers prepare a workspace for using the server. To modify source and run tests, use the development environment in the server reference .
docs.title: 2. Install MCP dependencies

docs.text: Open a new terminal and change to the workspace: cd C :\ path \ to \ forge-mcp-workspace claude # Claude Code cd C :\ path \ to \ forge-mcp-workspace $env:CODEX_HOME = ( Join-Path ( Get-Location ) '.codex' ) codex # Codex CLI On macOS / Linux, use export CODEX_HOME="$PWD/.codex" . With CODEX_HOME set, Codex reads the copied .codex/config.toml ; Claude Code reads .mcp.json from the workspace root. The client automatically starts the MCP server over stdio using its configuration. A minimal MCP workspace uses the installer's mcp-server/.venv ; the full repository's uv workspace uses the root .venv , which must first be prepared using the development environment instructions . The --no-sync option only skips dependency synchronization; it does not create or repair the environment.
docs.title: 3. Start an agent in the workspace

docs.text: Codex: run codex mcp list , or enter /mcp in the TUI; Claude Code: run claude mcp list , or enter /mcp and confirm that forge is connected; The default port is 9876 . For a non-default or remote endpoint, set FORGE_MCP_HOST and FORGE_MCP_PORT consistently in the env sections of .mcp.json and .codex/config.toml . Cross-machine connections must also use the same non-empty FORGE_MCP_TOKEN on both sides; restrict the bridge port with a firewall or VPN.
docs.title: 4. Verify the connection

docs.text: Symptom Check first No forge entry in the client Workspace location, client configuration, and whether the client was restarted Server process fails to start Installer results, availability of uv , and tool filters or directory overrides in runtime configuration MCP connects, but scene operations fail or time out Blender is running, Forge is enabled, the Bridge is started, and host, port, and token match Bridge fails to start Blender online access and port availability; see Config Forge Once connected, use the server reference for runtime configuration and MCP Skills for authoring rules.
docs.title: Connection troubleshooting

docs.text: .mcp.json : MCP configuration read by Claude Code, Cursor, and similar clients; .claude/settings.local.json : enables the project's forge MCP entry; .codex/config.toml : project-level MCP configuration for Codex; the project must be trusted by Codex; OpenAI's documentation explains that Codex CLI, IDE extensions, and the desktop app share MCP configuration. Project-level configuration is stored in .codex/config.toml for trusted projects; use codex mcp list or the TUI /mcp command to inspect the connection: https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/ . 中文 | English

docs.text: Forge MCP 安装与连接 ¶ 中文 | English 本页负责从准备工作区到首次连接成功的流程。环境变量的完整定义、服务运行方式、Skills 与文档加载机制以及开发说明统一放在 服务端参考 。 本项目把 Agent 侧的 stdio MCP 服务放在 mcp-server/ ，把客户端配置放在 .mcp.json （Claude Code 等客户端）和 .codex/config.toml （Codex）。因此可以把下面四项复制或 clone 到一个空工作目录，再从该目录启动 Agent： .claude/ .codex/ .mcp.json mcp-server/ 精简 MCP 工作区只需上述项目，不需要复制 Blender 测试工程。运行场景查询或编辑工具时，Blender 中必须安装并启用 addon/Forge ，并启动插件的 MCP Bridge（默认 localhost:9876 ）；读取 Skills 和搜索本地文档不需要运行 Blender。 连接前检查 Blender ¶ 先完成 Forge 插件安装 ，在拥有场景的 Blender 实例中启用 Forge，并允许 Blender 在线访问。在 Forge 侧栏点击 Start MCP Bridge ，确认 Bridge 已启动。监听地址、Token、自动启动与轮询设置见 配置 Forge ，本页不重复插件参数说明。 1. 准备工作目录 ¶ 推荐 clone（会自动得到完整目录结构）： git clone <仓库地址> forge-mcp-workspace cd forge-mcp-workspace 如果是从已有目录复制，请确保复制了上面列出的隐藏目录和 .mcp.json ，不要只复制 mcp-server/ 。复制时请检查这些以 . 开头的配置项是否完整。 2. 安装 MCP 依赖 ¶ 先安装 uv 。若使用包含根目录 pyproject.toml 的完整仓库，在仓库根目录执行 uv sync ，准备客户端实际使用的根目录 .venv ；详细说明见 开发环境 。 若使用仅复制上述项目的精简 MCP 工作区，在工作目录执行下面的安装脚本。脚本会在 mcp-server/.venv 创建 Python 3.11 环境，并安装 mcp 与 forge-mcp ，不会改动系统 Python。 Windows PowerShell： Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 macOS / Linux / WSL： bash mcp-server/install.sh 也可以让脚本安装后直接启动客户端： .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 -Launch claude .\ mcp-server \ install . ps1 -Launch codex bash mcp-server/install.sh claude bash mcp-server/install.sh codex 以上脚本面向使用服务的工作区。需要修改源码并运行测试时，改用 服务端参考中的开发环境 。 3. 在该目录启动 Agent ¶ 安装完成后，打开新的控制台并进入工作目录： cd C :\ path \ to \ forge-mcp-workspace claude # Claude Code cd C :\ path \ to \ forge-mcp-workspace $env:CODEX_HOME = ( Join-Path ( Get-Location ) '.codex' ) codex # Codex CLI macOS / Linux 使用 export CODEX_HOME="$PWD/.codex" 。设置 CODEX_HOME 后，Codex 会读取复制来的 .codex/config.toml ；Claude Code 会读取工作目录根部的 .mcp.json 。客户端会按配置自动通过 stdio 启动 MCP 服务。精简 MCP 工作区使用安装脚本创建的 mcp-server/.venv ；完整仓库中的 uv workspace 使用根目录 .venv ，需先按 开发环境说明 准备依赖。配置中的 --no-sync 只跳过依赖同步，不会自动创建或修复环境。 4. 验证连接 ¶ Codex：运行 codex mcp list ，或在 TUI 输入 /mcp ； Claude Code：运行 claude mcp list ，或输入 /mcp 查看 forge 是否为 connected； 默认端口为 9876 。远程或非默认端口时，在 .mcp.json 与 .codex/config.toml 的 env 中同步设置 FORGE_MCP_HOST 、 FORGE_MCP_PORT ；跨机器连接还必须设置两端相同的非空 FORGE_MCP_TOKEN ，并用防火墙或 VPN 限制 Bridge 端口。 连接问题排查 ¶ 现象 先检查 客户端没有 forge 条目 工作目录、客户端配置文件及客户端是否已重新启动 服务进程启动失败 安装脚本是否成功、 uv 是否可用，以及 运行时配置 中的过滤条件和目录设置 MCP 已连接，但场景操作失败或超时 Blender 是否运行、Forge 是否启用、Bridge 是否启动，以及主机、端口、Token 是否匹配 Bridge 无法启动 Blender 在线访问许可、端口是否占用；详细设置见 配置 Forge 连接成功后，查阅 服务端参考 了解运行时配置；模型创作规则见 英文 MCP Skills 。 配置文件说明 ¶ .mcp.json ：Claude Code、Cursor 等读取的 MCP 配置； .claude/settings.local.json ：启用项目中的 forge MCP 条目； .codex/config.toml ：Codex 的项目级 MCP 配置；项目必须被 Codex 信任； OpenAI 官方文档说明，Codex CLI、IDE 扩展和桌面端共享 MCP 配置；项目级配置位于受信任项目的 .codex/config.toml ，可用 codex mcp list 和 TUI 的 /mcp 检查连接： https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/ 。 English | 中文

docs.text: Forge MCP Server Reference ¶ 中文说明 This page covers the agent-side MCP Server architecture, environment variables, Skills and document discovery, tool categories, and development. Initial installation, client configuration, startup, and connection troubleshooting live in MCP setup and connection . Runtime architecture ¶ AI agent ──stdio──> Forge MCP Server ──TCP──> Blender Forge MCP Bridge The MCP Server runs beside the agent; the Bridge runs in the Blender process that owns the scene. Scene queries and modeling operations go through the Bridge. Skill reads and documentation searches use files local to the server and do not require Blender to be running. For Blender-side preferences and dependencies, see Config Forge . Client startup and process management ¶ After preparing the environment as described in setup and connection , use this workflow: Enable Forge in Blender and start the MCP Bridge . Start Claude Code or Codex from the workspace directory containing the client configuration. The client reads the workspace configuration, starts and manages Forge MCP Server automatically, and communicates with it over stdio. Check the MCP connection status in the client and confirm that forge is connected before running Forge operations. After changing environment variables, Skills, or document files, reconnect or restart the MCP server through the client. Restarting only the Blender Bridge does not reload server-side documentation. Runtime configuration ¶ Env var Default Description FORGE_MCP_HOST localhost Blender bridge host FORGE_MCP_PORT 9876 Blender bridge port FORGE_MCP_TOKEN (empty) Shared bridge token; required when Blender binds outside localhost FORGE_MCP_TIMEOUT 1800 Response timeout in seconds (matches the addon deferred timeout) FORGE_MCP_SKILL_GATE soft How the authoring-guide gate behaves: soft runs the operation and attaches a one-time skill_hint naming the guide, strict refuses until the guide is read, off never intervenes FORGE_SKILLS_DIR (search) Directory holding the skill .md guides served by forge_skill FORGE_DOCS_DIR (search) Directory holding the MJCF reference .md files searched by forge_search_docs FORGE_BLENDER_DOCS_DIR (search) Blender docs root containing api/ and manual/ RST files (searched recursively) FORGE_TOOLS (all) Serve only the listed tool categories / name substrings; readonly keeps just the read-only tools; an invalid non-empty filter fails startup Skills and document discovery ¶ At startup the server loads all *.md guides from the first populated Skills directory (search order: FORGE_SKILLS_DIR , the source-tree forge_mcp/skills/ , any legacy skills/ directory up the package path, then ./skills ). A one-line index of the loaded guides is injected as the server instructions, and each guide is served on demand by the forge_skill tool ( forge_skill(name="create") / forge_skill(name="modify") / forge_skill(name="operators") / forge_skill(name="custom_material") ), so agents discover the guides automatically but only pay the context cost when used. Pass section to fetch a single heading instead of the whole guide (e.g. forge_skill(name="create", section="joint") or forge_skill(name="operators", section="create_sensor") ). The forge_mcp/docs/mjcf/*.md element reference (same discovery scheme via FORGE_DOCS_DIR / forge_mcp/docs/mjcf on the package path) is loaded into a paragraph-level search index served by forge_search_docs . The same reference is also exposed as MCP resources ( mjcf://<element> per doc file, mjcf://index for the element hierarchy / path registry) so agents that prefer native resource reads can pull a whole document directly; forge_search_docs remains for keyword search. Read forge_skill(name="create") before authoring and forge_skill(name="modify") before editing. Enforcement is controlled by FORGE_MCP_SKILL_GATE : default soft allows the operation and attaches a one-time reading hint after a successful call; strict refuses operations until the required guide has been read. forge_execute uses the same policy for explicit bpy.ops.forge.* calls and Forge_* property writes; ordinary Blender modeling scripts are unaffected by this Forge gate. Tool filters retain forge_skill for operation access. Full authoring rules live in MCP Skills . forge_execute injects bpy and mathutils into the script namespace. Scripts must assign a JSON-serializable dictionary to result , for example result = {"scene": bpy.context.scene.name} . Blender RST documentation is loaded recursively from forge_mcp/docs/blender/ , including api/ and manual/ . Discovery checks FORGE_BLENDER_DOCS_DIR , forge_mcp/docs/blender/ , docs/blender/ along the package's ancestor paths, then ./docs/blender/ ; the first populated directory wins independently of MJCF. Missing Blender documentation is allowed. Restart the server after changing documentation files. forge_search_docs searches both references by default. Use source="mjcf" , "blender" , "blender_api" , or "blender_manual" to narrow results: forge_search_docs ( query = "bpy.ops.mesh.bevel" , source = "blender_api" ) forge_search_docs ( query = "bevel modifier" , source = "blender_manual" , max_results = 5 ) forge_search_docs ( query = "condim" , source = "mjcf" ) RST headings and API directives become section breadcrumbs, including fully qualified function/property names. Text, parameter fields and inline code are searchable; presentation metadata is omitted. This text parser does not build Sphinx, execute directives, or expand external includes. Results contain source , path (e.g. blender/api/bpy.ops.mesh.rst , relative to docs/ ), breadcrumb , text , score , and index ; existing MJCF paths stay unchanged. Results are sorted by score and context stays within the matching section. Documentation search requires no running Blender instance. Tools ¶ forge_mcp.tools registers tools by module: create.py — forge_create_* : link, inertial, joint, geometry, collider, height_field, plane, site, actuator, tendon, equality, contact, sensor, light, camera, frame, replicate, attach, include, material. modify.py — forge_define_* : model_type, geometry_type, collider_type, site_type, joint_type, actuator_type; plus define_parent, mark_root_link, mark_instance_link, mesh_check, scale_gizmo_size. utilities.py — scene_info, batch_rename, set_instance_idname, select_by_tag, select_hulls. scene.py — generic editing: object_info, measure, scene_config, set_transform, set_shape_size, set_property, set_scene_property, set_tendon_targets, rename, delete, execute. geometry.py — forge_coacd : decompose one Forge VISUAL mesh into new Collider hulls while preserving the source object. io.py — modal MJCF import/export plus explicit blend-file saving. capture.py — forge_screenshot : capture an area (default the 3D viewport) or the whole window as a PNG image, with imbuf downsampling to a size budget; layout=True returns the window layout as JSON instead. blendfile.py — forge_blendfile_summary : path/save status/backups, datablock counts, missing external files, linked libraries (direct vs indirect). docs.py — forge_search_docs : ranked full-text search over the bundled MJCF element reference and local Blender RST API/manual. skill.py — forge_skill : return the full text of an auto-loaded skills/*.md authoring guide, or a single section via section ( forge_skill(name="create", section="joint") ); unknown / ambiguous section names raise listing the available ones. Tools are annotated with MCP ToolAnnotations ( tools/_hints.py ): read-only hints on query tools, destructive hints on recursive delete, arbitrary execute, MJCF import, CoACD and blend-file saving. Every op tool ( create / modify / op wrappers in utilities ) accepts select: list[str] — object names that replace the Blender selection before the operator runs (order matters, first becomes active; null keeps the current selection). Results include created : names of new scene objects, so generated names never need guessing. Conventions worth knowing (learned building a Newton's cradle end-to-end): A joint's exported rotation axis is its local +Z in parent space — rotate the joint object so its Z points along the desired world axis. Shape sizes are local to the parent (a child link's local frame differs from world) — check with forge_measure (world bboxes) after editing. mesh_check ignores boundary-only point-point, point-edge, point-face, edge-edge, and edge-face contact when incident geometry does not cross the other mesh. A coplanar shared face is also valid when its plane separates both complete objects, independent of winding; non-separating coplanar overlap and actual crossings remain intersections. Valid contact needs no epsilon gap. Blender silently suffixes name collisions ( .001 ) — including with orphaned (out-of-scene) datablocks; forge_rename refuses instead. Forge_Model_Type is stored as an enum index ; tools resolve it to names ( LINK , JOINT , ...). Note: bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popup dialogs are UI-only and ineffective for agents — parameters are changed via direct property access ( obj.Forge_<Type>.<property> ) and shape / gizmo sizes via obj.modifiers[...] . Development and tests ¶ From the full repository root: uv sync uv run pytest tests/mcp/unit tests/mcp/integration uv sync installs forge-mcp in editable mode into the root .venv , alongside add-on test dependencies. uv sync --all-packages is also supported. End-to-end tests require Blender; see Development Forge . For server-package development in an independent source directory: cd mcp-server uv venv --python 3 .11 uv pip install --editable . Keep forge_mcp/skills/ and forge_mcp/docs/ with the source. Installer and client startup instructions are maintained only in setup and connection .
