docs.text: After preparing the environment as described in setup and connection , use this workflow: Enable Forge in Blender and start the MCP Bridge . Start Claude Code or Codex from the workspace directory containing the client configuration. The client reads the workspace configuration, starts and manages Forge MCP Server automatically, and communicates with it over stdio. Check the MCP connection status in the client and confirm that forge is connected before running Forge operations. After changing environment variables, Skills, or document files, reconnect or restart the MCP server through the client. Restarting only the Blender Bridge does not reload server-side documentation.
docs.title: Client startup and process management

docs.text: Env var Default Description FORGE_MCP_HOST localhost Blender bridge host FORGE_MCP_PORT 9876 Blender bridge port FORGE_MCP_TOKEN (empty) Shared bridge token; required when Blender binds outside localhost FORGE_MCP_TIMEOUT 1800 Response timeout in seconds (matches the addon deferred timeout) FORGE_MCP_SKILL_GATE soft How the authoring-guide gate behaves: soft runs the operation and attaches a one-time skill_hint naming the guide, strict refuses until the guide is read, off never intervenes FORGE_SKILLS_DIR (search) Directory holding the skill .md guides served by forge_skill FORGE_DOCS_DIR (search) Directory holding the MJCF reference .md files searched by forge_search_docs FORGE_BLENDER_DOCS_DIR (search) Blender docs root containing api/ and manual/ RST files (searched recursively) FORGE_TOOLS (all) Serve only the listed tool categories / name substrings; readonly keeps just the read-only tools; an invalid non-empty filter fails startup
docs.title: Runtime configuration

docs.text: At startup the server loads all *.md guides from the first populated Skills directory (search order: FORGE_SKILLS_DIR , the source-tree forge_mcp/skills/ , any legacy skills/ directory up the package path, then ./skills ). A one-line index of the loaded guides is injected as the server instructions, and each guide is served on demand by the forge_skill tool ( forge_skill(name="create") / forge_skill(name="modify") / forge_skill(name="operators") / forge_skill(name="custom_material") ), so agents discover the guides automatically but only pay the context cost when used. Pass section to fetch a single heading instead of the whole guide (e.g. forge_skill(name="create", section="joint") or forge_skill(name="operators", section="create_sensor") ). The forge_mcp/docs/mjcf/*.md element reference (same discovery scheme via FORGE_DOCS_DIR / forge_mcp/docs/mjcf on the package path) is loaded into a paragraph-level search index served by forge_search_docs . The same reference is also exposed as MCP resources ( mjcf://<element> per doc file, mjcf://index for the element hierarchy / path registry) so agents that prefer native resource reads can pull a whole document directly; forge_search_docs remains for keyword search. Read forge_skill(name="create") before authoring and forge_skill(name="modify") before editing. Enforcement is controlled by FORGE_MCP_SKILL_GATE : default soft allows the operation and attaches a one-time reading hint after a successful call; strict refuses operations until the required guide has been read. forge_execute uses the same policy for explicit bpy.ops.forge.* calls and Forge_* property writes; ordinary Blender modeling scripts are unaffected by this Forge gate. Tool filters retain forge_skill for operation access. Full authoring rules live in MCP Skills . forge_execute injects bpy and mathutils into the script namespace. Scripts must assign a JSON-serializable dictionary to result , for example result = {"scene": bpy.context.scene.name} . Blender RST documentation is loaded recursively from forge_mcp/docs/blender/ , including api/ and manual/ . Discovery checks FORGE_BLENDER_DOCS_DIR , forge_mcp/docs/blender/ , docs/blender/ along the package's ancestor paths, then ./docs/blender/ ; the first populated directory wins independently of MJCF. Missing Blender documentation is allowed. Restart the server after changing documentation files. forge_search_docs searches both references by default. Use source="mjcf" , "blender" , "blender_api" , or "blender_manual" to narrow results: forge_search_docs ( query = "bpy.ops.mesh.bevel" , source = "blender_api" ) forge_search_docs ( query = "bevel modifier" , source = "blender_manual" , max_results = 5 ) forge_search_docs ( query = "condim" , source = "mjcf" ) RST headings and API directives become section breadcrumbs, including fully qualified function/property names. Text, parameter fields and inline code are searchable; presentation metadata is omitted. This text parser does not build Sphinx, execute directives, or expand external includes. Results contain source , path (e.g. blender/api/bpy.ops.mesh.rst , relative to docs/ ), breadcrumb , text , score , and index ; existing MJCF paths stay unchanged. Results are sorted by score and context stays within the matching section. Documentation search requires no running Blender instance.
docs.title: Skills and document discovery

docs.text: forge_mcp.tools registers tools by module: create.py — forge_create_* : link, inertial, joint, geometry, collider, height_field, plane, site, actuator, tendon, equality, contact, sensor, light, camera, frame, replicate, attach, include, material. modify.py — forge_define_* : model_type, geometry_type, collider_type, site_type, joint_type, actuator_type; plus define_parent, mark_root_link, mark_instance_link, mesh_check, scale_gizmo_size. utilities.py — scene_info, batch_rename, set_instance_idname, select_by_tag, select_hulls. scene.py — generic editing: object_info, measure, scene_config, set_transform, set_shape_size, set_property, set_scene_property, set_tendon_targets, rename, delete, execute. geometry.py — forge_coacd : decompose one Forge VISUAL mesh into new Collider hulls while preserving the source object. io.py — modal MJCF import/export plus explicit blend-file saving. capture.py — forge_screenshot : capture an area (default the 3D viewport) or the whole window as a PNG image, with imbuf downsampling to a size budget; layout=True returns the window layout as JSON instead. blendfile.py — forge_blendfile_summary : path/save status/backups, datablock counts, missing external files, linked libraries (direct vs indirect). docs.py — forge_search_docs : ranked full-text search over the bundled MJCF element reference and local Blender RST API/manual. skill.py — forge_skill : return the full text of an auto-loaded skills/*.md authoring guide, or a single section via section ( forge_skill(name="create", section="joint") ); unknown / ambiguous section names raise listing the available ones. Tools are annotated with MCP ToolAnnotations ( tools/_hints.py ): read-only hints on query tools, destructive hints on recursive delete, arbitrary execute, MJCF import, CoACD and blend-file saving. Every op tool ( create / modify / op wrappers in utilities ) accepts select: list[str] — object names that replace the Blender selection before the operator runs (order matters, first becomes active; null keeps the current selection). Results include created : names of new scene objects, so generated names never need guessing. Conventions worth knowing (learned building a Newton's cradle end-to-end): A joint's exported rotation axis is its local +Z in parent space — rotate the joint object so its Z points along the desired world axis. Shape sizes are local to the parent (a child link's local frame differs from world) — check with forge_measure (world bboxes) after editing. mesh_check ignores boundary-only point-point, point-edge, point-face, edge-edge, and edge-face contact when incident geometry does not cross the other mesh. A coplanar shared face is also valid when its plane separates both complete objects, independent of winding; non-separating coplanar overlap and actual crossings remain intersections. Valid contact needs no epsilon gap. Blender silently suffixes name collisions ( .001 ) — including with orphaned (out-of-scene) datablocks; forge_rename refuses instead. Forge_Model_Type is stored as an enum index ; tools resolve it to names ( LINK , JOINT , ...). Note: bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popup dialogs are UI-only and ineffective for agents — parameters are changed via direct property access ( obj.Forge_<Type>.<property> ) and shape / gizmo sizes via obj.modifiers[...] .
docs.title: Tools

docs.text: From the full repository root: uv sync uv run pytest tests/mcp/unit tests/mcp/integration uv sync installs forge-mcp in editable mode into the root .venv , alongside add-on test dependencies. uv sync --all-packages is also supported. End-to-end tests require Blender; see Development Forge . For server-package development in an independent source directory: cd mcp-server uv venv --python 3 .11 uv pip install --editable . Keep forge_mcp/skills/ and forge_mcp/docs/ with the source. Installer and client startup instructions are maintained only in setup and connection .

docs.text: Forge MCP 服务端参考 ¶ English README 本页介绍 Agent 侧 MCP Server 的运行架构、环境变量、Skills 与文档加载机制、工具分类以及开发调试。首次安装、客户端配置、启动和连接排查统一见 MCP 安装与连接 。 运行架构 ¶ AI Agent ──stdio──> Forge MCP Server ──TCP──> Blender Forge MCP Bridge MCP Server 运行在 Agent 侧；Bridge 运行在拥有场景的 Blender 进程中。场景查询和建模操作经由 Bridge 执行，Skills 读取和文档搜索使用服务本地的文件，不要求 Blender 正在运行。Blender 端的设置和依赖见 配置 Forge 。 客户端启动与进程管理 ¶ 完成 安装与连接 中的环境准备后，按以下流程使用： 在 Blender 中启用 Forge，并启动 MCP Bridge 。 在包含客户端配置的工作区目录启动 Claude Code 或 Codex。 客户端读取工作区配置，自动启动和管理 Forge MCP Server，通过 stdio 与其通信。 在客户端查看 MCP 连接状态，确认 forge 已连接，再执行 Forge 操作。 修改环境变量、Skills 或文档文件后，通过客户端重新连接或重启 MCP 服务。仅重启 Blender Bridge 不会重新加载服务端文档。 运行时配置 ¶ 环境变量 默认值 说明 FORGE_MCP_HOST localhost Blender bridge 主机 FORGE_MCP_PORT 9876 Blender bridge 端口 FORGE_MCP_TOKEN 空 Blender 监听非 localhost 时使用的共享 Token FORGE_MCP_TIMEOUT 1800 响应超时时间（秒） FORGE_MCP_SKILL_GATE soft soft 执行并附带一次阅读提示； strict 要求先读取对应 skill； off 关闭检查 FORGE_SKILLS_DIR 自动搜索 forge_skill 使用的 skill 文档目录 FORGE_DOCS_DIR 自动搜索 forge_search_docs 使用的 MJCF 文档目录 FORGE_BLENDER_DOCS_DIR 自动搜索 Blender API/manual RST 文档根目录 FORGE_TOOLS 全部 按类别或名称过滤工具； readonly 只保留只读工具；无效的非空过滤条件会使服务启动失败 Skills 与文档自动加载 ¶ 启动时服务会加载第一个包含文档的目录： FORGE_SKILLS_DIR ； 源码目录 forge_mcp/skills/ ； 上层目录中的旧版 skills/ ； 当前目录的 ./skills 。 加载的 skill 摘要会注入 MCP server instructions，并通过 forge_skill 按需读取： forge_skill(name="create") forge_skill(name="modify") forge_skill(name="operators") forge_skill(name="custom_material") 可以传入 section 只读取一个章节，例如： forge_skill(name="create", section="joint") 。 MJCF 文档位于 forge_mcp/docs/mjcf/*.md ，通过 forge_search_docs 建立段落级搜索索引，也作为 MCP resources 暴露： mjcf://<element> 和 mjcf://index 。 Blender RST 文档位于 forge_mcp/docs/blender/ ，包括 api/ 和 manual/ 。可用 source="mjcf" 、 "blender" 、 "blender_api" 或 "blender_manual" 限定搜索： forge_search_docs ( query = "bpy.ops.mesh.bevel" , source = "blender_api" ) forge_search_docs ( query = "bevel modifier" , source = "blender_manual" , max_results = 5 ) forge_search_docs ( query = "condim" , source = "mjcf" ) Forge 建模应先读取相应的 create 或 modify skill。实际检查行为由 FORGE_MCP_SKILL_GATE 控制：默认 soft 不阻止操作，而是在成功调用后附带一次阅读提示； strict 才会拒绝尚未读取所需 skill 的操作。 forge_execute 对显式调用 bpy.ops.forge.* 或通过 Forge_* 属性组写入采用相同策略；普通 Blender 建模脚本不受这一 Forge 检查限制。完整创作规则见 英文 MCP Skills 。 forge_execute 会自动向脚本注入 bpy 和 mathutils 。脚本必须把 JSON 可序列化的字典赋给 result ，例如 result = {"scene": bpy.context.scene.name} 。 工具概览 ¶ forge_mcp.tools 按模块注册工具，主要包括： create.py ：创建 link、joint、geometry、material、sensor、camera 等 MJCF 元素； modify.py ：修改模型、geometry、collider、site、joint、actuator 等类型； utilities.py ：场景信息、批量重命名、按 tag 选择等； scene.py ：对象信息、测量、变换、属性设置、重命名、删除和执行操作； geometry.py ：对 Forge visual mesh 执行 CoACD 凸分解； io.py ：MJCF 导入/导出及 blend 文件保存； capture.py ：截取 Blender 区域或窗口； blendfile.py ：blend 文件摘要、缺失外部文件和链接库检查； docs.py ：MJCF 与 Blender 文档全文搜索； skill.py ：读取 skill 全文或指定章节。 所有工具都带有 MCP ToolAnnotations 。写操作、删除、导入、CoACD 和保存等高风险操作会标记相应的 destructive hint 或 approval hint。 开发与测试 ¶ 在完整仓库根目录执行： uv sync uv run pytest tests/mcp/unit tests/mcp/integration uv sync 把 forge-mcp 以可编辑模式安装到根 .venv ，并安装插件测试依赖。也可使用 uv sync --all-packages 。端到端测试需要 Blender，见 开发 Forge 。 仅开发服务包时，可在独立源码目录创建环境： cd mcp-server uv venv --python 3 .11 uv pip install --editable . 保留 forge_mcp/skills/ 和 forge_mcp/docs/ 。安装脚本与客户端启动步骤只在 安装与连接 维护。

docs.text: MCP Skills ¶ These English-only guides describe how agents use Forge MCP tools to create and modify MJCF scenes. They form a separate reference from the Blender UI user manual and MCP installation documentation. Guides ¶ Guide Use it for Forge create Creating model elements and building scene hierarchies Forge modify Editing existing elements, properties, and relationships Forge custom material Creating and checking custom textured materials Forge operators Looking up Operator signatures, selection requirements, and supported tool mappings Before using a skill ¶ Install and enable Forge in Blender, start its MCP Bridge, and configure the agent-side server using the MCP installation guide . For server configuration and runtime details, read the MCP Server README . Read the create or modify guide for workflow rules, then use the operator inventory for individual operations. Use the custom material guide when working with texture-based materials. Language and source ¶ MCP Skills are maintained in English only. Opening them preserves the current interface language: navigation, controls, and links remain Chinese or English while the article stays in English. The language selector changes the interface language, not the skill content. Both interface versions render the same Markdown sources, with no separate Chinese translation to maintain. Individual guides use matching routes under en/mcp_skills/ and cn/mcp_skills/ for the two interface languages. The site builds from portable snapshots in docs/content/reference/mcp-server/forge_mcp/skills/ . To refresh them from the runtime sources in a full Forge checkout, run python docs/scripts/sync_sources.py and review the changes. Preview and builds do not depend on files outside docs/ . Markdown guides added to the snapshot directory are included automatically.

docs.text: Forge create ¶ Create mjcf hierarchy relationship use forge tool. General rules ¶ Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Create the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not create objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider. MCP tool workflow ¶ Prefer the dedicated MCP tools over raw bpy : inspect with forge_blendfile_summary , forge_scene_info , forge_object_info and forge_measure ; create with forge_create_* ; change types/parenting with forge_define_* ; edit with forge_set_transform , forge_set_shape_size , forge_set_property and forge_rename ; validate with forge_mesh_check . Use forge_execute only when no dedicated tool represents the operation. Skill gate scope : generic Blender deletion/removal operations remain available without a Forge guide. Use Forge operations for Forge hierarchy changes, especially forge_define_parent ; do not assign obj.parent directly when establishing a Forge parent relationship. Every bpy.ops.forge.* operator (signature, defaults, poll , MCP wrapper) is inventoried in the operators skill — forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") for a single entry. Follow inspect → create/edit → verify → validate → save/export . Adjust location , rotation , and scale as needed, respecting locked axes. Do not change a component when the corresponding lock_scale , lock_rotation , or lock_location flag is True . Edit the parameters supported by the model type as needed. Existing files—including the current blend path—require explicit overwrite=True ; save_copy=True does not change the active blend path. forge_coacd(name, ...) wraps bpy.ops.forge.coacds for one selected VISUAL mesh. Position the joint at the pivot (e.g. top of a pendulum), not at the body center. First consider the location is at link local space location [0, 0, 0] , then consider location by needing. Otherwise, placement depends on the selected object's type. Select object in type [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] location will at local space [0, 0, 0] . Select object in type [VISUAL, COLLIDER] whose parent is [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : new link parented under that parent, location at selected object's local position and rotation zeroed. Select object in type [VISUAL, COLLIDER] without parent in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : location at selected object's location, marked as Root Link . With no selection, the link is created in the World collection as a root candidate. Use bpy.ops.forge.mark_root_link() to mark it. Export also discovers parentless roots in the Link and Frame collections; those roots are not exported twice. inertial : ¶ Use bpy.ops.forge.create_inertial(inertial_model_type='VISUAL', check_mesh_valid=False) with selected existing link objects. Compute mass, center of mass, and principal inertia from children of the chosen type ( VISUAL or COLLIDER ), recursively through FRAME descendants. Child LINK hierarchies are excluded; at least one matching geometry object is required. Geometry validation is optional and off by default. Mesh geometry requires TetGen; primitive shapes do not. Create one new INERTIAL child per successful Link calculation. Existing inertials are not replaced. joint : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_joint(joint_type='<ENUM>') based on selected existing link object. Parameter joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] , default is HINGE . geometry shape : ¶ visual : use bpy.ops.forge.create_geometry(geometry_type='<ENUM>', size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) Select object in type [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : create one geometry per selected object as child of it, location at local space [0, 0, 0] . Select none objects: create at 3d cursor location. Parameter geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] Parameter used corresponding to geometry_type : BOX : size_box CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height SPHERE : size_radius Size unit is meter collider : use bpy.ops.forge.create_collider(collider_type='<ENUM>', create_method='<ENUM>', auto_size=False, use_min_as_height=False, size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) Method of create_method is GEOMETRY_TYPE or COLLIDER_TYPE : GEOMETRY_TYPE : only for selected visual object(s), will auto detect shape from selected visual, other parameter not need for this method — collider_type is ignored, the collider takes the visual's own geometry type. For a mesh visual, prefer COLLIDER_TYPE with an explicit shape collider whenever that shape meets the collision requirements; use GEOMETRY_TYPE only when its resulting collider type follows the collider selection rule above. COLLIDER_TYPE : will need explicit choose collider_type , this is the only method when select none or select link / frame object. Parameter collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH, SDF] Parameter used corresponding to collider_type when create_method='COLLIDER_TYPE' : BOX : size_box or auto_size CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height or auto_size CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height or auto_size SPHERE : size_radius or auto_size MESH : no other parameter need, only available when visual object(s) selected, bake visual geometry to convex mesh collider SDF : only with selected visuals; shares the visual's Mesh Data as a linked duplicate, preserving its parent and transform. Vertex edits affect both objects. auto_size : auto-detect the selected visual geometry size; off by default. With a link / frame selection or no selection, explicit size_* values (or defaults) are used instead. A replicate selection is not accepted by this operator. use_min_as_height : CAPSULE / CYLINDER only, default is off. When on, the height is taken from the selected visual 's smallest bounding-box axis instead of its largest, and the shape is oriented along that axis. Only takes effect together with auto_size=True — with explicit size_radius / size_height the values are used as given and the flag is ignored. The MCP tool forge_create_collider exposes this as min_is_height . Size unit is meter geometry mesh : ¶ Create with traditional method. Use bpy.ops.forge.define_model_type(Model_Type='<ENUM>') to set object to corresponding model type. Model_Type is corresponding to: VISUAL for visual object, COLLIDER for collider object. hfield : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_height_field() : Only can create when nothing selected, exist as root node without parent. Default location at 3d cursor location. plane : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_plane() : Only can create when nothing selected, exist as root node without parent. Default location at 3d cursor location. site : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_site(site_type='<ENUM>', size_box=(0.2, 0.2, 0.2), size_radius=0.1, size_height=0.2) based on selected existing link object(s). Parameter site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] Parameter used corresponding to site_type : BOX : size_box CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height SPHERE : size_radius Size unit is meter actuator : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_actuator(actuator_type='<ENUM>') based on selected existing link | joint | tendon object(s). Selected joint objects → equality_type is JOINT . Selected link / site objects → equality_type is CONNECT or WELD . contact : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_contact(contact_type='<ENUM>') based on selected existing link | visual | collider | plane | hfield objects. Need select at least 2 objects. Selected link objects → contact_type is EXCLUDE . Selected visual / collider / plane / hfield objects → contact_type is PAIR . Create one contact for each pair combination of selected objects. sensor : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_sensor(Sensor_Type='<ENUM>', set_ref=False, set_xbody=False, set_subtree=False) based on selected existing link | joint | site | visual | collider | camera objects. Select none objects create world light at 3d cursor location, light_type in [DIRECTIONAL, SPOT, POINT] , light_mode in [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] . Select 1 link : light_type in [SPOT, POINT] , light_mode in [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] ; when light_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single world light at 3d cursor location targeting the selected link , other modes create child light of it. Select 2 link s: when light_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single light, first selected is light position, second is target; other modes create one light per selected link as child of it. Select 3+ link s: light_mode restricted to [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] , create one light per selected link as child of it. camera : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_camera(camera_type='<ENUM>', camera_mode='<ENUM>') optionally based on selected existing link object(s). camera_type in [PERSPECTIVE, ORTHOGRAPHIC] . Select none objects create world camera at 3d cursor location, camera_mode in [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] . Select 1 link : camera_mode in [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] ; when camera_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single world camera at 3d cursor location targeting the selected link , other modes create child camera of it. Select 2 link s: when camera_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single camera, first selected is camera position, second is target; other modes create one camera per selected link as child of it. Select 3+ link s: camera_mode restricted to [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] , create one camera per selected link as child of it. frame : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_frame() optionally based on selected existing link | frame | replicate object(s). Select none objects create at 3d cursor location. Select objects create one frame per selected object as child of it. Shift + Click: reverse parent, selected objects become child of new frame. replicate : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_replicate(count=0, sep='', offset=(0, 0, 0), euler=(0, 0, 0)) based on selected existing camera | light | visual | collider | site | link | frame | attach | replicate objects. Parameter count : replicate count. Parameter sep : separator string. Parameter offset : offset vector between copies. Parameter euler : euler rotation between copies. Create single replicate object, selected objects as its source. A replicate owns its source: the selected objects move into the replicate's own viewport-hidden collection and cannot be selected afterwards. Replicate objects that no later operation still needs to select. attach : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_attach() optionally based on selected existing link | frame | replicate object. Need select exactly 1 object or none. Choose file in dialog via Forge_Temp_Props : tmp_file , tmp_model , tmp_prefix , tmp_link . Import the model from external mjcf file into scene, then create attach reference. Requires Forge Library asset library (Preferences -> File Paths -> Asset Libraries). The file must not be one already include d in the scene — attach and include take separate files. Sharing one reports Attach fail: list index out of range . include : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_include() only when nothing selected. Choose file in dialog via Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include . Only add include tag when export, content of the file will not be exported. Material creation rules: ¶ Materials are PBR datablocks from the bundled Forge library — not mjcf model objects; they attach to visual , hfield or plane geometry. material : ¶ Use MCP forge_create_material(category, material, use_existing=True, select=[...]) , which wraps bpy.ops.forge.create_material(category='<str>', material='<str>') , based on selected visual , hfield or plane object(s): Requires a non-empty selection where every object is type VISUAL , HFIELD or PLANE — poll fails when nothing is selected or any other type is selected. Parameter category in [Crystal, Human, Liquid, Manmade, Metal, Organic, Plastic] (~110 materials total). Parameter material is the exact library name inside the category — e.g. Gold , Water , Skin I , Titanium (Anodized) ; names carry parenthesized variants, match them exactly. Enumerate at runtime: Builds a Principled BSDF material datablock named after the library entry (base color is linear, set directly), non-render fields ( density , viscosity , ...) stored as custom ID properties. Parameter use_existing (default True ): when an existing datablock with the same name is present it is assigned as-is — user tweaks are preserved, it is NOT rebuilt from the library. Pass use_existing=False to always build a fresh datablock from the library (Blender suffixes the taken name .001 ). Assigns to the first object-level material slot of every selected object (creating the slot when empty). This applies equally to mesh and primitive visual , hfield , and plane objects; shape/material modifier sockets are not edited by the operator. Enumerate categories / names from Python running inside Blender: import bpy import importlib # Resolve both legacy and extension-managed installs without assuming the # extension repository is named vscode_development or user_default. module_name = next ( ( name for name in bpy . context . preferences . addons . keys () if name == "Forge" or name . endswith ( ".Forge" )), None , ) if module_name is None : raise RuntimeError ( "Enable the Forge add-on before inspecting its material library" ) materials = importlib . import_module ( f " { module_name } .core.materials" ) materials . get_categories () # ['Crystal', 'Human', 'Liquid', ...] materials . get_material_names ( "Metal" ) # ['Aluminum', 'Brass', 'Chromium', ...]

docs.text: Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Create the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not create objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider.

Child LINK hierarchies are excluded; at least one matching geometry object is required. Geometry validation is optional and off by default. Mesh geometry requires TetGen; primitive shapes do not. Create one new INERTIAL child per successful Link calculation. Existing inertials are not replaced.

docs.text: visual : use bpy.ops.forge.create_geometry(geometry_type='<ENUM>', size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) Select object in type [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : create one geometry per selected object as child of it, location at local space [0, 0, 0] . Select none objects: create at 3d cursor location. Parameter geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] Parameter used corresponding to geometry_type : BOX : size_box CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height SPHERE : size_radius Size unit is meter collider : use bpy.ops.forge.create_collider(collider_type='<ENUM>', create_method='<ENUM>', auto_size=False, use_min_as_height=False, size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) Method of create_method is GEOMETRY_TYPE or COLLIDER_TYPE : GEOMETRY_TYPE : only for selected visual object(s), will auto detect shape from selected visual, other parameter not need for this method — collider_type is ignored, the collider takes the visual's own geometry type. For a mesh visual, prefer COLLIDER_TYPE with an explicit shape collider whenever that shape meets the collision requirements; use GEOMETRY_TYPE only when its resulting collider type follows the collider selection rule above. COLLIDER_TYPE : will need explicit choose collider_type , this is the only method when select none or select link / frame object. Parameter collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH, SDF] Parameter used corresponding to collider_type when create_method='COLLIDER_TYPE' : BOX : size_box or auto_size CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height or auto_size CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height or auto_size SPHERE : size_radius or auto_size MESH : no other parameter need, only available when visual object(s) selected, bake visual geometry to convex mesh collider SDF : only with selected visuals; shares the visual's Mesh Data as a linked duplicate, preserving its parent and transform. Vertex edits affect both objects. auto_size : auto-detect the selected visual geometry size; off by default. With a link / frame selection or no selection, explicit size_* values (or defaults) are used instead. A replicate selection is not accepted by this operator. use_min_as_height : CAPSULE / CYLINDER only, default is off. When on, the height is taken from the selected visual 's smallest bounding-box axis instead of its largest, and the shape is oriented along that axis. Only takes effect together with auto_size=True — with explicit size_radius / size_height the values are used as given and the flag is ignored. The MCP tool forge_create_collider exposes this as min_is_height . Size unit is meter

docs.text: Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_sensor(Sensor_Type='<ENUM>', set_ref=False, set_xbody=False, set_subtree=False) based on selected existing link | joint | site | visual | collider | camera objects. Sensor_Type available values are decided by selected target model type: joint : Jointpos , Jointvel site : Touch , Accelerometer , Velocimeter , Gyro , Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact link : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact , Subtreecom , Subtreelinvel , Subtreeangmom link with set_xbody=True : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel link with set_subtree=True : Contact visual / collider : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact camera : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel mixed selection in [LINK, SITE, VISUAL, COLLIDER, CAMERA] (e.g. 2 objects with different types): Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact set_ref=True : need select 2 objects, first selected is target, second is reference; Sensor_Type range as Framepos ~ Contact ; with site target start from Touch ; with link target and set_xbody=True end at Frameangvel . set_xbody / set_subtree only for link target, mutual exclusive. Contact subtree sensors must explicitly set both subtree1 and subtree2 . Select exactly two existing link objects in order [subtree1_root, subtree2_root] , then call forge_create_sensor(sensor_type="Contact", set_ref=True, set_subtree=True, select=[subtree1_root, subtree2_root]) . The first root becomes Forge_Sensor.target (MJCF subtree1 ), the second becomes Forge_Sensor.ref (MJCF subtree2 ). Do not create a one-sided subtree sensor or leave ref unset. Verify both pointers, use_subtree=True and target_type="SUBTREE" ; after export, verify the <contact> sensor contains both attributes with the intended body names.

docs.text: Use MCP forge_create_material(category, material, use_existing=True, select=[...]) , which wraps bpy.ops.forge.create_material(category='<str>', material='<str>') , based on selected visual , hfield or plane object(s): Requires a non-empty selection where every object is type VISUAL , HFIELD or PLANE — poll fails when nothing is selected or any other type is selected. Parameter category in [Crystal, Human, Liquid, Manmade, Metal, Organic, Plastic] (~110 materials total). Parameter material is the exact library name inside the category — e.g. Gold , Water , Skin I , Titanium (Anodized) ; names carry parenthesized variants, match them exactly. Enumerate at runtime: Builds a Principled BSDF material datablock named after the library entry (base color is linear, set directly), non-render fields ( density , viscosity , ...) stored as custom ID properties. Parameter use_existing (default True ): when an existing datablock with the same name is present it is assigned as-is — user tweaks are preserved, it is NOT rebuilt from the library. Pass use_existing=False to always build a fresh datablock from the library (Blender suffixes the taken name .001 ). Assigns to the first object-level material slot of every selected object (creating the slot when empty). This applies equally to mesh and primitive visual , hfield , and plane objects; shape/material modifier sockets are not edited by the operator. Enumerate categories / names from Python running inside Blender: import bpy import importlib # Resolve both legacy and extension-managed installs without assuming the # extension repository is named vscode_development or user_default. module_name = next ( ( name for name in bpy . context . preferences . addons . keys () if name == "Forge" or name . endswith ( ".Forge" )), None , ) if module_name is None : raise RuntimeError ( "Enable the Forge add-on before inspecting its material library" ) materials = importlib . import_module ( f " { module_name } .core.materials" ) materials . get_categories () # ['Crystal', 'Human', 'Liquid', ...] materials . get_material_names ( "Metal" ) # ['Aluminum', 'Brass', 'Chromium', ...]

docs.text: Forge create ¶ Create mjcf hierarchy relationship use forge tool. General rules ¶ Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Create the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not create objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider. MCP tool workflow ¶ Prefer the dedicated MCP tools over raw bpy : inspect with forge_blendfile_summary , forge_scene_info , forge_object_info and forge_measure ; create with forge_create_* ; change types/parenting with forge_define_* ; edit with forge_set_transform , forge_set_shape_size , forge_set_property and forge_rename ; validate with forge_mesh_check . Use forge_execute only when no dedicated tool represents the operation. Skill gate scope : generic Blender deletion/removal operations remain available without a Forge guide. Use Forge operations for Forge hierarchy changes, especially forge_define_parent ; do not assign obj.parent directly when establishing a Forge parent relationship. Every bpy.ops.forge.* operator (signature, defaults, poll , MCP wrapper) is inventoried in the operators skill — forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") for a single entry. Follow inspect → create/edit → verify → validate → save/export . Check the main scene and existing names first; after every creation capture the returned created names, inspect those exact objects, measure relevant world bounds, run forge_mesh_check on related visuals, and use forge_screenshot when visual confirmation adds value. Every MCP select=[...] argument is ordered. The first name becomes Blender's active object and every name receives a selected_order matching its list index. This order determines target/reference roles for tendon, equality, sensor, light/camera targeting and parent operations; never rely on bpy.context.selected_objects iteration order. Before a destructive or file-writing operation, inspect its explicit targets and destination. forge_delete recursively removes every descendant of each named root, so inspect children first and pass only intended roots. Forge mjcf model types ¶ In Forge treat all MJCF tags—including body , inertial , geom , joint , site , actuator , tendon , equality , contact , sensor , light , camera , frame , replicate , attach and include are treated as Blender objects, distinguished by the Forge_Model_Type attribute of the Object type. Code example: # register with bpy.types.Object.Forge_Model_Type bpy . data . objects [ "name_of_object" ] . Forge_Model_Type bpy . context . active_object . Forge_Model_Type bpy . context . selected_objects [ 0 ] . Forge_Model_Type Forge model types are: UNDEFINED , LINK , INERTIAL , VISUAL , COLLIDER , HFIELD , PLANE , JOINT , SITE , ACTUATOR , TENDON , EQUALITY , CONTACT , SENSOR , LIGHT , CAMERA , FRAME , REPLICATE , ATTACH , INCLUDE . UNDEFINED objects are not MJCF elements and are not exported as model elements. LINK represents an MJCF body in Blender's model hierarchy. VISUAL , COLLIDER , HFIELD , and PLANE all represent MJCF geom elements but have distinct Forge types and parameters. The remaining types each also have their own unique set of parameters. Hierarchy rules ¶ An articulated model starts with a root link . An inertial , joint , or site must be a child of a link . visual , collider , light , camera , frame , replicate and attach can either be children of a link , or exist as root nodes without a parent. A collider is never parented under a visual : keep it a sibling of its visual , under the same link . A collider under a visual is not exported — it vanishes from the MJCF — and forge_define_parent refuses to create that nesting. hfield and plane exist as root nodes without a parent for now. In mjcf actuator , tendon , equality , contact and sensor do not use a hierarchy. In Forge, they will be created as children of their corresponding target model type. Create rules ¶ Creation order: ¶ Create elements with bpy.ops.forge.create_<type> , optionally using selected existing model elements as targets. Adjust location , rotation , and scale as needed, respecting locked axes. Do not change a component when the corresponding lock_scale , lock_rotation , or lock_location flag is True . Edit the parameters supported by the model type as needed. File workflow and mesh preprocessing ¶ forge_import_mjcf(filepath, import_material=True) wraps bpy.ops.forge.import_mjcf and waits for its modal job. Import is destructive : it clears scene objects, collections, non-main scenes and orphaned data before rebuilding, so save first when current work matters. envhdr textures are imported into a Blender World environment texture and assigned to the main scene. Mesh assets support OBJ, STL and GLB. GLB accepts exactly one Mesh object; non-Mesh elements are discarded, and zero/multiple Mesh objects fail during asset loading. The Mesh node's transform is baked, file-space coordinates/UVs are preserved, and MJCF mesh scale is applied afterwards. MJCF defines the materials; embedded GLB materials are discarded. Missing/unsupported mesh files fail during asset loading. forge_export_mjcf(filepath, update_forge_only=False, use_glb=False, overwrite=False) wraps bpy.ops.forge.export_mjcf , waits for completion and reports whether the XML exists. Existing destinations require explicit overwrite=True . Export writes a linked World environment image as an MJCF <texture type="envhdr"> ; empty mesh assets (zero vertices or triangles) are skipped and do not produce mesh or geom references. forge_save_blendfile(filepath=None, overwrite=False, save_copy=False) saves the current blend or a named destination. Existing files—including the current blend path—require explicit overwrite=True ; save_copy=True does not change the active blend path. forge_coacd(name, ...) wraps bpy.ops.forge.coacds for one selected VISUAL mesh. It reads triangle faces from the evaluated mesh and creates collider hulls while preserving the source object; generated hull names are returned in created . Important parameters: threshold , max_convex_hull , preprocess_mode , sampling/MCTS controls, merge , decimate / max_ch_vertex , extrude / extrude_margin , and seed . Create tips: ¶ Joints : Joint in forge is Z-UP based and use local +Z in parent space; Rotate the joint object so Z points along the desired rotation axis. Position the joint at the pivot (e.g. top of a pendulum), not at the body center. First consider the location is at link local space location [0, 0, 0] , then consider location by needing. Inertials : create_inertial defaults to inertial_model_type='VISUAL' and check_mesh_valid=False . The operator can also use COLLIDER ; enable check_mesh_valid=True for validation before calculation. The dedicated MCP wrapper uses the defaults. Primitive shapes use analytic mass and inertia; mesh geometry requires TetGen. When validation is enabled, boundary-only contact and separating coplanar faces are valid; actual crossings and non-separating coplanar overlap fail. An epsilon gap is not required for valid contact. Names : operators use type prefixes for object names. If a name already exists, Blender automatically appends a numeric suffix such as .001 or .002 to keep it unique. Read the actual names from the tool's created result instead of guessing them, then use forge_batch_rename if needed. Spacing : geometry sizes given at creation are full dimensions (BOX) / true radius & height (SPHERE / CYLINDER / CAPSULE), exported to mjcf half-extents automatically; all in parent-local meters. Collider : create collider for shape geometry is not necessary, if really necessary need set visual shape geometry obj.Forge_Geometry props contype and conaffinity to 0 . Sensor_Type available values are decided by selected target model type: joint : Jointpos , Jointvel site : Touch , Accelerometer , Velocimeter , Gyro , Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact link : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact , Subtreecom , Subtreelinvel , Subtreeangmom link with set_xbody=True : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel link with set_subtree=True : Contact visual / collider : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact camera : Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel mixed selection in [LINK, SITE, VISUAL, COLLIDER, CAMERA] (e.g. 2 objects with different types): Framepos , Framequat , Framexaxis , Frameyaxis , Framezaxis , Framelinvel , Frameangvel , Contact set_ref=True : need select 2 objects, first selected is target, second is reference; Sensor_Type range as Framepos ~ Contact ; with site target start from Touch ; with link target and set_xbody=True end at Frameangvel . set_xbody / set_subtree only for link target, mutual exclusive. Contact subtree sensors must explicitly set both subtree1 and subtree2 . Select exactly two existing link objects in order [subtree1_root, subtree2_root] , then call forge_create_sensor(sensor_type="Contact", set_ref=True, set_subtree=True, select=[subtree1_root, subtree2_root]) . The first root becomes Forge_Sensor.target (MJCF subtree1 ), the second becomes Forge_Sensor.ref (MJCF subtree2 ). Do not create a one-sided subtree sensor or leave ref unset. Verify both pointers, use_subtree=True and target_type="SUBTREE" ; after export, verify the <contact> sensor contains both attributes with the intended body names. light : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_light(light_type='<ENUM>', light_mode='<ENUM>') optionally based on selected existing link object(s). Select none objects create world light at 3d cursor location, light_type in [DIRECTIONAL, SPOT, POINT] , light_mode in [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] . Select 1 link : light_type in [SPOT, POINT] , light_mode in [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] ; when light_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single world light at 3d cursor location targeting the selected link , other modes create child light of it. Select 2 link s: when light_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single light, first selected is light position, second is target; other modes create one light per selected link as child of it. Select 3+ link s: light_mode restricted to [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] , create one light per selected link as child of it. camera : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_camera(camera_type='<ENUM>', camera_mode='<ENUM>') optionally based on selected existing link object(s). camera_type in [PERSPECTIVE, ORTHOGRAPHIC] . Select none objects create world camera at 3d cursor location, camera_mode in [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] . Select 1 link : camera_mode in [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] ; when camera_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single world camera at 3d cursor location targeting the selected link , other modes create child camera of it. Select 2 link s: when camera_mode is [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM] create single camera, first selected is camera position, second is target; other modes create one camera per selected link as child of it. Select 3+ link s: camera_mode restricted to [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] , create one camera per selected link as child of it. frame : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_frame() optionally based on selected existing link | frame | replicate object(s). Select none objects create at 3d cursor location. Select objects create one frame per selected object as child of it. Shift + Click: reverse parent, selected objects become child of new frame. replicate : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_replicate(count=0, sep='', offset=(0, 0, 0), euler=(0, 0, 0)) based on selected existing camera | light | visual | collider | site | link | frame | attach | replicate objects. Parameter count : replicate count. Parameter sep : separator string. Parameter offset : offset vector between copies. Parameter euler : euler rotation between copies. Create single replicate object, selected objects as its source. A replicate owns its source: the selected objects move into the replicate's own viewport-hidden collection and cannot be selected afterwards. Replicate objects that no later operation still needs to select. attach : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_attach() optionally based on selected existing link | frame | replicate object. Need select exactly 1 object or none. Choose file in dialog via Forge_Temp_Props : tmp_file , tmp_model , tmp_prefix , tmp_link . Import the model from external mjcf file into scene, then create attach reference. Requires Forge Library asset library (Preferences -> File Paths -> Asset Libraries). The file must not be one already include d in the scene — attach and include take separate files. Sharing one reports Attach fail: list index out of range . include : ¶ Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_include() only when nothing selected. Choose file in dialog via Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include . Only add include tag when export, content of the file will not be exported. Material creation rules: ¶ Materials are PBR datablocks from the bundled Forge library — not mjcf model objects; they attach to visual , hfield or plane geometry. material : ¶ Use MCP forge_create_material(category, material, use_existing=True, select=[...]) , which wraps bpy.ops.forge.create_material(category='<str>', material='<str>') , based on selected visual , hfield or plane object(s): Requires a non-empty selection where every object is type VISUAL , HFIELD or PLANE — poll fails when nothing is selected or any other type is selected. Parameter category in [Crystal, Human, Liquid, Manmade, Metal, Organic, Plastic] (~110 materials total). Parameter material is the exact library name inside the category — e.g. Gold , Water , Skin I , Titanium (Anodized) ; names carry parenthesized variants, match them exactly. Enumerate at runtime: Builds a Principled BSDF material datablock named after the library entry (base color is linear, set directly), non-render fields ( density , viscosity , ...) stored as custom ID properties. Parameter use_existing (default True ): when an existing datablock with the same name is present it is assigned as-is — user tweaks are preserved, it is NOT rebuilt from the library. Pass use_existing=False to always build a fresh datablock from the library (Blender suffixes the taken name .001 ). Assigns to the first object-level material slot of every selected object (creating the slot when empty). This applies equally to mesh and primitive visual , hfield , and plane objects; shape/material modifier sockets are not edited by the operator. Enumerate categories / names from Python running inside Blender: import bpy import importlib # Resolve both legacy and extension-managed installs without assuming the # extension repository is named vscode_development or user_default. module_name = next ( ( name for name in bpy . context . preferences . addons . keys () if name == "Forge" or name . endswith ( ".Forge" )), None , ) if module_name is None : raise RuntimeError ( "Enable the Forge add-on before inspecting its material library" ) materials = importlib . import_module ( f " { module_name } .core.materials" ) materials . get_categories () # ['Crystal', 'Human', 'Liquid', ...] materials . get_material_names ( "Metal" ) # ['Aluminum', 'Brass', 'Chromium', ...]

docs.text: Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Create the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not create objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider.
docs.title: General rules

docs.text: Prefer the dedicated MCP tools over raw bpy : inspect with forge_blendfile_summary , forge_scene_info , forge_object_info and forge_measure ; create with forge_create_* ; change types/parenting with forge_define_* ; edit with forge_set_transform , forge_set_shape_size , forge_set_property and forge_rename ; validate with forge_mesh_check . Use forge_execute only when no dedicated tool represents the operation. Skill gate scope : generic Blender deletion/removal operations remain available without a Forge guide. Use Forge operations for Forge hierarchy changes, especially forge_define_parent ; do not assign obj.parent directly when establishing a Forge parent relationship. Every bpy.ops.forge.* operator (signature, defaults, poll , MCP wrapper) is inventoried in the operators skill — forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") for a single entry. Follow inspect → create/edit → verify → validate → save/export . Check the main scene and existing names first; after every creation capture the returned created names, inspect those exact objects, measure relevant world bounds, run forge_mesh_check on related visuals, and use forge_screenshot when visual confirmation adds value. Every MCP select=[...] argument is ordered. The first name becomes Blender's active object and every name receives a selected_order matching its list index. This order determines target/reference roles for tendon, equality, sensor, light/camera targeting and parent operations; never rely on bpy.context.selected_objects iteration order. Before a destructive or file-writing operation, inspect its explicit targets and destination. forge_delete recursively removes every descendant of each named root, so inspect children first and pass only intended roots.
docs.title: MCP tool workflow

docs.text: In Forge treat all MJCF tags—including body , inertial , geom , joint , site , actuator , tendon , equality , contact , sensor , light , camera , frame , replicate , attach and include are treated as Blender objects, distinguished by the Forge_Model_Type attribute of the Object type. Code example: # register with bpy.types.Object.Forge_Model_Type bpy . data . objects [ "name_of_object" ] . Forge_Model_Type bpy . context . active_object . Forge_Model_Type bpy . context . selected_objects [ 0 ] . Forge_Model_Type Forge model types are: UNDEFINED , LINK , INERTIAL , VISUAL , COLLIDER , HFIELD , PLANE , JOINT , SITE , ACTUATOR , TENDON , EQUALITY , CONTACT , SENSOR , LIGHT , CAMERA , FRAME , REPLICATE , ATTACH , INCLUDE . UNDEFINED objects are not MJCF elements and are not exported as model elements. LINK represents an MJCF body in Blender's model hierarchy. VISUAL , COLLIDER , HFIELD , and PLANE all represent MJCF geom elements but have distinct Forge types and parameters. The remaining types each also have their own unique set of parameters.
docs.title: Forge mjcf model types

docs.text: An articulated model starts with a root link . An inertial , joint , or site must be a child of a link . visual , collider , light , camera , frame , replicate and attach can either be children of a link , or exist as root nodes without a parent. A collider is never parented under a visual : keep it a sibling of its visual , under the same link . A collider under a visual is not exported — it vanishes from the MJCF — and forge_define_parent refuses to create that nesting. hfield and plane exist as root nodes without a parent for now. In mjcf actuator , tendon , equality , contact and sensor do not use a hierarchy. In Forge, they will be created as children of their corresponding target model type.
docs.title: Hierarchy rules

docs.text: Create elements with bpy.ops.forge.create_<type> , optionally using selected existing model elements as targets. Adjust location , rotation , and scale as needed, respecting locked axes. Do not change a component when the corresponding lock_scale , lock_rotation , or lock_location flag is True . Edit the parameters supported by the model type as needed.

docs.text: forge_import_mjcf(filepath, import_material=True) wraps bpy.ops.forge.import_mjcf and waits for its modal job. Import is destructive : it clears scene objects, collections, non-main scenes and orphaned data before rebuilding, so save first when current work matters. envhdr textures are imported into a Blender World environment texture and assigned to the main scene. Mesh assets support OBJ, STL and GLB. GLB accepts exactly one Mesh object; non-Mesh elements are discarded, and zero/multiple Mesh objects fail during asset loading. The Mesh node's transform is baked, file-space coordinates/UVs are preserved, and MJCF mesh scale is applied afterwards. MJCF defines the materials; embedded GLB materials are discarded. Missing/unsupported mesh files fail during asset loading. forge_export_mjcf(filepath, update_forge_only=False, use_glb=False, overwrite=False) wraps bpy.ops.forge.export_mjcf , waits for completion and reports whether the XML exists. Existing destinations require explicit overwrite=True . Export writes a linked World environment image as an MJCF <texture type="envhdr"> ; empty mesh assets (zero vertices or triangles) are skipped and do not produce mesh or geom references. forge_save_blendfile(filepath=None, overwrite=False, save_copy=False) saves the current blend or a named destination. Existing files—including the current blend path—require explicit overwrite=True ; save_copy=True does not change the active blend path. forge_coacd(name, ...) wraps bpy.ops.forge.coacds for one selected VISUAL mesh. It reads triangle faces from the evaluated mesh and creates collider hulls while preserving the source object; generated hull names are returned in created . Important parameters: threshold , max_convex_hull , preprocess_mode , sampling/MCTS controls, merge , decimate / max_ch_vertex , extrude / extrude_margin , and seed .
docs.title: File workflow and mesh preprocessing

docs.text: Joints : Joint in forge is Z-UP based and use local +Z in parent space; Rotate the joint object so Z points along the desired rotation axis. Position the joint at the pivot (e.g. top of a pendulum), not at the body center. First consider the location is at link local space location [0, 0, 0] , then consider location by needing. Inertials : create_inertial defaults to inertial_model_type='VISUAL' and check_mesh_valid=False . The operator can also use COLLIDER ; enable check_mesh_valid=True for validation before calculation. The dedicated MCP wrapper uses the defaults. Primitive shapes use analytic mass and inertia; mesh geometry requires TetGen. When validation is enabled, boundary-only contact and separating coplanar faces are valid; actual crossings and non-separating coplanar overlap fail. An epsilon gap is not required for valid contact. Names : operators use type prefixes for object names. If a name already exists, Blender automatically appends a numeric suffix such as .001 or .002 to keep it unique. Read the actual names from the tool's created result instead of guessing them, then use forge_batch_rename if needed. Spacing : geometry sizes given at creation are full dimensions (BOX) / true radius & height (SPHERE / CYLINDER / CAPSULE), exported to mjcf half-extents automatically; all in parent-local meters. Collider : create collider for shape geometry is not necessary, if really necessary need set visual shape geometry obj.Forge_Geometry props contype and conaffinity to 0 .

docs.text: Create use bpy.ops.forge.create_link() optionally based on selected existing object(s): With no selection, the default location is the 3D cursor. Otherwise, placement depends on the selected object's type. Select object in type [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] location will at local space [0, 0, 0] . Select object in type [VISUAL, COLLIDER] whose parent is [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : new link parented under that parent, location at selected object's local position and rotation zeroed. Select object in type [VISUAL, COLLIDER] without parent in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : location at selected object's location, marked as Root Link . With no selection, the link is created in the World collection as a root candidate. Use bpy.ops.forge.mark_root_link() to mark it. Export also discovers parentless roots in the Link and Frame collections; those roots are not exported twice.
docs.title: link:

docs.text: Use bpy.ops.forge.create_inertial(inertial_model_type='VISUAL', check_mesh_valid=False) with selected existing link objects. Compute mass, center of mass, and principal inertia from children of the chosen type ( VISUAL or COLLIDER ), recursively through FRAME descendants. Child LINK hierarchies are excluded; at least one matching geometry object is required. Geometry validation is optional and off by default. Mesh geometry requires TetGen; primitive shapes do not. Create one new INERTIAL child per successful Link calculation. Existing inertials are not replaced.

docs.text: visual : use bpy.ops.forge.create_geometry(geometry_type='<ENUM>', size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) Select object in type [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] : create one geometry per selected object as child of it, location at local space [0, 0, 0] . Select none objects: create at 3d cursor location. Parameter geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] Parameter used corresponding to geometry_type : BOX : size_box CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height SPHERE : size_radius Size unit is meter collider : use bpy.ops.forge.create_collider(collider_type='<ENUM>', create_method='<ENUM>', auto_size=False, use_min_as_height=False, size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) Method of create_method is GEOMETRY_TYPE or COLLIDER_TYPE : GEOMETRY_TYPE : only for selected visual object(s), will auto detect shape from selected visual, other parameter not need for this method — collider_type is ignored, the collider takes the visual's own geometry type. For a mesh visual, prefer COLLIDER_TYPE with an explicit shape collider whenever that shape meets the collision requirements; use GEOMETRY_TYPE only when its resulting collider type follows the collider selection rule above. COLLIDER_TYPE : will need explicit choose collider_type , this is the only method when select none or select link / frame object. Parameter collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH, SDF] Parameter used corresponding to collider_type when create_method='COLLIDER_TYPE' : BOX : size_box or auto_size CAPSULE : size_radius , size_height or auto_size CYLINDER : size_radius , size_height or auto_size SPHERE : size_radius or auto_size MESH : no other parameter need, only available when visual object(s) selected, bake visual geometry to convex mesh collider SDF : only with selected visuals; shares the visual's Mesh Data as a linked duplicate, preserving its parent and transform. Vertex edits affect both objects. auto_size : auto-detect the selected visual geometry size; off by default. With a link / frame selection or no selection, explicit size_* values (or defaults) are used instead. A replicate selection is not accepted by this operator. use_min_as_height : CAPSULE / CYLINDER only, default is off. When on, the height is taken from the selected visual 's smallest bounding-box axis instead of its largest, and the shape is oriented along that axis. Only takes effect together with auto_size=True — with explicit size_radius / size_height the values are used as given and the flag is ignored. The MCP tool forge_create_collider exposes this as min_is_height . Size unit is meter

Enumerate at runtime: Builds a Principled BSDF material datablock named after the library entry (base color is linear, set directly), non-render fields ( density , viscosity , ...) stored as custom ID properties. Parameter use_existing (default True ): when an existing datablock with the same name is present it is assigned as-is — user tweaks are preserved, it is NOT rebuilt from the library. Pass use_existing=False to always build a fresh datablock from the library (Blender suffixes the taken name .001 ). Assigns to the first object-level material slot of every selected object (creating the slot when empty). This applies equally to mesh and primitive visual , hfield , and plane objects; shape/material modifier sockets are not edited by the operator. Enumerate categories / names from Python running inside Blender: import bpy import importlib # Resolve both legacy and extension-managed installs without assuming the # extension repository is named vscode_development or user_default. module_name = next ( ( name for name in bpy . context . preferences . addons . keys () if name == "Forge" or name . endswith ( ".Forge" )), None , ) if module_name is None : raise RuntimeError ( "Enable the Forge add-on before inspecting its material library" ) materials = importlib . import_module ( f " { module_name } .core.materials" ) materials . get_categories () # ['Crystal', 'Human', 'Liquid', ...] materials . get_material_names ( "Metal" ) # ['Aluminum', 'Brass', 'Chromium', ...]
