docs.text: Forge modify ¶ Modify MJCF model elements with Forge tools. General rules ¶ Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Modify the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not modify objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider. MCP tool workflow ¶ Prefer dedicated MCP tools: inspect with forge_blendfile_summary , forge_scene_info , forge_object_info and forge_measure ; change model/type/parent with forge_define_* ; edit values with forge_set_transform , forge_set_shape_size , forge_set_property and forge_rename ; validate with forge_mesh_check . Use forge_execute only for a Forge property or collection edit that no dedicated tool can express. Its skill check applies to explicit bpy.ops.forge.* calls and direct Forge_* property writes; ordinary Blender modelling edits are allowed even when the target object has a Forge model type. Skill gate scope : generic Blender deletion/removal operations remain available without a Forge guide. Use the dedicated Forge operations for Forge hierarchy changes, especially forge_define_parent ; direct obj.parent assignment is only the documented detach escape hatch below. Every bpy.ops.forge.* operator (signature, defaults, poll , MCP wrapper) is inventoried in the operators skill — forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") for a single entry. Follow inspect → edit → verify → validate → save/export . Read object types, parents, locks and current property values before mutation. Re-read every changed object, remeasure world-space bounds, mesh-check the relevant visuals, and use forge_screenshot when visual confirmation adds value. Every MCP select=[...] argument is ordered. The first name becomes the active object and list indices become Forge selected_order values. For forge_define_parent , put the intended parent first and the children after it; for target/reference operations preserve the order documented in the create rules. forge_object_info returns the whole Forge_<Type> group, modifier sockets and transforms — but not Blender-native obj.data . Read light / camera data ( energy , angle , clip_start , ...) with forge_execute ; write it with forge_set_property data: -prefixed keys. forge_delete recursively removes all descendants of every named root. Inspect children first and name only the intended roots. Inspect output destinations before save/export and do not overwrite files unless requested. Modify tips ¶ Joint axis : the exported mjcf axis is the joint object's local +Z expressed in parent space ( obj.matrix_local.to_3x3().transposed()[2] ). Default creation gives +Z along parent +Z; rotate the joint object's euler so its Z aligns with the desired world axis (e.g. rotation_euler = (-90°, 0, 0) makes the axis point along parent +Y). Local vs world coordinates : location and shape sizes are in the parent's local space. When a link sits below / away from the world origin, convert: local = world - parent_world (for unrotated parents). Verify placements with evaluated world bounding boxes, not socket values. Shape size sockets are arrays for BOX ( Socket_0 = full xyz dimensions, written as a 3-tuple) and scalars for SPHERE (visual Socket_0 / collider Socket_3 = radius); assigning a scalar to an array socket raises TypeError . On Blender 5.2+ read/write a socket as mod.properties.inputs.Socket_N.value ; on Blender 4.x–5.1 use mod["Socket_N"] . Prefer forge_set_shape_size , which handles both. Modifier names capitalize the shape ( Geometry_Box , Collider_Sphere ). forge_set_shape_size covers all four shapes: BOX takes the full (x, y, z) tuple, SPHERE a radius, CAPSULE / CYLINDER a (radius, height) pair — height is the full length of the straight section (capsule overall length = height + 2·radius); height socket is visual Socket_2 , collider / site Socket_4 . mesh_check scope : the check reports pairwise intersections between all selected objects. Boundary-only point-point, point-edge, point-face, edge-edge, and edge-face contact is allowed when incident geometry does not cross the other mesh. A coplanar shared face is also allowed when its plane separates the two complete objects (for example aligned boxes placed flush), independent of face winding. Non-separating coplanar area overlap and actual face crossings still count as intersections. Scope selection per-link to avoid reporting unrelated geometry. Name collisions : Blender silently suffixes duplicates ( .001 ) — including against orphaned datablocks left out of the scene after failed operations. Renaming to a "free-looking" name can no-op; check the result or purge orphans first. Locked transforms : Forge locks scale on most model objects (and location/rotation on some); scripts must respect lock_location / lock_rotation / lock_scale instead of assigning. forge_set_property value types are not what the names suggest — always read the returned skipped map. A write that lands in skipped did not happen, and the tool still returns success. Two traps seen in practice: several Forge_* flags are uppercase string enums, not bools (actuator ctrllimited takes 'FALSE' / 'TRUE' / 'AUTO' — passing true or "true" is skipped), and array properties have fixed arity (actuator gear needs 6 elements, not 1). The skipped value carries the underlying bpy_struct message, which names the expected type or arity. Modify rules ¶ Modify order: ¶ Select target object(s). Change the type with the appropriate documented bpy.ops.forge.define_* operator when needed. Edit parameters supported by the model type through obj.Forge_<Type>.<property> directly; popup dialogs are UI-only. Adjust location , rotation , and scale as needed, respecting locked axes. Relationship retargeting: ¶ Post-creation relationship changes go through forge_set_property Object-target properties — pass the target object's name as a string, null clears: actuator.target — any link / joint / tendon object; target_type re-detects from the new target. equality.target1 / target2 — JOINT equality uses target1 and an optional target2 ; when present, both are exported as joint references. contact.target1 / target2 . sensor.target and sensor.ref (frame sensor types and Contact filters). For a Contact subtree sensor, both must reference existing link objects: target exports as subtree1 , ref as subtree2 . Set both explicitly when creating or retargeting; do not clear either endpoint. Verify use_subtree=True , target_type="SUBTREE" and both pointers after editing, and both named attributes in the exported <contact> sensor. light.target / camera.target — only meaningful while mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM . Tendon joint path: forge_set_tendon_targets (ordered replace). attach reference fields ( model / file / link / prefix ) are plain strings, not pointers. Detach has no dedicated implementation : forge_define_parent only assigns a parent; no operator or tool clears one. The only path is the forge_execute escape hatch ( obj.parent = None ; collection membership is not updated) — otherwise report the gap. Model modify rules: ¶ model type : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_model_type(Model_Type='<type>') only for selected UNDEFINED type object(s): Available Model_Type decided by selected object type: EMPTY object: LINK MESH object: VISUAL or COLLIDER LIGHT object: LIGHT CAMERA object: CAMERA VISUAL : set geometry type MESH , group 2 , contype / conaffinity 0 , rename with prefix GEO_ . COLLIDER : set geometry type MESH , group 3 , rename with prefix COL_ . LINK : rename with prefix LNK_ . LIGHT : set light type by Blender light type ( SUN → DIRECTIONAL , else SPOT / POINT ), mode FIXED , rename with prefix LIT_ ; AREA light not support. CAMERA : set camera type by Blender camera type ( ORTHO → ORTHOGRAPHIC , PERSP → PERSPECTIVE ), mode FIXED , rename with prefix CAM_ ; only PERSP / ORTHO camera support. Object with parent move to corresponding type collection, without parent move to WORLD collection. geometry type (visual): ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_geometry_type(geometry_type='<type>', apply_to_all=False) based on selected visual object(s): parameter geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH, SDF] apply_to_all : default False only apply to active object, True apply to all selected. Size is preserved as the bounding-box equivalent; exact shape parameters may differ across a round-trip through another shape (e.g. CYLINDER r=0.05 -> SPHERE -> CYLINDER yields r=0.1). Switch to MESH / SDF : bake primitive geometry into mesh, scale unlock. Switching between MESH and SDF preserves the mesh and modifiers. SDF exports with a mesh asset reference. Switch from MESH / SDF : use object dimensions as size. collider type : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_collider_type(collider_type='<type>', apply_to_all=False) based on selected collider object(s): parameter collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH, SDF] Size is preserved as the bounding-box equivalent; exact shape parameters may differ across a round-trip through another shape (e.g. CYLINDER r=0.05 -> SPHERE -> CYLINDER yields r=0.1). Switch to MESH / SDF : bake current primitive or convex modifier into mesh, scale unlock. Existing mesh geometry is preserved. Switch from MESH / SDF : use object dimensions as size. site type : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_site_type(site_type='<type>', apply_to_all=False) based on selected site object(s): parameter site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] Size is preserved as the bounding-box equivalent; exact shape parameters may differ across a round-trip through another shape. joint type : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_joint_type(joint_type='<type>', apply_to_all=False) based on selected joint object(s): parameter joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] Update joint shape gizmo when type changed. actuator type : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_actuator_type(actuator_type='<type>', apply_to_all=False) based on selected actuator object(s): parameter actuator_type in [GENERAL, MOTOR, POSITION, VELOCITY, ADHESION] parent : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.define_parent() change parent of selected object(s) to active object: Active object is link | frame | replicate : parent selected object(s) in [LINK, VISUAL, COLLIDER, JOINT, SITE, LIGHT, CAMERA, FRAME, REPLICATE, ATTACH] to it. Active object is visual : refused (poll fails) — a collider under a visual is not exported; parent the collider to the link instead. Children of a selected visual object (for example colliders still bound to it) are reparented to the active object first, so a legacy collider -under- visual nesting is repaired rather than recreated. World position of child preserved after reparent. root link : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.mark_root_link() based on selected link | frame | replicate object(s): Parentless objects are marked directly. Objects with a parent are unparented while preserving their world transform, then marked. Set obj["Root Link"] = True . mesh check : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.mesh_check() based on selected visual object(s): Check mesh validation, report error info. Use before compute inertial / export. gizmo size : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.scale_gizmo_size() change gizmo display size of selected object(s), or all objects when none selected: Scale from scene Forge_Props.gizmo_scale . Utilities: ¶ batch rename : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.batch_rename(new_name='', numerate='###') based on selected object(s): Rename selected objects to {new_name}_{index} with zero padding by numerate length, index start from 0. instance idname : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.set_instance_idname() based on selected link object(s): Mark selected links as instances of scene Forge_Props.instance_body ( INSTANCE_IDNAME custom property); run again with no instance body to clear. Links already marked INSTANCE_LINK are refused (warning). Mark the instance source first with bpy.ops.forge.mark_instance_link() ( INSTANCE_LINK custom property, toggle). A marked link never exports as a <body> ; referenced ones provide assets for their copies, unreferenced ones export nothing at all (warned); Forge_Props.instance_body only lists marked links. The instance link's children are written into every INSTANCE_IDNAME link, element names prefixed <instance>_<name> ; global sections ( actuator / sensor / …) are not duplicated per instance. select by tag : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.select_by_tag() only in object mode: Select objects whose name contains scene Forge_Props.select_tag . select hulls : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.select_hulls() only in object mode: Select convex hull objects by name template from addon preferences ( coacd_name_template ). Parameter modify rules: ¶ Each model type has its own parameter group obj.Forge_<Type> on the object — always change parameters by direct property assignment. bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popup dialogs are UI-only and ineffective for agents; never use them. Direct property access: ¶ Parameters grouped by model type, then by sub-type (set property type / mode directly to switch sub-type, same as bpy.ops.forge.define_* ). Shape / gizmo sizes live in geometry-node modifier sockets obj.modifiers[...] — readable / writable as mod.properties.inputs.Socket_N.value on Blender 5.2+ and mod["Socket_N"] on Blender 4.x–5.1. Both surfaces are Forge edits, so forge_set_property and forge_set_shape_size ask for this guide. link : obj.Forge_Link — mocap , gravcomp visual / collider / hfield / plane (all mjcf geom ): obj.Forge_Geometry — group , condim , contype , conaffinity , priority , friction , mass , density , solmix , solref , solimp , margin , gap (hfield / plane UI hides friction / mass / density , but they are exported when non-default) shape size in geometry modifier obj.modifiers[...] : visual : BOX size Socket_0 ; SPHERE size Socket_0 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_0 + height Socket_2 ; MESH no size sockets. Material is the first object-level material slot, assigned by forge_create_material . collider : BOX / SPHERE size Socket_3 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_3 + height Socket_4 ; MESH no size sockets hfield : nrow Socket_0 , ncol Socket_2 , use_elevation Socket_3 , radius_x Socket_4 , radius_y Socket_5 , elevation_z Socket_6 , base_z Socket_7 , height_map Socket_8 , use_height_map Socket_10 , offset Socket_11 ; material is the first object-level material slot. plane : half_size_x Socket_2 , half_size_y Socket_3 , infinite Socket_4 ; material is the first object-level material slot. site : obj.Forge_Geometry — group ; shape size in site modifier: BOX / SPHERE size Socket_3 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_3 + height Socket_4 joint : obj.Forge_Joint per type: range on BALL / HINGE is stored in radians . Export converts it to degrees only when Forge_GlobalConfig.g_compiler.angle == "DEGREE" ; with "RADIAN" it is written unchanged. For a HINGE limit of ±90°, set range = [-pi/2, pi/2] , not [-90, 90] . forge_object_info returns the stored radians. ref and springref on HINGE follow the same rule, and are scalars : a 90° reference is ref = pi/2 , exported as ref="90" . A SLIDE 's range , ref and springref are linear values (meters) and are written unchanged whatever the compiler unit; actuatorfrcrange is a force range, not an angle. A BALL has no ref or springref : MJCF's ball joint does not carry them, so they are not exported at all. FREE : stiffness , armature , damping , frictionloss BALL : springdamper , solreflimit , solimplimit , solreffriction , solimpfriction , stiffness , range , limited , margin , armature , damping , frictionloss SLIDE / HINGE : BALL params + ref , springref , actuatorfrcrange , actuatorfrclimited gizmo modifier: display_size Socket_0 , range display Socket_3 actuator : obj.Forge_Actuator — type , target , target_type (auto-detected from target ) always; per type: GENERAL / MOTOR : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gear , gaintype , biastype , dynprm , gainprm , biasprm POSITION : same as GENERAL + kp , kv , inheritrange VELOCITY : same as GENERAL + kv ADHESION : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gain (no gear / dynprm / gainprm / biasprm ) tendon : obj.Forge_Tendon — type , targets (ordered target path; every targets.items[] has target and exported coef , default 0.5 ; replace safely with forge_set_tendon_targets , or edit with forge.add_tendon_target_item / forge.remove_tendon_target_item ), range , limited , solreflimit , solimplimit , springlength , stiffness , damping equality : obj.Forge_Equality — active , type , target1 , target2 , target_type ; target2 is optional, including for JOINT equality. Type-specific parameters: CONNECT : anchor , solref , solimp WELD : anchor , solref , solimp , relpose JOINT : solref , solimp , polycoef contact : obj.Forge_Contact — type , target1 , target2 always; per type: EXCLUDE : no extra params PAIR : condim , friction , solref , solreffriction , margin , gap sensor : obj.Forge_Sensor — type , target_type , target , noise , cutoff always; per type: Framepos / Framequat / Framexaxis / Frameyaxis / Framezaxis / Framelinvel / Frameangvel : ref_type , ref , use_xbody . ref_type is independent of target_type and exports as MJCF reftype ; use the actual reference object's kind — MJCF reftype accepts only BODY , XBODY , GEOM , SITE , CAMERA , so a JOINT can never be a reference ( create_sensor refuses a selection that pairs a joint with another object). Contact : ref , use_subtree , num (auto-computed from data ), data , reduce . With use_subtree=True , explicitly set both target ( subtree1 ) and ref ( subtree2 ) to link objects; a missing second root is incomplete under this authoring workflow. Touch / Accelerometer / Velocimeter / Gyro / Jointpos / Jointvel / Subtreecom / Subtreelinvel / Subtreeangmom : no extra params light : obj.Forge_Light — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender light data obj.data : use_shadow , color , energy ; SPOT / POINT additionally shadow_soft_size , cutoff_distance ; DIRECTIONAL instead angle ; SPOT additionally spot_size , spot_blend camera : obj.Forge_Camera — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender camera data obj.data : PERSPECTIVE angle / ORTHOGRAPHIC ortho_scale , plus clip_start , clip_end inertial : obj.Forge_Inertial — mass , diaginertia , fullinertia (position / quaternion from object transform) attach : obj.Forge_Attach — model , file , link , prefix replicate : obj.Forge_Replicate — count , sep , offset , euler ( count / offset / euler mirrored to modifier sockets Socket_0 / Socket_2 / Socket_3 ) include : obj.Forge_Include — file is the user-facing/reference filename; rawfile is the resolved source path used by export. Preserve or update rawfile when relocating an include, otherwise export may read the stale source. Scene-level configs — Forge_GlobalConfig / Forge_VisualConfig : ¶ File workflow, compiler / option / statistic and visual settings live on the scene , not on objects. Use forge_scene_config(group) to inspect and forge_set_scene_property(group, values) to edit. The direct equivalents are scene.Forge_Props , scene.Forge_GlobalConfig.<group> and scene.Forge_VisualConfig.<group> (same rule as object params: popup operators are UI-only). Every global/visual group and sub-group has a reset() method; only non-default properties are exported. Forge_Props ( group="forge_props" ) — workflow/display settings: scale_factor , gizmo_scale , rel_path , select_tag , import_file_path , export_path , import_material , update_forge_only , instance_body , world_collection , use_glb . Treat is_importing , is_exporting , is_attaching , is_including , the modal-operation slot ( modal_operation_active , modal_operation_name , modal_operation_token , modal_operation_deferred , modal_operation_status , modal_operation_message , cancel_requested ), progress values and info strings as operation state; read them but do not manually drive them. Only one modal Forge operation may run at a time — a second one fails while modal_operation_active is set. Forge_GlobalConfig — exported as root-level mjcf sections: g_compiler ( <compiler> ): autolimits , angle in [RADIAN, DEGREE] , eulerseq in [XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX] , assetdir , meshdir , texturedir g_option ( <option> ): timestep , iterations , tolerance , gravity (float[3]), o_solref / o_solimp / o_friction (float arrays, contact override), o_margin g_option.flag ( <flag> ): constraint , equality , frictionloss , limit , contact , gravity , actuation , refsafe , override — bool, exported as enable / disable g_statistic ( <statistic> ): extent , center (float[3]) Forge_VisualConfig — exported as the <visual> section: v_global ( <global> ): orthographic , fovy , azimuth , elevation — angle props are radians (converted to degrees at export) v_headlight ( <headlight> ): active (0/1), ambient / diffuse / specular (float[3] color) v_map ( <map> ): fogstart , fogend , znear , zfar v_rgba ( <rgba> ): fog , haze , joint , bv , contactforce (float[4] color) v_quality ( <quality> ): shadowsize , pointshadowsize v_tonemapping ( <tonemapping> ): method in [none, aces] v_ssgi ( <ssgi> ) (Motphys extension): active , resolutionscale , raycount , stepcount , thickness , intensity , gidenoiseoffset , rraycount , rdenoiseoffset Popup dialogs — ineffective for agents: ¶ All bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popups ( properties_link , properties_shape , properties_shape_site , properties_hfield , properties_plane , properties_joint , properties_actuator , properties_tendon , properties_equality , properties_contact , properties_sensor , properties_light , properties_camera , properties_replicate , and scene-level properties_global / properties_visual ) open a modal UI window that cannot be driven programmatically — never use them. Every parameter they edit is reachable via the direct property access above. The file-browser helpers are dialog-driven too — assign their target property directly instead: forge.temp_file / forge.temp_link / forge.temp_include → write scene.Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file / tmp_model / tmp_prefix / tmp_link / tmp_include directly (this is what forge_create_attach / forge_create_include do). forge.file_path / forge.export_path → write scene.Forge_Props.import_file_path / export_path (plus rel_path ) directly (this is what forge_import_mjcf / forge_export_mjcf do).

Renaming to a "free-looking" name can no-op; check the result or purge orphans first. Locked transforms : Forge locks scale on most model objects (and location/rotation on some); scripts must respect lock_location / lock_rotation / lock_scale instead of assigning. forge_set_property value types are not what the names suggest — always read the returned skipped map. A write that lands in skipped did not happen, and the tool still returns success. Two traps seen in practice: several Forge_* flags are uppercase string enums, not bools (actuator ctrllimited takes 'FALSE' / 'TRUE' / 'AUTO' — passing true or "true" is skipped), and array properties have fixed arity (actuator gear needs 6 elements, not 1). The skipped value carries the underlying bpy_struct message, which names the expected type or arity.

docs.text: Parameters grouped by model type, then by sub-type (set property type / mode directly to switch sub-type, same as bpy.ops.forge.define_* ). Shape / gizmo sizes live in geometry-node modifier sockets obj.modifiers[...] — readable / writable as mod.properties.inputs.Socket_N.value on Blender 5.2+ and mod["Socket_N"] on Blender 4.x–5.1. Both surfaces are Forge edits, so forge_set_property and forge_set_shape_size ask for this guide. link : obj.Forge_Link — mocap , gravcomp visual / collider / hfield / plane (all mjcf geom ): obj.Forge_Geometry — group , condim , contype , conaffinity , priority , friction , mass , density , solmix , solref , solimp , margin , gap (hfield / plane UI hides friction / mass / density , but they are exported when non-default) shape size in geometry modifier obj.modifiers[...] : visual : BOX size Socket_0 ; SPHERE size Socket_0 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_0 + height Socket_2 ; MESH no size sockets. Material is the first object-level material slot, assigned by forge_create_material . collider : BOX / SPHERE size Socket_3 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_3 + height Socket_4 ; MESH no size sockets hfield : nrow Socket_0 , ncol Socket_2 , use_elevation Socket_3 , radius_x Socket_4 , radius_y Socket_5 , elevation_z Socket_6 , base_z Socket_7 , height_map Socket_8 , use_height_map Socket_10 , offset Socket_11 ; material is the first object-level material slot. plane : half_size_x Socket_2 , half_size_y Socket_3 , infinite Socket_4 ; material is the first object-level material slot. site : obj.Forge_Geometry — group ; shape size in site modifier: BOX / SPHERE size Socket_3 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_3 + height Socket_4 joint : obj.Forge_Joint per type: range on BALL / HINGE is stored in radians . Export converts it to degrees only when Forge_GlobalConfig.g_compiler.angle == "DEGREE" ; with "RADIAN" it is written unchanged. For a HINGE limit of ±90°, set range = [-pi/2, pi/2] , not [-90, 90] . forge_object_info returns the stored radians. ref and springref on HINGE follow the same rule, and are scalars : a 90° reference is ref = pi/2 , exported as ref="90" . A SLIDE 's range , ref and springref are linear values (meters) and are written unchanged whatever the compiler unit; actuatorfrcrange is a force range, not an angle. A BALL has no ref or springref : MJCF's ball joint does not carry them, so they are not exported at all. FREE : stiffness , armature , damping , frictionloss BALL : springdamper , solreflimit , solimplimit , solreffriction , solimpfriction , stiffness , range , limited , margin , armature , damping , frictionloss SLIDE / HINGE : BALL params + ref , springref , actuatorfrcrange , actuatorfrclimited gizmo modifier: display_size Socket_0 , range display Socket_3 actuator : obj.Forge_Actuator — type , target , target_type (auto-detected from target ) always; per type: GENERAL / MOTOR : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gear , gaintype , biastype , dynprm , gainprm , biasprm POSITION : same as GENERAL + kp , kv , inheritrange VELOCITY : same as GENERAL + kv ADHESION : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gain (no gear / dynprm / gainprm / biasprm ) tendon : obj.Forge_Tendon — type , targets (ordered target path; every targets.items[] has target and exported coef , default 0.5 ; replace safely with forge_set_tendon_targets , or edit with forge.add_tendon_target_item / forge.remove_tendon_target_item ), range , limited , solreflimit , solimplimit , springlength , stiffness , damping equality : obj.Forge_Equality — active , type , target1 , target2 , target_type ; target2 is optional, including for JOINT equality. Type-specific parameters: CONNECT : anchor , solref , solimp WELD : anchor , solref , solimp , relpose JOINT : solref , solimp , polycoef contact : obj.Forge_Contact — type , target1 , target2 always; per type: EXCLUDE : no extra params PAIR : condim , friction , solref , solreffriction , margin , gap sensor : obj.Forge_Sensor — type , target_type , target , noise , cutoff always; per type: Framepos / Framequat / Framexaxis / Frameyaxis / Framezaxis / Framelinvel / Frameangvel : ref_type , ref , use_xbody . ref_type is independent of target_type and exports as MJCF reftype ; use the actual reference object's kind — MJCF reftype accepts only BODY , XBODY , GEOM , SITE , CAMERA , so a JOINT can never be a reference ( create_sensor refuses a selection that pairs a joint with another object). Contact : ref , use_subtree , num (auto-computed from data ), data , reduce . With use_subtree=True , explicitly set both target ( subtree1 ) and ref ( subtree2 ) to link objects; a missing second root is incomplete under this authoring workflow. Touch / Accelerometer / Velocimeter / Gyro / Jointpos / Jointvel / Subtreecom / Subtreelinvel / Subtreeangmom : no extra params light : obj.Forge_Light — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender light data obj.data : use_shadow , color , energy ; SPOT / POINT additionally shadow_soft_size , cutoff_distance ; DIRECTIONAL instead angle ; SPOT additionally spot_size , spot_blend camera : obj.Forge_Camera — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender camera data obj.data : PERSPECTIVE angle / ORTHOGRAPHIC ortho_scale , plus clip_start , clip_end inertial : obj.Forge_Inertial — mass , diaginertia , fullinertia (position / quaternion from object transform) attach : obj.Forge_Attach — model , file , link , prefix replicate : obj.Forge_Replicate — count , sep , offset , euler ( count / offset / euler mirrored to modifier sockets Socket_0 / Socket_2 / Socket_3 ) include : obj.Forge_Include — file is the user-facing/reference filename; rawfile is the resolved source path used by export. Preserve or update rawfile when relocating an include, otherwise export may read the stale source.

docs.text: File workflow, compiler / option / statistic and visual settings live on the scene , not on objects. Use forge_scene_config(group) to inspect and forge_set_scene_property(group, values) to edit. The direct equivalents are scene.Forge_Props , scene.Forge_GlobalConfig.<group> and scene.Forge_VisualConfig.<group> (same rule as object params: popup operators are UI-only). Every global/visual group and sub-group has a reset() method; only non-default properties are exported. Forge_Props ( group="forge_props" ) — workflow/display settings: scale_factor , gizmo_scale , rel_path , select_tag , import_file_path , export_path , import_material , update_forge_only , instance_body , world_collection , use_glb . Treat is_importing , is_exporting , is_attaching , is_including , the modal-operation slot ( modal_operation_active , modal_operation_name , modal_operation_token , modal_operation_deferred , modal_operation_status , modal_operation_message , cancel_requested ), progress values and info strings as operation state; read them but do not manually drive them. Only one modal Forge operation may run at a time — a second one fails while modal_operation_active is set. Forge_GlobalConfig — exported as root-level mjcf sections: g_compiler ( <compiler> ): autolimits , angle in [RADIAN, DEGREE] , eulerseq in [XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX] , assetdir , meshdir , texturedir g_option ( <option> ): timestep , iterations , tolerance , gravity (float[3]), o_solref / o_solimp / o_friction (float arrays, contact override), o_margin g_option.flag ( <flag> ): constraint , equality , frictionloss , limit , contact , gravity , actuation , refsafe , override — bool, exported as enable / disable g_statistic ( <statistic> ): extent , center (float[3]) Forge_VisualConfig — exported as the <visual> section: v_global ( <global> ): orthographic , fovy , azimuth , elevation — angle props are radians (converted to degrees at export) v_headlight ( <headlight> ): active (0/1), ambient / diffuse / specular (float[3] color) v_map ( <map> ): fogstart , fogend , znear , zfar v_rgba ( <rgba> ): fog , haze , joint , bv , contactforce (float[4] color) v_quality ( <quality> ): shadowsize , pointshadowsize v_tonemapping ( <tonemapping> ): method in [none, aces] v_ssgi ( <ssgi> ) (Motphys extension): active , resolutionscale , raycount , stepcount , thickness , intensity , gidenoiseoffset , rraycount , rdenoiseoffset
docs.title: Scene-level configs — Forge_GlobalConfig / Forge_VisualConfig:

docs.text: All bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popups ( properties_link , properties_shape , properties_shape_site , properties_hfield , properties_plane , properties_joint , properties_actuator , properties_tendon , properties_equality , properties_contact , properties_sensor , properties_light , properties_camera , properties_replicate , and scene-level properties_global / properties_visual ) open a modal UI window that cannot be driven programmatically — never use them. Every parameter they edit is reachable via the direct property access above. The file-browser helpers are dialog-driven too — assign their target property directly instead: forge.temp_file / forge.temp_link / forge.temp_include → write scene.Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file / tmp_model / tmp_prefix / tmp_link / tmp_include directly (this is what forge_create_attach / forge_create_include do). forge.file_path / forge.export_path → write scene.Forge_Props.import_file_path / export_path (plus rel_path ) directly (this is what forge_import_mjcf / forge_export_mjcf do).

docs.text: Forge modify ¶ Modify MJCF model elements with Forge tools. General rules ¶ Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Modify the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not modify objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider. MCP tool workflow ¶ Prefer dedicated MCP tools: inspect with forge_blendfile_summary , forge_scene_info , forge_object_info and forge_measure ; change model/type/parent with forge_define_* ; edit values with forge_set_transform , forge_set_shape_size , forge_set_property and forge_rename ; validate with forge_mesh_check . Use forge_execute only for a Forge property or collection edit that no dedicated tool can express. Its skill check applies to explicit bpy.ops.forge.* calls and direct Forge_* property writes; ordinary Blender modelling edits are allowed even when the target object has a Forge model type. Skill gate scope : generic Blender deletion/removal operations remain available without a Forge guide. Use the dedicated Forge operations for Forge hierarchy changes, especially forge_define_parent ; direct obj.parent assignment is only the documented detach escape hatch below. Every bpy.ops.forge.* operator (signature, defaults, poll , MCP wrapper) is inventoried in the operators skill — forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") for a single entry. Follow inspect → edit → verify → validate → save/export . Read object types, parents, locks and current property values before mutation. Re-read every changed object, remeasure world-space bounds, mesh-check the relevant visuals, and use forge_screenshot when visual confirmation adds value. Every MCP select=[...] argument is ordered. The first name becomes the active object and list indices become Forge selected_order values. For forge_define_parent , put the intended parent first and the children after it; for target/reference operations preserve the order documented in the create rules. forge_object_info returns the whole Forge_<Type> group, modifier sockets and transforms — but not Blender-native obj.data . Read light / camera data ( energy , angle , clip_start , ...) with forge_execute ; write it with forge_set_property data: -prefixed keys. forge_delete recursively removes all descendants of every named root. Inspect children first and name only the intended roots. Inspect output destinations before save/export and do not overwrite files unless requested. Modify tips ¶ Joint axis : the exported mjcf axis is the joint object's local +Z expressed in parent space ( obj.matrix_local.to_3x3().transposed()[2] ). Default creation gives +Z along parent +Z; rotate the joint object's euler so its Z aligns with the desired world axis (e.g. rotation_euler = (-90°, 0, 0) makes the axis point along parent +Y). Local vs world coordinates : location and shape sizes are in the parent's local space. When a link sits below / away from the world origin, convert: local = world - parent_world (for unrotated parents). Verify placements with evaluated world bounding boxes, not socket values. Shape size sockets are arrays for BOX ( Socket_0 = full xyz dimensions, written as a 3-tuple) and scalars for SPHERE (visual Socket_0 / collider Socket_3 = radius); assigning a scalar to an array socket raises TypeError . On Blender 5.2+ read/write a socket as mod.properties.inputs.Socket_N.value ; on Blender 4.x–5.1 use mod["Socket_N"] . Prefer forge_set_shape_size , which handles both. Modifier names capitalize the shape ( Geometry_Box , Collider_Sphere ). forge_set_shape_size covers all four shapes: BOX takes the full (x, y, z) tuple, SPHERE a radius, CAPSULE / CYLINDER a (radius, height) pair — height is the full length of the straight section (capsule overall length = height + 2·radius); height socket is visual Socket_2 , collider / site Socket_4 . mesh_check scope : the check reports pairwise intersections between all selected objects. Boundary-only point-point, point-edge, point-face, edge-edge, and edge-face contact is allowed when incident geometry does not cross the other mesh. A coplanar shared face is also allowed when its plane separates the two complete objects (for example aligned boxes placed flush), independent of face winding. Non-separating coplanar area overlap and actual face crossings still count as intersections. Scope selection per-link to avoid reporting unrelated geometry. A marked link never exports as a <body> ; referenced ones provide assets for their copies, unreferenced ones export nothing at all (warned); Forge_Props.instance_body only lists marked links. The instance link's children are written into every INSTANCE_IDNAME link, element names prefixed <instance>_<name> ; global sections ( actuator / sensor / …) are not duplicated per instance. select by tag : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.select_by_tag() only in object mode: Select objects whose name contains scene Forge_Props.select_tag . select hulls : ¶ bpy.ops.forge.select_hulls() only in object mode: Select convex hull objects by name template from addon preferences ( coacd_name_template ). Parameter modify rules: ¶ Each model type has its own parameter group obj.Forge_<Type> on the object — always change parameters by direct property assignment. bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popup dialogs are UI-only and ineffective for agents; never use them. Direct property access: ¶ Parameters grouped by model type, then by sub-type (set property type / mode directly to switch sub-type, same as bpy.ops.forge.define_* ). Shape / gizmo sizes live in geometry-node modifier sockets obj.modifiers[...] — readable / writable as mod.properties.inputs.Socket_N.value on Blender 5.2+ and mod["Socket_N"] on Blender 4.x–5.1. Both surfaces are Forge edits, so forge_set_property and forge_set_shape_size ask for this guide. link : obj.Forge_Link — mocap , gravcomp visual / collider / hfield / plane (all mjcf geom ): obj.Forge_Geometry — group , condim , contype , conaffinity , priority , friction , mass , density , solmix , solref , solimp , margin , gap (hfield / plane UI hides friction / mass / density , but they are exported when non-default) shape size in geometry modifier obj.modifiers[...] : visual : BOX size Socket_0 ; SPHERE size Socket_0 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_0 + height Socket_2 ; MESH no size sockets. Material is the first object-level material slot, assigned by forge_create_material . collider : BOX / SPHERE size Socket_3 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_3 + height Socket_4 ; MESH no size sockets hfield : nrow Socket_0 , ncol Socket_2 , use_elevation Socket_3 , radius_x Socket_4 , radius_y Socket_5 , elevation_z Socket_6 , base_z Socket_7 , height_map Socket_8 , use_height_map Socket_10 , offset Socket_11 ; material is the first object-level material slot. plane : half_size_x Socket_2 , half_size_y Socket_3 , infinite Socket_4 ; material is the first object-level material slot. site : obj.Forge_Geometry — group ; shape size in site modifier: BOX / SPHERE size Socket_3 ; CAPSULE / CYLINDER size Socket_3 + height Socket_4 joint : obj.Forge_Joint per type: range on BALL / HINGE is stored in radians . Export converts it to degrees only when Forge_GlobalConfig.g_compiler.angle == "DEGREE" ; with "RADIAN" it is written unchanged. For a HINGE limit of ±90°, set range = [-pi/2, pi/2] , not [-90, 90] . forge_object_info returns the stored radians. ref and springref on HINGE follow the same rule, and are scalars : a 90° reference is ref = pi/2 , exported as ref="90" . A SLIDE 's range , ref and springref are linear values (meters) and are written unchanged whatever the compiler unit; actuatorfrcrange is a force range, not an angle. A BALL has no ref or springref : MJCF's ball joint does not carry them, so they are not exported at all. FREE : stiffness , armature , damping , frictionloss BALL : springdamper , solreflimit , solimplimit , solreffriction , solimpfriction , stiffness , range , limited , margin , armature , damping , frictionloss SLIDE / HINGE : BALL params + ref , springref , actuatorfrcrange , actuatorfrclimited gizmo modifier: display_size Socket_0 , range display Socket_3 actuator : obj.Forge_Actuator — type , target , target_type (auto-detected from target ) always; per type: GENERAL / MOTOR : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gear , gaintype , biastype , dynprm , gainprm , biasprm POSITION : same as GENERAL + kp , kv , inheritrange VELOCITY : same as GENERAL + kv ADHESION : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gain (no gear / dynprm / gainprm / biasprm ) tendon : obj.Forge_Tendon — type , targets (ordered target path; every targets.items[] has target and exported coef , default 0.5 ; replace safely with forge_set_tendon_targets , or edit with forge.add_tendon_target_item / forge.remove_tendon_target_item ), range , limited , solreflimit , solimplimit , springlength , stiffness , damping equality : obj.Forge_Equality — active , type , target1 , target2 , target_type ; target2 is optional, including for JOINT equality. Type-specific parameters: CONNECT : anchor , solref , solimp WELD : anchor , solref , solimp , relpose JOINT : solref , solimp , polycoef contact : obj.Forge_Contact — type , target1 , target2 always; per type: EXCLUDE : no extra params PAIR : condim , friction , solref , solreffriction , margin , gap sensor : obj.Forge_Sensor — type , target_type , target , noise , cutoff always; per type: Framepos / Framequat / Framexaxis / Frameyaxis / Framezaxis / Framelinvel / Frameangvel : ref_type , ref , use_xbody . ref_type is independent of target_type and exports as MJCF reftype ; use the actual reference object's kind — MJCF reftype accepts only BODY , XBODY , GEOM , SITE , CAMERA , so a JOINT can never be a reference ( create_sensor refuses a selection that pairs a joint with another object). Contact : ref , use_subtree , num (auto-computed from data ), data , reduce . With use_subtree=True , explicitly set both target ( subtree1 ) and ref ( subtree2 ) to link objects; a missing second root is incomplete under this authoring workflow. Touch / Accelerometer / Velocimeter / Gyro / Jointpos / Jointvel / Subtreecom / Subtreelinvel / Subtreeangmom : no extra params light : obj.Forge_Light — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender light data obj.data : use_shadow , color , energy ; SPOT / POINT additionally shadow_soft_size , cutoff_distance ; DIRECTIONAL instead angle ; SPOT additionally spot_size , spot_blend camera : obj.Forge_Camera — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender camera data obj.data : PERSPECTIVE angle / ORTHOGRAPHIC ortho_scale , plus clip_start , clip_end inertial : obj.Forge_Inertial — mass , diaginertia , fullinertia (position / quaternion from object transform) attach : obj.Forge_Attach — model , file , link , prefix replicate : obj.Forge_Replicate — count , sep , offset , euler ( count / offset / euler mirrored to modifier sockets Socket_0 / Socket_2 / Socket_3 ) include : obj.Forge_Include — file is the user-facing/reference filename; rawfile is the resolved source path used by export. Preserve or update rawfile when relocating an include, otherwise export may read the stale source. Scene-level configs — Forge_GlobalConfig / Forge_VisualConfig : ¶ File workflow, compiler / option / statistic and visual settings live on the scene , not on objects. Use forge_scene_config(group) to inspect and forge_set_scene_property(group, values) to edit. The direct equivalents are scene.Forge_Props , scene.Forge_GlobalConfig.<group> and scene.Forge_VisualConfig.<group> (same rule as object params: popup operators are UI-only). Every global/visual group and sub-group has a reset() method; only non-default properties are exported. Forge_Props ( group="forge_props" ) — workflow/display settings: scale_factor , gizmo_scale , rel_path , select_tag , import_file_path , export_path , import_material , update_forge_only , instance_body , world_collection , use_glb . Treat is_importing , is_exporting , is_attaching , is_including , the modal-operation slot ( modal_operation_active , modal_operation_name , modal_operation_token , modal_operation_deferred , modal_operation_status , modal_operation_message , cancel_requested ), progress values and info strings as operation state; read them but do not manually drive them. Only one modal Forge operation may run at a time — a second one fails while modal_operation_active is set. Forge_GlobalConfig — exported as root-level mjcf sections: g_compiler ( <compiler> ): autolimits , angle in [RADIAN, DEGREE] , eulerseq in [XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX] , assetdir , meshdir , texturedir g_option ( <option> ): timestep , iterations , tolerance , gravity (float[3]), o_solref / o_solimp / o_friction (float arrays, contact override), o_margin g_option.flag ( <flag> ): constraint , equality , frictionloss , limit , contact , gravity , actuation , refsafe , override — bool, exported as enable / disable g_statistic ( <statistic> ): extent , center (float[3]) Forge_VisualConfig — exported as the <visual> section: v_global ( <global> ): orthographic , fovy , azimuth , elevation — angle props are radians (converted to degrees at export) v_headlight ( <headlight> ): active (0/1), ambient / diffuse / specular (float[3] color) v_map ( <map> ): fogstart , fogend , znear , zfar v_rgba ( <rgba> ): fog , haze , joint , bv , contactforce (float[4] color) v_quality ( <quality> ): shadowsize , pointshadowsize v_tonemapping ( <tonemapping> ): method in [none, aces] v_ssgi ( <ssgi> ) (Motphys extension): active , resolutionscale , raycount , stepcount , thickness , intensity , gidenoiseoffset , rraycount , rdenoiseoffset Popup dialogs — ineffective for agents: ¶ All bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popups ( properties_link , properties_shape , properties_shape_site , properties_hfield , properties_plane , properties_joint , properties_actuator , properties_tendon , properties_equality , properties_contact , properties_sensor , properties_light , properties_camera , properties_replicate , and scene-level properties_global / properties_visual ) open a modal UI window that cannot be driven programmatically — never use them. Every parameter they edit is reachable via the direct property access above. The file-browser helpers are dialog-driven too — assign their target property directly instead: forge.temp_file / forge.temp_link / forge.temp_include → write scene.Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file / tmp_model / tmp_prefix / tmp_link / tmp_include directly (this is what forge_create_attach / forge_create_include do). forge.file_path / forge.export_path → write scene.Forge_Props.import_file_path / export_path (plus rel_path ) directly (this is what forge_import_mjcf / forge_export_mjcf do).

docs.text: Specification compliance : these guides are the authoritative specification of the Forge tool surface — strictly follow the rules, signatures, parameter ranges and workflows documented here. Never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. Runtime inspection through the MCP tools ( forge_object_info , forge_scene_config , ...) is allowed. No undocumented operations : work only through what these guides document. When a needed operation, parameter or enum value has no documented implementation, do not improvise with raw bpy or undocumented APIs — stop and report the gap (what was attempted, what is missing) as feedback. Main scene : the main scene must be named Scene . Forge resolves the active scene through scene.Main_Scene (defaults to "Scene" ), e.g. bpy.data.scenes[scene.Main_Scene].Forge_Props . Modify the model in the scene named Scene only — do not rename or delete it, and do not modify objects in another scene. Collider selection : prefer shape colliders ( BOX , CAPSULE , CYLINDER , SPHERE ). Consider a MESH collider only when shape colliders cannot meet the required collision geometry or accuracy. A mesh visual alone is not a reason to choose a mesh collider.
docs.title: General rules

docs.text: Prefer dedicated MCP tools: inspect with forge_blendfile_summary , forge_scene_info , forge_object_info and forge_measure ; change model/type/parent with forge_define_* ; edit values with forge_set_transform , forge_set_shape_size , forge_set_property and forge_rename ; validate with forge_mesh_check . Use forge_execute only for a Forge property or collection edit that no dedicated tool can express. Its skill check applies to explicit bpy.ops.forge.* calls and direct Forge_* property writes; ordinary Blender modelling edits are allowed even when the target object has a Forge model type. Skill gate scope : generic Blender deletion/removal operations remain available without a Forge guide. Use the dedicated Forge operations for Forge hierarchy changes, especially forge_define_parent ; direct obj.parent assignment is only the documented detach escape hatch below. Every bpy.ops.forge.* operator (signature, defaults, poll , MCP wrapper) is inventoried in the operators skill — forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") for a single entry. Follow inspect → edit → verify → validate → save/export . Read object types, parents, locks and current property values before mutation. Re-read every changed object, remeasure world-space bounds, mesh-check the relevant visuals, and use forge_screenshot when visual confirmation adds value. Every MCP select=[...] argument is ordered. The first name becomes the active object and list indices become Forge selected_order values. For forge_define_parent , put the intended parent first and the children after it; for target/reference operations preserve the order documented in the create rules. forge_object_info returns the whole Forge_<Type> group, modifier sockets and transforms — but not Blender-native obj.data . Read light / camera data ( energy , angle , clip_start , ...) with forge_execute ; write it with forge_set_property data: -prefixed keys. forge_delete recursively removes all descendants of every named root. Inspect children first and name only the intended roots. Inspect output destinations before save/export and do not overwrite files unless requested.
docs.title: MCP tool workflow

docs.text: Joint axis : the exported mjcf axis is the joint object's local +Z expressed in parent space ( obj.matrix_local.to_3x3().transposed()[2] ). Default creation gives +Z along parent +Z; rotate the joint object's euler so its Z aligns with the desired world axis (e.g. rotation_euler = (-90°, 0, 0) makes the axis point along parent +Y). Local vs world coordinates : location and shape sizes are in the parent's local space. When a link sits below / away from the world origin, convert: local = world - parent_world (for unrotated parents). Verify placements with evaluated world bounding boxes, not socket values. Shape size sockets are arrays for BOX ( Socket_0 = full xyz dimensions, written as a 3-tuple) and scalars for SPHERE (visual Socket_0 / collider Socket_3 = radius); assigning a scalar to an array socket raises TypeError . On Blender 5.2+ read/write a socket as mod.properties.inputs.Socket_N.value ; on Blender 4.x–5.1 use mod["Socket_N"] . Prefer forge_set_shape_size , which handles both. Modifier names capitalize the shape ( Geometry_Box , Collider_Sphere ). forge_set_shape_size covers all four shapes: BOX takes the full (x, y, z) tuple, SPHERE a radius, CAPSULE / CYLINDER a (radius, height) pair — height is the full length of the straight section (capsule overall length = height + 2·radius); height socket is visual Socket_2 , collider / site Socket_4 . mesh_check scope : the check reports pairwise intersections between all selected objects. Boundary-only point-point, point-edge, point-face, edge-edge, and edge-face contact is allowed when incident geometry does not cross the other mesh. A coplanar shared face is also allowed when its plane separates the two complete objects (for example aligned boxes placed flush), independent of face winding. Non-separating coplanar area overlap and actual face crossings still count as intersections. Scope selection per-link to avoid reporting unrelated geometry. Name collisions : Blender silently suffixes duplicates ( .001 ) — including against orphaned datablocks left out of the scene after failed operations. Renaming to a "free-looking" name can no-op; check the result or purge orphans first. Locked transforms : Forge locks scale on most model objects (and location/rotation on some); scripts must respect lock_location / lock_rotation / lock_scale instead of assigning. forge_set_property value types are not what the names suggest — always read the returned skipped map. A write that lands in skipped did not happen, and the tool still returns success. Two traps seen in practice: several Forge_* flags are uppercase string enums, not bools (actuator ctrllimited takes 'FALSE' / 'TRUE' / 'AUTO' — passing true or "true" is skipped), and array properties have fixed arity (actuator gear needs 6 elements, not 1). The skipped value carries the underlying bpy_struct message, which names the expected type or arity.

docs.text: Post-creation relationship changes go through forge_set_property Object-target properties — pass the target object's name as a string, null clears: actuator.target — any link / joint / tendon object; target_type re-detects from the new target. equality.target1 / target2 — JOINT equality uses target1 and an optional target2 ; when present, both are exported as joint references. contact.target1 / target2 . sensor.target and sensor.ref (frame sensor types and Contact filters). For a Contact subtree sensor, both must reference existing link objects: target exports as subtree1 , ref as subtree2 . Set both explicitly when creating or retargeting; do not clear either endpoint. Verify use_subtree=True , target_type="SUBTREE" and both pointers after editing, and both named attributes in the exported <contact> sensor. light.target / camera.target — only meaningful while mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM . Tendon joint path: forge_set_tendon_targets (ordered replace). attach reference fields ( model / file / link / prefix ) are plain strings, not pointers. Detach has no dedicated implementation : forge_define_parent only assigns a parent; no operator or tool clears one. The only path is the forge_execute escape hatch ( obj.parent = None ; collection membership is not updated) — otherwise report the gap.

A BALL has no ref or springref : MJCF's ball joint does not carry them, so they are not exported at all. FREE : stiffness , armature , damping , frictionloss BALL : springdamper , solreflimit , solimplimit , solreffriction , solimpfriction , stiffness , range , limited , margin , armature , damping , frictionloss SLIDE / HINGE : BALL params + ref , springref , actuatorfrcrange , actuatorfrclimited gizmo modifier: display_size Socket_0 , range display Socket_3 actuator : obj.Forge_Actuator — type , target , target_type (auto-detected from target ) always; per type: GENERAL / MOTOR : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gear , gaintype , biastype , dynprm , gainprm , biasprm POSITION : same as GENERAL + kp , kv , inheritrange VELOCITY : same as GENERAL + kv ADHESION : ctrllimited , ctrlrange , forcelimited , forcerange , gain (no gear / dynprm / gainprm / biasprm ) tendon : obj.Forge_Tendon — type , targets (ordered target path; every targets.items[] has target and exported coef , default 0.5 ; replace safely with forge_set_tendon_targets , or edit with forge.add_tendon_target_item / forge.remove_tendon_target_item ), range , limited , solreflimit , solimplimit , springlength , stiffness , damping equality : obj.Forge_Equality — active , type , target1 , target2 , target_type ; target2 is optional, including for JOINT equality. Type-specific parameters: CONNECT : anchor , solref , solimp WELD : anchor , solref , solimp , relpose JOINT : solref , solimp , polycoef contact : obj.Forge_Contact — type , target1 , target2 always; per type: EXCLUDE : no extra params PAIR : condim , friction , solref , solreffriction , margin , gap sensor : obj.Forge_Sensor — type , target_type , target , noise , cutoff always; per type: Framepos / Framequat / Framexaxis / Frameyaxis / Framezaxis / Framelinvel / Frameangvel : ref_type , ref , use_xbody . ref_type is independent of target_type and exports as MJCF reftype ; use the actual reference object's kind — MJCF reftype accepts only BODY , XBODY , GEOM , SITE , CAMERA , so a JOINT can never be a reference ( create_sensor refuses a selection that pairs a joint with another object). Contact : ref , use_subtree , num (auto-computed from data ), data , reduce . With use_subtree=True , explicitly set both target ( subtree1 ) and ref ( subtree2 ) to link objects; a missing second root is incomplete under this authoring workflow. Touch / Accelerometer / Velocimeter / Gyro / Jointpos / Jointvel / Subtreecom / Subtreelinvel / Subtreeangmom : no extra params light : obj.Forge_Light — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender light data obj.data : use_shadow , color , energy ; SPOT / POINT additionally shadow_soft_size , cutoff_distance ; DIRECTIONAL instead angle ; SPOT additionally spot_size , spot_blend camera : obj.Forge_Camera — type , mode ; target only when mode is TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM ; Blender camera data obj.data : PERSPECTIVE angle / ORTHOGRAPHIC ortho_scale , plus clip_start , clip_end inertial : obj.Forge_Inertial — mass , diaginertia , fullinertia (position / quaternion from object transform) attach : obj.Forge_Attach — model , file , link , prefix replicate : obj.Forge_Replicate — count , sep , offset , euler ( count / offset / euler mirrored to modifier sockets Socket_0 / Socket_2 / Socket_3 ) include : obj.Forge_Include — file is the user-facing/reference filename; rawfile is the resolved source path used by export. Preserve or update rawfile when relocating an include, otherwise export may read the stale source.

docs.text: File workflow, compiler / option / statistic and visual settings live on the scene , not on objects. Use forge_scene_config(group) to inspect and forge_set_scene_property(group, values) to edit. The direct equivalents are scene.Forge_Props , scene.Forge_GlobalConfig.<group> and scene.Forge_VisualConfig.<group> (same rule as object params: popup operators are UI-only). Every global/visual group and sub-group has a reset() method; only non-default properties are exported. Forge_Props ( group="forge_props" ) — workflow/display settings: scale_factor , gizmo_scale , rel_path , select_tag , import_file_path , export_path , import_material , update_forge_only , instance_body , world_collection , use_glb . Treat is_importing , is_exporting , is_attaching , is_including , the modal-operation slot ( modal_operation_active , modal_operation_name , modal_operation_token , modal_operation_deferred , modal_operation_status , modal_operation_message , cancel_requested ), progress values and info strings as operation state; read them but do not manually drive them. Only one modal Forge operation may run at a time — a second one fails while modal_operation_active is set. Forge_GlobalConfig — exported as root-level mjcf sections: g_compiler ( <compiler> ): autolimits , angle in [RADIAN, DEGREE] , eulerseq in [XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX] , assetdir , meshdir , texturedir g_option ( <option> ): timestep , iterations , tolerance , gravity (float[3]), o_solref / o_solimp / o_friction (float arrays, contact override), o_margin g_option.flag ( <flag> ): constraint , equality , frictionloss , limit , contact , gravity , actuation , refsafe , override — bool, exported as enable / disable g_statistic ( <statistic> ): extent , center (float[3]) Forge_VisualConfig — exported as the <visual> section: v_global ( <global> ): orthographic , fovy , azimuth , elevation — angle props are radians (converted to degrees at export) v_headlight ( <headlight> ): active (0/1), ambient / diffuse / specular (float[3] color) v_map ( <map> ): fogstart , fogend , znear , zfar v_rgba ( <rgba> ): fog , haze , joint , bv , contactforce (float[4] color) v_quality ( <quality> ): shadowsize , pointshadowsize v_tonemapping ( <tonemapping> ): method in [none, aces] v_ssgi ( <ssgi> ) (Motphys extension): active , resolutionscale , raycount , stepcount , thickness , intensity , gidenoiseoffset , rraycount , rdenoiseoffset

docs.text: All bpy.ops.forge.properties_* popups ( properties_link , properties_shape , properties_shape_site , properties_hfield , properties_plane , properties_joint , properties_actuator , properties_tendon , properties_equality , properties_contact , properties_sensor , properties_light , properties_camera , properties_replicate , and scene-level properties_global / properties_visual ) open a modal UI window that cannot be driven programmatically — never use them. Every parameter they edit is reachable via the direct property access above. The file-browser helpers are dialog-driven too — assign their target property directly instead: forge.temp_file / forge.temp_link / forge.temp_include → write scene.Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file / tmp_model / tmp_prefix / tmp_link / tmp_include directly (this is what forge_create_attach / forge_create_include do). forge.file_path / forge.export_path → write scene.Forge_Props.import_file_path / export_path (plus rel_path ) directly (this is what forge_import_mjcf / forge_export_mjcf do).

docs.text: Forge custom material ¶ Create, inspect, or repair a Blender material that follows the custom textured-material node contract documented by the Forge material workflow. When this skill applies ¶ Use this guide when a Forge VISUAL , HEIGHT FIELD , or PLANE needs a custom Blender material with texture maps, or when an existing material must be checked before MJCF export. The graph is an authoring contract: keep the four framed branches separate so each branch can be disconnected and replaced by a Principled BSDF parameter when a texture is not needed. The material is assigned through the object's first material slot. Do not confuse that slot with Forge geometry properties such as group , friction , or density . Required graph ¶ Build one ShaderNodeOutputMaterial and one ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled . Keep the Principled node's name set to exactly Principled BSDF , because the Forge exporter resolves this node by name. Connect the BSDF to the Output Surface . Use one ShaderNodeTexCoord and one ShaderNodeMapping as the shared coordinate source: Texture Coordinate (UV) -> Mapping (Vector) ├-> albedo Image Texture (Vector) ├-> ARM Image Texture (Vector) ├-> normal Image Texture (Vector) └-> emission Image Texture (Vector) The reference Mapping node is Type: Point , Location: (0, 0, 0) , Rotation: (0°, 0°, 0°) , and Scale: (1, 1, 1) . Use the UV output for ordinary mesh assets. If the asset intentionally uses generated/object coordinates, keep that choice consistent for every image branch. Base Color branch (orange frame) ¶ Image Texture for the albedo/base-color map. Use the image's native color data as sRGB . Feed its Color to a ShaderNodeMix configured with data_type = "RGBA" , blend_type = "MULTIPLY" , and Factor = 1.0 ; keep the other color input ( B ) white ( (1, 1, 1, 1) ). Connect the multiply result to Principled BSDF Base Color . If no albedo map is required, disconnect this branch and set the BSDF Base Color directly; do not leave a dead texture link that claims a texture dependency. Alpha branch (conditional) ¶ Alpha is linked only when the material's intended use requires transparency. Decide this from the material usage, not from Blender's surface_render_method or blend_method properties. Use an explicit usage decision such as: OPAQUE : no Alpha link; SEMITRANSPARENT : create the Alpha link; MASK_CLIP : create the Alpha link. For SEMITRANSPARENT or MASK_CLIP , the source color layer must be rgba ; an rgb layer must not create an Alpha link. Opaque materials, hashed/dithered-only materials, and the importer's direct material.texture path do not get a synthesized Alpha link. The material-usage decision is the gate; the rgba role only confirms that an alpha source exists. Keep the material's base alpha value as the second input of a ShaderNodeMath set to MULTIPLY with clamping enabled (the importer uses the linear material alpha; the default is 1.0 ). Connect the RGBA color Image Texture Alpha output to the Math node's first input, then connect the Math result to Principled BSDF Alpha . When there is no RGBA layer, leave Principled Alpha unlinked and use its direct scalar value. If an explicit material rgba parameter has an alpha below 1.0 , set that direct value even when no texture is present. Do not infer alpha from an RGB image, ARM, normal, or emission map. The branch is opt-in and must be disconnected when the material is opaque or its source is absent. ARM branch (green frame) ¶ ARM is a packed, non-color texture. Set its Image Texture color space to Non-Color and connect its Color to ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ Vector . Separate XYZ Y (the packed roughness channel) -> a ShaderNodeMath set to MULTIPLY , with the other value at 1.0 and clamping enabled -> Principled Roughness . Separate XYZ Z (the packed metallic channel) -> a second clamped MULTIPLY with the other value at 1.0 -> Principled Metallic . Separate XYZ X is the packed ambient-occlusion channel. The reference graph does not connect it to Principled; leave it unconnected unless the intended material workflow explicitly adds AO handling outside the Forge export contract. If ARM is absent, disconnect the roughness/metallic links and use the BSDF's direct scalar parameters. The multiply nodes are identity controls in the reference ( Value = 1.0 , Clamp enabled). Preserve them when repairing the reference graph; changing them changes the exported channel values. Normal branch (blue frame) ¶ Image Texture for the normal map, color space Non-Color . Image Color -> ShaderNodeNormalMap Color . Normal Map Strength = 1.0 , Space = Tangent . Normal Map Normal -> Principled BSDF Normal . Without a normal map, disconnect the branch and leave the BSDF Normal input unlinked. Emission branch (teal frame) ¶ Image Texture for the emission map. The reference uses sRGB . Image Color -> ShaderNodeMix with data_type = "RGBA" , blend_type = "MULTIPLY" , Factor = 1.0 , and the other color input ( B ) white. Connect the result to Principled BSDF Emission Color . Set Principled Emission Strength to the desired value; the reference image uses 10.0 . Without an emission map, disconnect this branch and use the BSDF's direct emission color/strength. Reference defaults ¶ The screenshot shows these useful defaults: Principled IOR = 1.5 , Alpha = 1.0 ; image textures use Interpolation: Linear , Projection: Flat , Extension: Repeat , and Single Image ; Normal Map Strength = 1.0 ; Mapping scale (1, 1, 1) . Treat these as reference values, not reasons to overwrite intentional material settings. Construction and repair rules ¶ Inspect the existing material and its first node tree before editing. Reuse image datablocks where possible; do not duplicate images merely to rename nodes. Keep one shared Mapping node and fan its Vector output out to every active image branch. A branch may omit the Mapping connection only when it deliberately uses another documented coordinate source. Use explicit node types and socket links, not screen coordinates or node labels alone. Labels such as Tex_*_alb , Tex_*_arm , Tex_*_nrm , and *_Emissive are helpful conventions but are not substitutes for links. Set texture color space by data meaning: albedo/emission are sRGB ; ARM/normal are Non-Color . Preserve the four branch boundaries (Base Color, ARM, Normal, Emission). Each branch can be replaced by a direct Principled input when its map is unavailable. Validate every link after construction: Output Surface, Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, Normal, and Emission Color must resolve to the intended sockets; verify image paths exist and the material is in the object's first slot. A pure-parameter material is valid: no texture needs to be connected to Principled when direct BSDF values are intended. If no tiling is needed, the Mapping node may be omitted from the image vectors. Before export, ensure the graph still matches this contract. The Forge documentation warns that an incompatible custom graph can cause export failure; report unsupported node conversions instead of silently approximating them. Minimal Blender Python skeleton ¶ Use this as a construction pattern, adapting image loading and material values to the asset. It deliberately leaves the ARM X/AO output unconnected, matching the reference image, and only adds the Alpha link when the material usage is SEMITRANSPARENT or MASK_CLIP and the color layer role is rgba . import bpy mat = bpy . data . materials . new ( "Custom_Material" ) mat . use_nodes = True nt = mat . node_tree nt . nodes . clear () out = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeOutputMaterial" ) bsdf = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled" ) bsdf . name = "Principled BSDF" texcoord = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeTexCoord" ) mapping = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeMapping" ) mapping . vector_type = "POINT" mapping . inputs [ "Scale" ] . default_value = ( 1.0 , 1.0 , 1.0 ) nt . links . new ( texcoord . outputs [ "UV" ], mapping . inputs [ "Vector" ]) def image_node ( image , label , non_color = False ): node = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeTexImage" ) node . image = image node . label = label node . interpolation = "Linear" node . projection = "FLAT" node . extension = "REPEAT" image . colorspace_settings . name = "Non-Color" if non_color else "sRGB" nt . links . new ( mapping . outputs [ "Vector" ], node . inputs [ "Vector" ]) return node def color_multiply ( label ): node = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeMix" ) node . data_type = "RGBA" node . blend_type = "MULTIPLY" node . inputs [ "Factor" ] . default_value = 1.0 node . inputs [ "B" ] . default_value = ( 1.0 , 1.0 , 1.0 , 1.0 ) node . label = label return node def value_multiply ( label ): node = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeMath" ) node . operation = "MULTIPLY" node . use_clamp = True node . inputs [ 1 ] . default_value = 1.0 node . label = label return node # Supply Image datablocks (or None for a direct BSDF parameter) before running # this block, for example: albedo_image = bpy.data.images.get("wood_alb.png"). # A None value leaves that branch unlinked and uses the BSDF parameter instead. # Replace these placeholders with the appropriate Image datablocks. albedo_image = None arm_image = None normal_image = None emission_image = None color_layer_role = "rgb" # use "rgba" only when the source layer explicitly carries alpha material_usage = "OPAQUE" # or "SEMITRANSPARENT" / "MASK_CLIP" base_alpha = 1.0 bsdf . inputs [ "Alpha" ] . default_value = base_alpha alb = image_node ( albedo_image , "Tex_material_alb" ) if albedo_image else None arm = image_node ( arm_image , "Tex_material_arm" , non_color = True ) if arm_image else None nrm = image_node ( normal_image , "Tex_material_nrm" , non_color = True ) if normal_image else None emi = image_node ( emission_image , "Tex_material_emission" ) if emission_image else None if alb : alb_mix = color_multiply ( "Base Color Multiply" ) nt . links . new ( alb . outputs [ "Color" ], alb_mix . inputs [ "A" ]) nt . links . new ( alb_mix . outputs [ "Result" ], bsdf . inputs [ "Base Color" ]) alpha_required = color_layer_role == "rgba" and material_usage in { "SEMITRANSPARENT" , "MASK_CLIP" } if alpha_required : alpha_mul = value_multiply ( "Alpha Multiply" ) alpha_mul . inputs [ 1 ] . default_value = base_alpha nt . links . new ( alb . outputs [ "Alpha" ], alpha_mul . inputs [ 0 ]) nt . links . new ( alpha_mul . outputs [ "Value" ], bsdf . inputs [ "Alpha" ]) if arm : sep = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ" ) rough_mul = value_multiply ( "ARM Roughness Multiply" ) metal_mul = value_multiply ( "ARM Metallic Multiply" ) nt . links . new ( arm . outputs [ "Color" ], sep . inputs [ "Vector" ]) nt . links . new ( sep . outputs [ "Y" ], rough_mul . inputs [ 0 ]) nt . links . new ( sep . outputs [ "Z" ], metal_mul . inputs [ 0 ]) nt . links . new ( rough_mul . outputs [ "Value" ], bsdf . inputs [ "Roughness" ]) nt . links . new ( metal_mul . outputs [ "Value" ], bsdf . inputs [ "Metallic" ]) if nrm : normal = nt . nodes . new ( "ShaderNodeNormalMap" ) normal . space = "TANGENT" normal . inputs [ "Strength" ] . default_value = 1.0 nt . links . new ( nrm . outputs [ "Color" ], normal . inputs [ "Color" ]) nt . links . new ( normal . outputs [ "Normal" ], bsdf . inputs [ "Normal" ]) if emi : emi_mix = color_multiply ( "Emission Multiply" ) nt . links . new ( emi . outputs [ "Color" ], emi_mix . inputs [ "A" ]) emission_input = bsdf . inputs . get ( "Emission Color" ) or bsdf . inputs . get ( "Emission" ) if emission_input : nt . links . new ( emi_mix . outputs [ "Result" ], emission_input ) if bsdf . inputs . get ( "Emission Strength" ): bsdf . inputs [ "Emission Strength" ] . default_value = 10.0 nt . links . new ( bsdf . outputs [ "BSDF" ], out . inputs [ "Surface" ]) # Replace this placeholder with the requested Forge VISUAL, HFIELD, or PLANE. target = bpy . data . objects [ "Visual" ] if not target . material_slots : target . data . materials . append ( None ) target . material_slots [ 0 ] . link = "OBJECT" target . material_slots [ 0 ] . material = mat result = { "object" : target . name , "material" : mat . name } When modifying an existing material, prefer preserving its material name and image assignments. After editing, inspect the node links and save/export only to the user-specified destination.
