docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME] , or all VISUAL , or nothing selected. create_method='GEOMETRY_TYPE' (default): only with visual selection — auto-detects shape from each visual ( MESH included); size params unused and collider_type is ignored (the collider takes the visual's own geometry type). create_method='COLLIDER_TYPE' : explicit collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH] with size params or auto_size=True (measure from selected visual); MESH bakes the visual geometry into a convex mesh collider and needs a visual selection. auto_size=True is ignored with a link / frame selection or no selection: with no selected visual to measure, explicit size parameters (or their defaults) are used. A replicate selection is not accepted by this operator. use_min_as_height=True : CAPSULE/CYLINDER only — the height is taken from the selected visual 's smallest bounding-box axis rather than its largest, and the shape is oriented along that axis. Only effective together with auto_size=True ; with explicit size_radius / size_height the values are used as given and the flag is ignored. MCP: forge_create_collider (exposes this parameter as min_is_height ).
docs.title: forge.create_collider(collider_type='BOX', create_method='GEOMETRY_TYPE', auto_size=False, use_min_as_height=False, size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1)

docs.text: Requires: nothing selected. Creates a root hfield node (no parent) in the World collection at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_height_field .
docs.title: forge.create_height_field()

docs.text: Requires: nothing selected. Creates a root plane node (no parent) in the World collection at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_plane .
docs.title: forge.create_plane()

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK . One site per selected link as its child. site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] ; size param mapping as create_geometry . MCP: forge_create_site .
docs.title: forge.create_site(site_type='SPHERE', size_box=(0.2, 0.2, 0.2), size_radius=0.1, size_height=0.2)

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] , or all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER] , or nothing selected. No parameters. Based on [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] → child at local [0, 0, 0] ; based on VISUAL / COLLIDER with forge parent → sibling under that parent at the object's local position; based on parentless VISUAL / COLLIDER → link at the object's location marked Root Link ; nothing selected → World collection root candidate (mark with forge.mark_root_link ). MCP: forge_create_link .
docs.title: forge.create_link()

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK . One joint per selected link as its child. joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] . MCP: forge_create_joint .
docs.title: forge.create_joint(joint_type='HINGE')

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, JOINT, TENDON] . One actuator per selected target. actuator_type in [GENERAL, MOTOR, POSITION, VELOCITY, ADHESION] . MCP: forge_create_actuator .
docs.title: forge.create_actuator(actuator_type='POSITION')

docs.text: Requires: at least 2 selected, all JOINT , every joint subtype in [SLIDE, HINGE] . Creates a single tendon from the ordered selection; each target item exports coef (default 0.5 ). tendon_type currently only FIXED . MCP: forge_create_tendon .
docs.title: forge.create_tendon(tendon_type='FIXED')

docs.text: Requires: exactly 2 selected, all LINK , all JOINT or all SITE . Dynamic type items: JOINT selection → JOINT only (joint-coupling equality); LINK / SITE selection → CONNECT / WELD . Ordered selection: first object is target1 , second is target2 . MCP: forge_create_equality .
docs.title: forge.create_equality(equality_type='CONNECT')

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK , all JOINT , all SITE , all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER] , or all in [LINK, SITE, VISUAL, COLLIDER, CAMERA] (mixed — also covers camera-only selections). Available Sensor_Type items are computed from the selection / flags — full ranges in the create skill (joint → Jointpos / Jointvel ; site → Touch … Contact ; link → frame + subtree types; visual/collider → frame types + Contact ; camera → frame types only). set_ref=True : needs exactly 2 selected — first is target, second is reference. set_xbody / set_subtree : only for LINK targets, mutually exclusive ( xbody → xbody frame sensors, subtree → Contact only). Contact subtree workflow: require exactly two LINK roots and use both set_ref=True and set_subtree=True . Ordered selection maps the first root to subtree1 ( target ), the second to subtree2 ( ref ); both must be explicitly set and verified in the exported sensor. MCP: forge_create_sensor .
docs.title: forge.create_sensor(Sensor_Type, set_ref=False, set_xbody=False, set_subtree=False)

docs.text: Requires: at least 2 selected, all LINK , or all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER, PLANE, HFIELD] . Dynamic type items: LINK selection → EXCLUDE (default); geom selection → PAIR (default). Creates one contact per pair combination of the ordered selection (n·(n−1)/2 objects). MCP: forge_create_contact .
docs.title: forge.create_contact(contact_type)

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK , or nothing selected. Dynamic items: nothing selected → light_type [DIRECTIONAL, SPOT, POINT] , light_mode [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (defaults DIRECTIONAL / FIXED ); links selected → light_type [SPOT, POINT] (default SPOT ); 1–2 links → light_mode full [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default TARGETBODY ), 3+ links or nothing selected → [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default FIXED ). 1 link + TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM → single world light at the 3D cursor targeting that link; 2 links + targeting mode → single light, first selected is position, second is target; otherwise one light per link as its child. Nothing selected → world light at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_light .
docs.title: forge.create_light(light_type, light_mode)

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK , or nothing selected. camera_type in [PERSPECTIVE, ORTHOGRAPHIC] . Dynamic camera_mode : 1–2 links selected → full [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default TARGETBODY ); nothing or 3+ links selected → [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default FIXED ). 1 link + targeting mode → single world camera at the 3D cursor targeting that link; 2 links + targeting mode → single camera, first selected is position, second is target; otherwise one camera per link as its child. Nothing selected → world camera at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_camera .
docs.title: forge.create_camera(camera_type='PERSPECTIVE', camera_mode)

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, REPLICATE, FRAME] , or nothing selected. One frame per selected object as its child; nothing selected → World root at the 3D cursor. Shift+Click in the UI reverses parenting (selected objects become children of the new frame) — reverse_parent is a plain class attribute, not an operator parameter; scripts use forge_define_parent instead. MCP: forge_create_frame .
docs.title: forge.create_frame()

docs.text: Requires: selection non-empty and all in [CAMERA, LIGHT, VISUAL, COLLIDER, SITE, LINK, FRAME, ATTACH, REPLICATE] . Creates a single replicate object with the selection as its sources; copies differ by offset / euler and are named with sep . Moves the sources (with their subtrees) into the replicate's own collection, created viewport-hidden. Blender cannot select objects there, so a later operator over them selects nothing and fails its poll ( context is incorrect ). MCP: forge_create_replicate .
docs.title: forge.create_replicate(count=0, sep='', offset=(0, 0, 0), euler=(0, 0, 0))

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK (links without children are skipped). Collects children of the selected type ( VISUAL or COLLIDER ), recursively through FRAME descendants, without entering child LINK hierarchies; needs at least one matching geometry object. Mesh validation runs only when check_mesh_valid=True . A failed check skips the Link. Primitive shapes use analytic mass and inertia; MESH geometry requires TetGen. A successful calculation creates a new INERTIAL child without replacing existing inertials. MCP: forge_create_inertial uses the defaults above and accepts only select . For the other calculation options, use the documented operator parameters through forge_execute .
docs.title: forge.create_inertial(inertial_model_type='VISUAL', check_mesh_valid=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection non-empty and all in [VISUAL, HFIELD, PLANE] (materials can be assigned to visual, height-field and plane geometry). category / material are exact bundled Forge PBR library names; use_existing=True assigns an existing same-named datablock as-is, False always rebuilds (Blender suffixes the taken name). Assignment uses the first object-level material slot, creating it when empty; the operator does not write primitive geometry-node material sockets. MCP: forge_create_material .
docs.title: forge.create_material(category, material, use_existing=True)

docs.text: Requires: selection non-empty and all in [VISUAL, HFIELD, PLANE] . material is the exact name of an existing Blender material, including any Blender suffix. Reuses its nodes and settings as-is, assigning the first object-level material slot on each selected object. Does not create or copy a material; other slots and unselected object assignments are preserved. MCP: call through forge_execute after reading the modify skill.
docs.title: forge.assign_material(material)

docs.text: Requires: selection all UNDEFINED (plain Blender objects). Available Model_Type from the Blender object type: EMPTY → LINK ; MESH → VISUAL or COLLIDER ; LIGHT → LIGHT ; CAMERA → CAMERA . Side effects: VISUAL sets geometry type MESH , group 2 , contype / conaffinity 0 , prefix GEO_ ; COLLIDER sets type MESH , group 3 , prefix COL_ ; LINK prefix LNK_ ; LIGHT maps Blender type ( SUN → DIRECTIONAL , else SPOT / POINT , AREA cancels), mode FIXED , prefix LIT_ ; CAMERA maps ORTHO / PERSP (others cancel), mode FIXED , prefix CAM_ . Objects move to the matching type collection ( WORLD when parentless). MCP: forge_define_model_type .
docs.title: forge.define_model_type(Model_Type)

docs.text: Requires: selection all VISUAL . geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH] ; size preserved when switching shapes; to MESH bakes current geometry and unlocks scale; from MESH uses object dimensions as size. apply_to_all=False applies to the active object only. MCP: forge_define_geometry_type .
docs.title: forge.define_geometry_type(geometry_type='MESH', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all COLLIDER . Behavior as define_geometry_type (size preserved, MESH bakes). MCP: forge_define_collider_type .
docs.title: forge.define_collider_type(collider_type='SPHERE', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all SITE . site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] ; size preserved. MCP: forge_define_site_type .
docs.title: forge.define_site_type(site_type='SPHERE', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all JOINT . joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] ; updates the joint shape gizmo. MCP: forge_define_joint_type .
docs.title: forge.define_joint_type(joint_type='HINGE', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all ACTUATOR . actuator_type in [GENERAL, MOTOR, POSITION, VELOCITY, ADHESION] . MCP: forge_define_actuator_type .
docs.title: forge.define_actuator_type(actuator_type='POSITION', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: an active object plus selection. Active VISUAL is refused — a collider under a visual is not exported. Active in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] → parents selected objects of type [LINK, VISUAL, COLLIDER, JOINT, SITE, LIGHT, CAMERA, FRAME, REPLICATE, ATTACH] to it; children of a selected VISUAL are lifted to the same parent first. Active object itself is skipped. World position of children is preserved. Every reparented object moves into the collection of its model type ( visual → Visual , collider → Collider , …), so a root object in World leaves it. Ordered selection matters: parent first, children after (MCP forge_define_parent ). MCP: forge_define_parent .
docs.title: forge.define_parent()

docs.text: Requires: any selection. Renames each selected object to {new_name}_{index} with zero padding of numerate length, index from 0 in Blender's selected-object iteration order; this is not the recorded click order. MCP: forge_batch_rename .
docs.title: forge.batch_rename(new_name='', numerate='###')

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, VISUAL] . Applies only to selected LINK objects (Frame and Visual objects are skipped): writes obj["INSTANCE_IDNAME"] = Forge_Props.instance_body (an object reference that survives renames), or removes the property when no instance body is chosen. Reports how many links were marked / cleared. Links already marked INSTANCE_LINK are refused (warning). The instance source is a link marked with INSTANCE_LINK (via forge.mark_instance_link ); Forge_Props.instance_body (panel Instance field) only accepts marked links. A marked instance link never appears as a <body> in the multibody tree; a referenced one feeds the <asset> section with its subtree's meshes / materials, while an unreferenced one exports nothing at all (warned). Export semantics: the instance link's children are written into every link marked with INSTANCE_IDNAME = <instance link name> . Each such link keeps its own body element (name / pos / quat / link props) but its children are replaced by the copy, with every element name prefixed "<instance>_<name>" (camera / light target refs inside the subtree renamed too). Instance subtrees gather no assets of their own, and global sections ( actuator / sensor / tendon / equality / contact ) are not duplicated per instance — don't reference instance-link-internal elements from them. A marked link nested inside a template subtree is never copied as a <body> either — its content still only exports through the placeholders referencing it. MCP: forge_set_instance_idname .
docs.title: forge.set_instance_idname()

docs.text: Requires: object mode. Adds every scene object whose name contains the main scene's Forge_Props.select_tag to the current selection — it does not clear first, so pre-selected objects stay selected. An empty select_tag matches every object name ( "" is contained in any string) and therefore selects the whole scene. MCP: forge_select_by_tag .
docs.title: forge.select_by_tag()

docs.text: Requires: Object Mode. Adds selectable objects whose Forge type matches the main scene's Forge_Props.select_model_type to the current selection; existing selection is preserved. No dedicated MCP wrapper. Set Forge_Props.select_model_type and invoke the documented operator through forge_execute when needed.
docs.title: forge.select_by_model_type()

docs.text: Requires: object mode. Selects every scene object whose full name matches the addon preference coacd_name_template interpreted as a pattern ( ? → any name segment, # → digits) — the same template CoACD uses to name hulls. MCP: forge_select_hulls .
docs.title: forge.select_hulls()

docs.text: No poll. Sets gizmo display of selected objects — or all objects in the blend file when nothing is selected — using the main scene's Forge_Props.gizmo_scale relative to each object's stored base size: modifier Socket_0 for JOINT / CONTACT / EQUALITY / TENDON / ACTUATOR / SENSOR , empty_display_size for LINK / FRAME / ATTACH . INERTIAL display is determined by mass and inertia and is excluded. MCP: forge_scale_gizmo_size .
docs.title: forge.scale_gizmo_size()

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] . Parentless objects are marked with obj["Root Link"] = True ; objects that have a parent are first unparented while preserving world transform, then marked. MCP: forge_mark_root_link .
docs.title: forge.mark_root_link()

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK . Toggles obj["INSTANCE_LINK"] = True per selected link (run again to unmark); reports how many links were marked / unmarked. A marked instance link never exports as a <body> ; its children are written under every INSTANCE_IDNAME link. A referenced marked link feeds the <asset> section with its subtree's meshes / materials; an unreferenced one exports nothing at all (warned). Forge_Props.instance_body 's picker only lists marked links. MCP: forge_mark_instance_link .
docs.title: forge.mark_instance_link()

docs.text: Requires: selection all VISUAL . Reports self- and pairwise intersections (boundary-only contact and separating coplanar faces are valid — details in the modify skill). Run before create_inertial / export. MCP: forge_mesh_check .
docs.title: forge.mesh_check()

docs.text: Requires: the active object is TENDON . Appends an item to obj.Forge_Tendon.targets.items and sets active_index to the new last entry (fill target / coef afterwards via property access). No MCP wrapper — prefer forge_set_tendon_targets(name, [...]) which replaces the whole ordered path.
docs.title: forge.add_tendon_target_item()

docs.text: Requires: the active object is TENDON . Removes the item at Forge_Tendon.targets.active_index and clamps the index. No MCP wrapper — prefer forge_set_tendon_targets .
docs.title: forge.remove_tendon_target_item()

docs.text: Modal ( BaseProgressOperator ). filepath argument wins, else the main scene's Forge_Props.import_file_path ; missing file cancels. Destructive : clears scene objects, collections, non-main scenes and orphaned data before rebuilding the model (stage order: compiler → option → statistic → visual → asset → worldbody → contact → equality → tendon → actuator → sensor → replicates). Requires the Forge Library asset library (auto-recreated from the addon's lib/assets when missing). MCP: forge_import_mjcf (sets import_file_path / import_material , invokes, waits for is_importing to clear).
docs.title: forge.import_mjcf(filepath)

docs.text: Modal . No filepath parameter — always writes the main scene's Forge_Props.export_path (resolved against the blend file when rel_path is set). Stage order: gather assets → export images / hfields / visual meshes / collider meshes → XML sections (include, compiler, option, statistic, visual, asset, world, contact, equality, tendon, actuator, sensor) → write file. update_forge_only skips asset file writes; use_glb switches visual mesh format. Empty mesh visuals/colliders (zero vertices or triangles) are skipped, so no mesh asset or <geom mesh="..."> reference is emitted. A World environment image connected through an Environment Texture is exported as <texture type="envhdr"> and restored to the main scene World on import. MCP: forge_export_mjcf (sets export_path + rel_path=False and the two flags, refuses existing destinations without overwrite=True , waits for is_exporting to clear).
docs.title: forge.export_mjcf()

docs.text: Modal . Requires: exactly 1 selected [LINK, REPLICATE, FRAME] object (becomes the attach parent), or nothing selected. Reads the main scene's Forge_Temp_Props : tmp_file , tmp_model , tmp_prefix , tmp_link — all must be non-empty (file must exist). Imports the external model into its own scene / collection, then creates the attach reference. A file already include d in the scene yields an empty attach task list and reports Attach fail: list index out of range ; attach and include take separate files. MCP: forge_create_attach (sets Forge_Temp_Props directly from the file / model / prefix / link arguments and waits).
docs.title: forge.create_attach()

docs.text: Modal . Requires: nothing selected. Reads Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include ; imports the file's collections into the scene but only an <include> tag is written on export (file content never exported). MCP: forge_create_include (sets tmp_include directly).
docs.title: forge.create_include()

docs.text: UI file browser ( *.xml ) feeding create_attach . On execute stores Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file , derives tmp_model (basename) and tmp_prefix ( model + "_" ), resets tmp_link to "None" . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props directly (what forge_create_attach does); drivable via EXEC_DEFAULT with filepath=... .
docs.title: forge.temp_file(filepath)

docs.text: UI enum dialog listing the <body> links parsed from Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file ( get_link_names identifiers); stores the choice in tmp_link . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_link directly with the link identifier.
docs.title: forge.temp_link(tmp_link)

docs.text: UI file browser ( *.xml ) feeding create_include ; stores Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include directly.
docs.title: forge.temp_include(filepath)

docs.text: UI file browser; stores the chosen path in Forge_Props.import_file_path (used by import_mjcf invoke). Agent path: assign Forge_Props.import_file_path directly.
docs.title: forge.file_path(filepath)

docs.text: UI file browser; appends .xml when missing and stores Forge_Props.export_path ; sets rel_path=True when the path lies under the blend file's directory (stores a blend-relative path), else rel_path=False . Agent path: assign Forge_Props.export_path (+ rel_path ) directly.
docs.title: forge.export_path(filepath)

docs.text: Requires: object mode with one or more selected VISUAL objects; needs the coacd python package (install via addon preferences pip). Decomposes triangle faces from the evaluated mesh without applying a Triangulate modifier to or deleting the source object; processing can take minutes. Creates one mesh object per convex hull in the source object's first collection, named from the add-on preference coacd_name_template ( ? → source object name, # → 1-based zero-padded hull index). Each hull has Forge_Model_Type='COLLIDER' , geometry type MESH , the source's world transform, and the same parent as the source. Key parameters: threshold (concavity termination), max_convex_hull (only with merge ), preprocess_mode in [Auto, On, Off] , sampling / MCTS controls, decimate + max_ch_vertex , extrude + extrude_margin , seed . MCP: forge_coacd (single object by name).
docs.title: forge.coacds(threshold=0.05, max_convex_hull=-1, preprocess_mode='Auto', preprocess_resolution=50, resolution=2000, mcts_nodes=20, mcts_iterations=100, mcts_max_depth=3, pca=False, merge=True, decimate=False, max_ch_vertex=128, extrude=False, extrude_margin=0.01, apx_mode='CH', seed=0)

docs.text: All 16 open invoke_props_dialog windows whose edits happen through the live UI; their execute is a no-op for agents. Every value they expose is reachable by direct property assignment — see the parameter reference in the modify skill. Never call them from scripts. forge.properties_global — scene Forge_GlobalConfig ( compiler / option / statistic ). forge.properties_visual — scene Forge_VisualConfig ( <visual> section groups). forge.properties_link , forge.properties_shape , forge.properties_shape_site , forge.properties_hfield , forge.properties_plane , forge.properties_joint , forge.properties_actuator , forge.properties_tendon , forge.properties_equality , forge.properties_contact , forge.properties_sensor , forge.properties_light , forge.properties_camera , forge.properties_replicate — per-object Forge_<Type> property groups.
docs.title: UI-only popup operators

docs.text: Not model-authoring; manage the environment and the MCP bridge itself. No MCP wrappers. forge.pip_install(package) — install / upgrade a python package into Blender's environment (addon preferences dependency rows). forge.ensure_pip() — bootstrap pip / setuptools / wheel when missing. forge.mcp_server_start — start the in-Blender TCP bridge the MCP server connects to; refuses in --background mode (use blender --background --command forge_mcp instead). forge.mcp_server_stop — stop the bridge and unregister its polling timer.
docs.title: Addon infrastructure operators

docs.text: Forge operators ¶ Complete inventory of every bpy.ops.forge.* operator implemented by the Forge addon ( addon/Forge ): signature with defaults, selection requirement ( poll ), behavior and the MCP tool that wraps it. Workflow rules live in the create / modify skills — this guide is the exhaustive lookup; fetch a single entry with forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") . Agent usage rules ¶ Contract : this inventory is the complete supported operator surface. Strictly follow it — never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. When an operator, parameter or enum value you need is not documented here or in the create / modify skills, it has no supported implementation: report the missing capability as feedback instead of improvising a workaround. Operators are grouped below as creation, definition, utility, file/IO, CoACD, UI-only popups, and add-on infrastructure. Sources: ops/creation.py , ops/materials.py , ops/definition.py , ops/utilities.py , ops/io_ops.py , ops/coacd.py , ops/properties_operators.py , core/props.py , settings.py , mcp/operator.py . Selection semantics: every poll below means each selected object must match the listed Forge_Model_Type set ( check_selected_model_types , all-of). Operators additionally allowing an empty selection say "or nothing selected". Creation/definition operators read the ordered selection ( selected_order custom property) — MCP select=[...] lists set that order. Creation / definition operators open a parameter dialog only via INVOKE_DEFAULT ; calling with EXEC_DEFAULT plus keyword arguments runs headless — this is what the MCP wrappers do. Prefer the wrapper ( forge_create_* , forge_define_* , ...) whenever one exists: it manages selection, waits for modal jobs and returns created names. Modal operators ( import_mjcf , export_mjcf , create_attach , create_include ) return RUNNING_MODAL and keep working on a UI timer; poll Forge_Props.is_importing / is_exporting / is_attaching / is_including for completion, or use the MCP wrappers that wait. Every modal operation also claims the scene-level slot Forge_Props.modal_operation_active (with modal_operation_name / token / status / message ); a second modal operator fails while the slot is held — read, never write, these state properties. UI-only operators (section below) cannot be driven by agents — the agent path is direct property assignment ( obj.Forge_<Type>.<property> , scene.Forge_Props , scene.Forge_Temp_Props ) documented in the modify skill. File-browser helpers ( forge.temp_file etc.) are drivable via EXEC_DEFAULT with an explicit filepath , but setting the target property directly is simpler and is what the MCP wrappers do. Creation operators ¶ forge.create_geometry(geometry_type='BOX', size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] , or nothing selected. One visual per selected object as its child at local [0, 0, 0] ; nothing selected → standalone visual in the World collection at the 3D cursor. geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] (MESH excluded); size param per type: BOX → size_box (full dimensions), SPHERE → size_radius , CAPSULE / CYLINDER → size_radius + size_height (full straight-section height; the socket stores the same full height). MCP: forge_create_geometry . forge.create_collider(collider_type='BOX', create_method='GEOMETRY_TYPE', auto_size=False, use_min_as_height=False, size_box=(1, 1, 1), size_radius=0.5, size_height=1) ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME] , or all VISUAL , or nothing selected. create_method='GEOMETRY_TYPE' (default): only with visual selection — auto-detects shape from each visual ( MESH included); size params unused and collider_type is ignored (the collider takes the visual's own geometry type). create_method='COLLIDER_TYPE' : explicit collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH] with size params or auto_size=True (measure from selected visual); MESH bakes the visual geometry into a convex mesh collider and needs a visual selection. auto_size=True is ignored with a link / frame selection or no selection: with no selected visual to measure, explicit size parameters (or their defaults) are used. A replicate selection is not accepted by this operator. use_min_as_height=True : CAPSULE/CYLINDER only — the height is taken from the selected visual 's smallest bounding-box axis rather than its largest, and the shape is oriented along that axis. Only effective together with auto_size=True ; with explicit size_radius / size_height the values are used as given and the flag is ignored. MCP: forge_create_collider (exposes this parameter as min_is_height ). forge.create_height_field() ¶ Requires: nothing selected. Creates a root hfield node (no parent) in the World collection at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_height_field . forge.create_plane() ¶ Requires: nothing selected. Creates a root plane node (no parent) in the World collection at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_plane . forge.create_site(site_type='SPHERE', size_box=(0.2, 0.2, 0.2), size_radius=0.1, size_height=0.2) ¶ Requires: selection all LINK . One site per selected link as its child. site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] ; size param mapping as create_geometry . MCP: forge_create_site . forge.create_link() ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] , or all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER] , or nothing selected. No parameters. Based on [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] → child at local [0, 0, 0] ; based on VISUAL / COLLIDER with forge parent → sibling under that parent at the object's local position; based on parentless VISUAL / COLLIDER → link at the object's location marked Root Link ; nothing selected → World collection root candidate (mark with forge.mark_root_link ). MCP: forge_create_link . forge.create_joint(joint_type='HINGE') ¶ Requires: selection all LINK . One joint per selected link as its child. joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] . MCP: forge_create_joint . forge.create_actuator(actuator_type='POSITION') ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, JOINT, TENDON] . One actuator per selected target. actuator_type in [GENERAL, MOTOR, POSITION, VELOCITY, ADHESION] . MCP: forge_create_actuator . forge.create_tendon(tendon_type='FIXED') ¶ Requires: at least 2 selected, all JOINT , every joint subtype in [SLIDE, HINGE] . Creates a single tendon from the ordered selection; each target item exports coef (default 0.5 ). tendon_type currently only FIXED . MCP: forge_create_tendon . forge.create_equality(equality_type='CONNECT') ¶ Requires: exactly 2 selected, all LINK , all JOINT or all SITE . Dynamic type items: JOINT selection → JOINT only (joint-coupling equality); LINK / SITE selection → CONNECT / WELD . Ordered selection: first object is target1 , second is target2 . MCP: forge_create_equality . forge.create_sensor(Sensor_Type, set_ref=False, set_xbody=False, set_subtree=False) ¶ Requires: selection all LINK , all JOINT , all SITE , all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER] , or all in [LINK, SITE, VISUAL, COLLIDER, CAMERA] (mixed — also covers camera-only selections). Available Sensor_Type items are computed from the selection / flags — full ranges in the create skill (joint → Jointpos / Jointvel ; site → Touch … Contact ; link → frame + subtree types; visual/collider → frame types + Contact ; camera → frame types only). set_ref=True : needs exactly 2 selected — first is target, second is reference. set_xbody / set_subtree : only for LINK targets, mutually exclusive ( xbody → xbody frame sensors, subtree → Contact only). Contact subtree workflow: require exactly two LINK roots and use both set_ref=True and set_subtree=True . Ordered selection maps the first root to subtree1 ( target ), the second to subtree2 ( ref ); both must be explicitly set and verified in the exported sensor. MCP: forge_create_sensor . forge.create_contact(contact_type) ¶ Requires: at least 2 selected, all LINK , or all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER, PLANE, HFIELD] . Dynamic type items: LINK selection → EXCLUDE (default); geom selection → PAIR (default). Creates one contact per pair combination of the ordered selection (n·(n−1)/2 objects). MCP: forge_create_contact . forge.create_light(light_type, light_mode) ¶ Requires: selection all LINK , or nothing selected. Dynamic items: nothing selected → light_type [DIRECTIONAL, SPOT, POINT] , light_mode [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (defaults DIRECTIONAL / FIXED ); links selected → light_type [SPOT, POINT] (default SPOT ); 1–2 links → light_mode full [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default TARGETBODY ), 3+ links or nothing selected → [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default FIXED ). 1 link + TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM → single world light at the 3D cursor targeting that link; 2 links + targeting mode → single light, first selected is position, second is target; otherwise one light per link as its child. Nothing selected → world light at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_light . forge.create_camera(camera_type='PERSPECTIVE', camera_mode) ¶ Requires: selection all LINK , or nothing selected. camera_type in [PERSPECTIVE, ORTHOGRAPHIC] . Dynamic camera_mode : 1–2 links selected → full [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default TARGETBODY ); nothing or 3+ links selected → [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default FIXED ). 1 link + targeting mode → single world camera at the 3D cursor targeting that link; 2 links + targeting mode → single camera, first selected is position, second is target; otherwise one camera per link as its child. Nothing selected → world camera at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_camera . forge.create_frame() ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, REPLICATE, FRAME] , or nothing selected. One frame per selected object as its child; nothing selected → World root at the 3D cursor. Shift+Click in the UI reverses parenting (selected objects become children of the new frame) — reverse_parent is a plain class attribute, not an operator parameter; scripts use forge_define_parent instead. MCP: forge_create_frame . forge.create_replicate(count=0, sep='', offset=(0, 0, 0), euler=(0, 0, 0)) ¶ Requires: selection non-empty and all in [CAMERA, LIGHT, VISUAL, COLLIDER, SITE, LINK, FRAME, ATTACH, REPLICATE] . Creates a single replicate object with the selection as its sources; copies differ by offset / euler and are named with sep . Moves the sources (with their subtrees) into the replicate's own collection, created viewport-hidden. Blender cannot select objects there, so a later operator over them selects nothing and fails its poll ( context is incorrect ). MCP: forge_create_replicate . forge.create_inertial(inertial_model_type='VISUAL', check_mesh_valid=False) ¶ Requires: selection all LINK (links without children are skipped). Collects children of the selected type ( VISUAL or COLLIDER ), recursively through FRAME descendants, without entering child LINK hierarchies; needs at least one matching geometry object. Mesh validation runs only when check_mesh_valid=True . A failed check skips the Link. Primitive shapes use analytic mass and inertia; MESH geometry requires TetGen. A successful calculation creates a new INERTIAL child without replacing existing inertials. MCP: forge_create_inertial uses the defaults above and accepts only select . For the other calculation options, use the documented operator parameters through forge_execute . forge.create_material(category, material, use_existing=True) ¶ Requires: selection non-empty and all in [VISUAL, HFIELD, PLANE] (materials can be assigned to visual, height-field and plane geometry). category / material are exact bundled Forge PBR library names; use_existing=True assigns an existing same-named datablock as-is, False always rebuilds (Blender suffixes the taken name). Assignment uses the first object-level material slot, creating it when empty; the operator does not write primitive geometry-node material sockets. MCP: forge_create_material . forge.assign_material(material) ¶ Requires: selection non-empty and all in [VISUAL, HFIELD, PLANE] . material is the exact name of an existing Blender material, including any Blender suffix. Reuses its nodes and settings as-is, assigning the first object-level material slot on each selected object. Does not create or copy a material; other slots and unselected object assignments are preserved. MCP: call through forge_execute after reading the modify skill. Definition operators ¶ forge.define_model_type(Model_Type) ¶ Requires: selection all UNDEFINED (plain Blender objects). Available Model_Type from the Blender object type: EMPTY → LINK ; MESH → VISUAL or COLLIDER ; LIGHT → LIGHT ; CAMERA → CAMERA . Side effects: VISUAL sets geometry type MESH , group 2 , contype / conaffinity 0 , prefix GEO_ ; COLLIDER sets type MESH , group 3 , prefix COL_ ; LINK prefix LNK_ ; LIGHT maps Blender type ( SUN → DIRECTIONAL , else SPOT / POINT , AREA cancels), mode FIXED , prefix LIT_ ; CAMERA maps ORTHO / PERSP (others cancel), mode FIXED , prefix CAM_ . Objects move to the matching type collection ( WORLD when parentless). MCP: forge_define_model_type . forge.define_geometry_type(geometry_type='MESH', apply_to_all=False) ¶ Requires: selection all VISUAL . geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH] ; size preserved when switching shapes; to MESH bakes current geometry and unlocks scale; from MESH uses object dimensions as size. apply_to_all=False applies to the active object only. MCP: forge_define_geometry_type . forge.define_collider_type(collider_type='SPHERE', apply_to_all=False) ¶ Requires: selection all COLLIDER . Behavior as define_geometry_type (size preserved, MESH bakes). MCP: forge_define_collider_type . forge.define_site_type(site_type='SPHERE', apply_to_all=False) ¶ Requires: selection all SITE . site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] ; size preserved. MCP: forge_define_site_type . forge.define_joint_type(joint_type='HINGE', apply_to_all=False) ¶ Requires: selection all JOINT . joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] ; updates the joint shape gizmo. MCP: forge_define_joint_type . forge.define_actuator_type(actuator_type='POSITION', apply_to_all=False) ¶ Requires: selection all ACTUATOR . actuator_type in [GENERAL, MOTOR, POSITION, VELOCITY, ADHESION] . MCP: forge_define_actuator_type . forge.define_parent() ¶ Requires: an active object plus selection. Active VISUAL is refused — a collider under a visual is not exported. Active in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] → parents selected objects of type [LINK, VISUAL, COLLIDER, JOINT, SITE, LIGHT, CAMERA, FRAME, REPLICATE, ATTACH] to it; children of a selected VISUAL are lifted to the same parent first. Active object itself is skipped. World position of children is preserved. Every reparented object moves into the collection of its model type ( visual → Visual , collider → Collider , …), so a root object in World leaves it. Ordered selection matters: parent first, children after (MCP forge_define_parent ). MCP: forge_define_parent . Utility operators ¶ forge.batch_rename(new_name='', numerate='###') ¶ Requires: any selection. Renames each selected object to {new_name}_{index} with zero padding of numerate length, index from 0 in Blender's selected-object iteration order; this is not the recorded click order. MCP: forge_batch_rename . forge.set_instance_idname() ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, VISUAL] . Applies only to selected LINK objects (Frame and Visual objects are skipped): writes obj["INSTANCE_IDNAME"] = Forge_Props.instance_body (an object reference that survives renames), or removes the property when no instance body is chosen. Reports how many links were marked / cleared. Links already marked INSTANCE_LINK are refused (warning). The instance source is a link marked with INSTANCE_LINK (via forge.mark_instance_link ); Forge_Props.instance_body (panel Instance field) only accepts marked links. A marked instance link never appears as a <body> in the multibody tree; a referenced one feeds the <asset> section with its subtree's meshes / materials, while an unreferenced one exports nothing at all (warned). Export semantics: the instance link's children are written into every link marked with INSTANCE_IDNAME = <instance link name> . Each such link keeps its own body element (name / pos / quat / link props) but its children are replaced by the copy, with every element name prefixed "<instance>_<name>" (camera / light target refs inside the subtree renamed too). Instance subtrees gather no assets of their own, and global sections ( actuator / sensor / tendon / equality / contact ) are not duplicated per instance — don't reference instance-link-internal elements from them. A marked link nested inside a template subtree is never copied as a <body> either — its content still only exports through the placeholders referencing it. MCP: forge_set_instance_idname . forge.select_by_tag() ¶ Requires: object mode. Adds every scene object whose name contains the main scene's Forge_Props.select_tag to the current selection — it does not clear first, so pre-selected objects stay selected. An empty select_tag matches every object name ( "" is contained in any string) and therefore selects the whole scene. MCP: forge_select_by_tag . forge.select_by_model_type() ¶ Requires: Object Mode. Adds selectable objects whose Forge type matches the main scene's Forge_Props.select_model_type to the current selection; existing selection is preserved. No dedicated MCP wrapper. Set Forge_Props.select_model_type and invoke the documented operator through forge_execute when needed. forge.select_hulls() ¶ Requires: object mode. Selects every scene object whose full name matches the addon preference coacd_name_template interpreted as a pattern ( ? → any name segment, # → digits) — the same template CoACD uses to name hulls. MCP: forge_select_hulls . forge.scale_gizmo_size() ¶ No poll. Sets gizmo display of selected objects — or all objects in the blend file when nothing is selected — using the main scene's Forge_Props.gizmo_scale relative to each object's stored base size: modifier Socket_0 for JOINT / CONTACT / EQUALITY / TENDON / ACTUATOR / SENSOR , empty_display_size for LINK / FRAME / ATTACH . INERTIAL display is determined by mass and inertia and is excluded. MCP: forge_scale_gizmo_size . forge.mark_root_link() ¶ Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] . Parentless objects are marked with obj["Root Link"] = True ; objects that have a parent are first unparented while preserving world transform, then marked. MCP: forge_mark_root_link . forge.mark_instance_link() ¶ Requires: selection all LINK . Toggles obj["INSTANCE_LINK"] = True per selected link (run again to unmark); reports how many links were marked / unmarked. A marked instance link never exports as a <body> ; its children are written under every INSTANCE_IDNAME link. A referenced marked link feeds the <asset> section with its subtree's meshes / materials; an unreferenced one exports nothing at all (warned). Forge_Props.instance_body 's picker only lists marked links. MCP: forge_mark_instance_link . forge.mesh_check() ¶ Requires: selection all VISUAL . Reports self- and pairwise intersections (boundary-only contact and separating coplanar faces are valid — details in the modify skill). Run before create_inertial / export. MCP: forge_mesh_check . forge.add_tendon_target_item() ¶ Requires: the active object is TENDON . Appends an item to obj.Forge_Tendon.targets.items and sets active_index to the new last entry (fill target / coef afterwards via property access). No MCP wrapper — prefer forge_set_tendon_targets(name, [...]) which replaces the whole ordered path. forge.remove_tendon_target_item() ¶ Requires: the active object is TENDON . Removes the item at Forge_Tendon.targets.active_index and clamps the index. No MCP wrapper — prefer forge_set_tendon_targets . File and IO operators ¶ forge.import_mjcf(filepath) ¶ Modal ( BaseProgressOperator ). filepath argument wins, else the main scene's Forge_Props.import_file_path ; missing file cancels. Destructive : clears scene objects, collections, non-main scenes and orphaned data before rebuilding the model (stage order: compiler → option → statistic → visual → asset → worldbody → contact → equality → tendon → actuator → sensor → replicates). Requires the Forge Library asset library (auto-recreated from the addon's lib/assets when missing). MCP: forge_import_mjcf (sets import_file_path / import_material , invokes, waits for is_importing to clear). forge.export_mjcf() ¶ Modal . No filepath parameter — always writes the main scene's Forge_Props.export_path (resolved against the blend file when rel_path is set). Stage order: gather assets → export images / hfields / visual meshes / collider meshes → XML sections (include, compiler, option, statistic, visual, asset, world, contact, equality, tendon, actuator, sensor) → write file. update_forge_only skips asset file writes; use_glb switches visual mesh format. Empty mesh visuals/colliders (zero vertices or triangles) are skipped, so no mesh asset or <geom mesh="..."> reference is emitted. A World environment image connected through an Environment Texture is exported as <texture type="envhdr"> and restored to the main scene World on import. MCP: forge_export_mjcf (sets export_path + rel_path=False and the two flags, refuses existing destinations without overwrite=True , waits for is_exporting to clear). forge.create_attach() ¶ Modal . Requires: exactly 1 selected [LINK, REPLICATE, FRAME] object (becomes the attach parent), or nothing selected. Reads the main scene's Forge_Temp_Props : tmp_file , tmp_model , tmp_prefix , tmp_link — all must be non-empty (file must exist). Imports the external model into its own scene / collection, then creates the attach reference. A file already include d in the scene yields an empty attach task list and reports Attach fail: list index out of range ; attach and include take separate files. MCP: forge_create_attach (sets Forge_Temp_Props directly from the file / model / prefix / link arguments and waits). forge.create_include() ¶ Modal . Requires: nothing selected. Reads Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include ; imports the file's collections into the scene but only an <include> tag is written on export (file content never exported). MCP: forge_create_include (sets tmp_include directly). forge.temp_file(filepath) ¶ UI file browser ( *.xml ) feeding create_attach . On execute stores Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file , derives tmp_model (basename) and tmp_prefix ( model + "_" ), resets tmp_link to "None" . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props directly (what forge_create_attach does); drivable via EXEC_DEFAULT with filepath=... . forge.temp_link(tmp_link) ¶ UI enum dialog listing the <body> links parsed from Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file ( get_link_names identifiers); stores the choice in tmp_link . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_link directly with the link identifier. forge.temp_include(filepath) ¶ UI file browser ( *.xml ) feeding create_include ; stores Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include directly. forge.file_path(filepath) ¶ UI file browser; stores the chosen path in Forge_Props.import_file_path (used by import_mjcf invoke). Agent path: assign Forge_Props.import_file_path directly. forge.export_path(filepath) ¶ UI file browser; appends .xml when missing and stores Forge_Props.export_path ; sets rel_path=True when the path lies under the blend file's directory (stores a blend-relative path), else rel_path=False . Agent path: assign Forge_Props.export_path (+ rel_path ) directly. CoACD ¶ forge.coacds(threshold=0.05, max_convex_hull=-1, preprocess_mode='Auto', preprocess_resolution=50, resolution=2000, mcts_nodes=20, mcts_iterations=100, mcts_max_depth=3, pca=False, merge=True, decimate=False, max_ch_vertex=128, extrude=False, extrude_margin=0.01, apx_mode='CH', seed=0) ¶ Requires: object mode with one or more selected VISUAL objects; needs the coacd python package (install via addon preferences pip). Decomposes triangle faces from the evaluated mesh without applying a Triangulate modifier to or deleting the source object; processing can take minutes. Creates one mesh object per convex hull in the source object's first collection, named from the add-on preference coacd_name_template ( ? → source object name, # → 1-based zero-padded hull index). Each hull has Forge_Model_Type='COLLIDER' , geometry type MESH , the source's world transform, and the same parent as the source. Key parameters: threshold (concavity termination), max_convex_hull (only with merge ), preprocess_mode in [Auto, On, Off] , sampling / MCTS controls, decimate + max_ch_vertex , extrude + extrude_margin , seed . MCP: forge_coacd (single object by name). UI-only popup operators ¶ All 16 open invoke_props_dialog windows whose edits happen through the live UI; their execute is a no-op for agents. Every value they expose is reachable by direct property assignment — see the parameter reference in the modify skill. Never call them from scripts. forge.properties_global — scene Forge_GlobalConfig ( compiler / option / statistic ). forge.properties_visual — scene Forge_VisualConfig ( <visual> section groups). forge.properties_link , forge.properties_shape , forge.properties_shape_site , forge.properties_hfield , forge.properties_plane , forge.properties_joint , forge.properties_actuator , forge.properties_tendon , forge.properties_equality , forge.properties_contact , forge.properties_sensor , forge.properties_light , forge.properties_camera , forge.properties_replicate — per-object Forge_<Type> property groups. Addon infrastructure operators ¶ Not model-authoring; manage the environment and the MCP bridge itself. No MCP wrappers. forge.pip_install(package) — install / upgrade a python package into Blender's environment (addon preferences dependency rows). forge.ensure_pip() — bootstrap pip / setuptools / wheel when missing. forge.mcp_server_start — start the in-Blender TCP bridge the MCP server connects to; refuses in --background mode (use blender --background --command forge_mcp instead). forge.mcp_server_stop — stop the bridge and unregister its polling timer.

docs.text: Complete inventory of every bpy.ops.forge.* operator implemented by the Forge addon ( addon/Forge ): signature with defaults, selection requirement ( poll ), behavior and the MCP tool that wraps it. Workflow rules live in the create / modify skills — this guide is the exhaustive lookup; fetch a single entry with forge_skill(name="operators", section="<operator name>") .
docs.title: Forge operators

docs.text: Contract : this inventory is the complete supported operator surface. Strictly follow it — never read, search or infer behavior from the addon source code ( addon/Forge/** ); source internals are not part of the interface. When an operator, parameter or enum value you need is not documented here or in the create / modify skills, it has no supported implementation: report the missing capability as feedback instead of improvising a workaround. Operators are grouped below as creation, definition, utility, file/IO, CoACD, UI-only popups, and add-on infrastructure. Sources: ops/creation.py , ops/materials.py , ops/definition.py , ops/utilities.py , ops/io_ops.py , ops/coacd.py , ops/properties_operators.py , core/props.py , settings.py , mcp/operator.py . Selection semantics: every poll below means each selected object must match the listed Forge_Model_Type set ( check_selected_model_types , all-of). Operators additionally allowing an empty selection say "or nothing selected". Creation/definition operators read the ordered selection ( selected_order custom property) — MCP select=[...] lists set that order. Creation / definition operators open a parameter dialog only via INVOKE_DEFAULT ; calling with EXEC_DEFAULT plus keyword arguments runs headless — this is what the MCP wrappers do. Prefer the wrapper ( forge_create_* , forge_define_* , ...) whenever one exists: it manages selection, waits for modal jobs and returns created names. Modal operators ( import_mjcf , export_mjcf , create_attach , create_include ) return RUNNING_MODAL and keep working on a UI timer; poll Forge_Props.is_importing / is_exporting / is_attaching / is_including for completion, or use the MCP wrappers that wait. Every modal operation also claims the scene-level slot Forge_Props.modal_operation_active (with modal_operation_name / token / status / message ); a second modal operator fails while the slot is held — read, never write, these state properties. UI-only operators (section below) cannot be driven by agents — the agent path is direct property assignment ( obj.Forge_<Type>.<property> , scene.Forge_Props , scene.Forge_Temp_Props ) documented in the modify skill. File-browser helpers ( forge.temp_file etc.) are drivable via EXEC_DEFAULT with an explicit filepath , but setting the target property directly is simpler and is what the MCP wrappers do.

One visual per selected object as its child at local [0, 0, 0] ; nothing selected → standalone visual in the World collection at the 3D cursor. geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] (MESH excluded); size param per type: BOX → size_box (full dimensions), SPHERE → size_radius , CAPSULE / CYLINDER → size_radius + size_height (full straight-section height; the socket stores the same full height). docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME] , or all VISUAL , or nothing selected. create_method='GEOMETRY_TYPE' (default): only with visual selection — auto-detects shape from each visual ( MESH included); size params unused and collider_type is ignored (the collider takes the visual's own geometry type). create_method='COLLIDER_TYPE' : explicit collider_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH] with size params or auto_size=True (measure from selected visual); MESH bakes the visual geometry into a convex mesh collider and needs a visual selection. auto_size=True is ignored with a link / frame selection or no selection: with no selected visual to measure, explicit size parameters (or their defaults) are used. A replicate selection is not accepted by this operator. use_min_as_height=True : CAPSULE/CYLINDER only — the height is taken from the selected visual 's smallest bounding-box axis rather than its largest, and the shape is oriented along that axis. Only effective together with auto_size=True ; with explicit size_radius / size_height the values are used as given and the flag is ignored. MCP: forge_create_collider (exposes this parameter as min_is_height ).

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK , all JOINT , all SITE , all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER] , or all in [LINK, SITE, VISUAL, COLLIDER, CAMERA] (mixed — also covers camera-only selections). Available Sensor_Type items are computed from the selection / flags — full ranges in the create skill (joint → Jointpos / Jointvel ; site → Touch … Contact ; link → frame + subtree types; visual/collider → frame types + Contact ; camera → frame types only). set_ref=True : needs exactly 2 selected — first is target, second is reference. set_xbody / set_subtree : only for LINK targets, mutually exclusive ( xbody → xbody frame sensors, subtree → Contact only). Contact subtree workflow: require exactly two LINK roots and use both set_ref=True and set_subtree=True . Ordered selection maps the first root to subtree1 ( target ), the second to subtree2 ( ref ); both must be explicitly set and verified in the exported sensor. MCP: forge_create_sensor .
docs.title: forge.create_sensor(Sensor_Type, set_ref=False, set_xbody=False, set_subtree=False)

docs.text: Requires: at least 2 selected, all LINK , or all in [VISUAL, COLLIDER, PLANE, HFIELD] . Dynamic type items: LINK selection → EXCLUDE (default); geom selection → PAIR (default). Creates one contact per pair combination of the ordered selection (n·(n−1)/2 objects). MCP: forge_create_contact .
docs.title: forge.create_contact(contact_type)

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK , or nothing selected. Dynamic items: nothing selected → light_type [DIRECTIONAL, SPOT, POINT] , light_mode [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (defaults DIRECTIONAL / FIXED ); links selected → light_type [SPOT, POINT] (default SPOT ); 1–2 links → light_mode full [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default TARGETBODY ), 3+ links or nothing selected → [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default FIXED ). 1 link + TARGETBODY / TARGETBODYCOM → single world light at the 3D cursor targeting that link; 2 links + targeting mode → single light, first selected is position, second is target; otherwise one light per link as its child. Nothing selected → world light at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_light .
docs.title: forge.create_light(light_type, light_mode)

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK , or nothing selected. camera_type in [PERSPECTIVE, ORTHOGRAPHIC] . Dynamic camera_mode : 1–2 links selected → full [TARGETBODY, TARGETBODYCOM, FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default TARGETBODY ); nothing or 3+ links selected → [FIXED, TRACK, TRACKCOM] (default FIXED ). 1 link + targeting mode → single world camera at the 3D cursor targeting that link; 2 links + targeting mode → single camera, first selected is position, second is target; otherwise one camera per link as its child. Nothing selected → world camera at the 3D cursor. MCP: forge_create_camera .
docs.title: forge.create_camera(camera_type='PERSPECTIVE', camera_mode)

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, REPLICATE, FRAME] , or nothing selected. One frame per selected object as its child; nothing selected → World root at the 3D cursor. Shift+Click in the UI reverses parenting (selected objects become children of the new frame) — reverse_parent is a plain class attribute, not an operator parameter; scripts use forge_define_parent instead. MCP: forge_create_frame .
docs.title: forge.create_frame()

docs.text: Requires: selection non-empty and all in [CAMERA, LIGHT, VISUAL, COLLIDER, SITE, LINK, FRAME, ATTACH, REPLICATE] . Creates a single replicate object with the selection as its sources; copies differ by offset / euler and are named with sep . Moves the sources (with their subtrees) into the replicate's own collection, created viewport-hidden. Blender cannot select objects there, so a later operator over them selects nothing and fails its poll ( context is incorrect ). MCP: forge_create_replicate .
docs.title: forge.create_replicate(count=0, sep='', offset=(0, 0, 0), euler=(0, 0, 0))

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK (links without children are skipped). Collects children of the selected type ( VISUAL or COLLIDER ), recursively through FRAME descendants, without entering child LINK hierarchies; needs at least one matching geometry object. Mesh validation runs only when check_mesh_valid=True . A failed check skips the Link. Primitive shapes use analytic mass and inertia; MESH geometry requires TetGen. A successful calculation creates a new INERTIAL child without replacing existing inertials. MCP: forge_create_inertial uses the defaults above and accepts only select . For the other calculation options, use the documented operator parameters through forge_execute .
docs.title: forge.create_inertial(inertial_model_type='VISUAL', check_mesh_valid=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection non-empty and all in [VISUAL, HFIELD, PLANE] (materials can be assigned to visual, height-field and plane geometry). category / material are exact bundled Forge PBR library names; use_existing=True assigns an existing same-named datablock as-is, False always rebuilds (Blender suffixes the taken name). Assignment uses the first object-level material slot, creating it when empty; the operator does not write primitive geometry-node material sockets. MCP: forge_create_material .
docs.title: forge.create_material(category, material, use_existing=True)

docs.text: Requires: selection non-empty and all in [VISUAL, HFIELD, PLANE] . material is the exact name of an existing Blender material, including any Blender suffix. Reuses its nodes and settings as-is, assigning the first object-level material slot on each selected object. Does not create or copy a material; other slots and unselected object assignments are preserved. MCP: call through forge_execute after reading the modify skill.
docs.title: forge.assign_material(material)

docs.text: Requires: selection all UNDEFINED (plain Blender objects). Available Model_Type from the Blender object type: EMPTY → LINK ; MESH → VISUAL or COLLIDER ; LIGHT → LIGHT ; CAMERA → CAMERA . Side effects: VISUAL sets geometry type MESH , group 2 , contype / conaffinity 0 , prefix GEO_ ; COLLIDER sets type MESH , group 3 , prefix COL_ ; LINK prefix LNK_ ; LIGHT maps Blender type ( SUN → DIRECTIONAL , else SPOT / POINT , AREA cancels), mode FIXED , prefix LIT_ ; CAMERA maps ORTHO / PERSP (others cancel), mode FIXED , prefix CAM_ . Objects move to the matching type collection ( WORLD when parentless). MCP: forge_define_model_type .
docs.title: forge.define_model_type(Model_Type)

docs.text: Requires: selection all VISUAL . geometry_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE, MESH] ; size preserved when switching shapes; to MESH bakes current geometry and unlocks scale; from MESH uses object dimensions as size. apply_to_all=False applies to the active object only. MCP: forge_define_geometry_type .
docs.title: forge.define_geometry_type(geometry_type='MESH', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all COLLIDER . Behavior as define_geometry_type (size preserved, MESH bakes). MCP: forge_define_collider_type .
docs.title: forge.define_collider_type(collider_type='SPHERE', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all SITE . site_type in [BOX, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, SPHERE] ; size preserved. MCP: forge_define_site_type .
docs.title: forge.define_site_type(site_type='SPHERE', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all JOINT . joint_type in [FREE, BALL, SLIDE, HINGE] ; updates the joint shape gizmo. MCP: forge_define_joint_type .
docs.title: forge.define_joint_type(joint_type='HINGE', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: selection all ACTUATOR . actuator_type in [GENERAL, MOTOR, POSITION, VELOCITY, ADHESION] . MCP: forge_define_actuator_type .
docs.title: forge.define_actuator_type(actuator_type='POSITION', apply_to_all=False)

docs.text: Requires: an active object plus selection. Active VISUAL is refused — a collider under a visual is not exported. Active in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] → parents selected objects of type [LINK, VISUAL, COLLIDER, JOINT, SITE, LIGHT, CAMERA, FRAME, REPLICATE, ATTACH] to it; children of a selected VISUAL are lifted to the same parent first. Active object itself is skipped. World position of children is preserved. Every reparented object moves into the collection of its model type ( visual → Visual , collider → Collider , …), so a root object in World leaves it. Ordered selection matters: parent first, children after (MCP forge_define_parent ). MCP: forge_define_parent .
docs.title: forge.define_parent()

docs.text: Requires: any selection. Renames each selected object to {new_name}_{index} with zero padding of numerate length, index from 0 in Blender's selected-object iteration order; this is not the recorded click order. MCP: forge_batch_rename .
docs.title: forge.batch_rename(new_name='', numerate='###')

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, VISUAL] . Applies only to selected LINK objects (Frame and Visual objects are skipped): writes obj["INSTANCE_IDNAME"] = Forge_Props.instance_body (an object reference that survives renames), or removes the property when no instance body is chosen. Reports how many links were marked / cleared. Links already marked INSTANCE_LINK are refused (warning). The instance source is a link marked with INSTANCE_LINK (via forge.mark_instance_link ); Forge_Props.instance_body (panel Instance field) only accepts marked links. A marked instance link never appears as a <body> in the multibody tree; a referenced one feeds the <asset> section with its subtree's meshes / materials, while an unreferenced one exports nothing at all (warned). Export semantics: the instance link's children are written into every link marked with INSTANCE_IDNAME = <instance link name> . Each such link keeps its own body element (name / pos / quat / link props) but its children are replaced by the copy, with every element name prefixed "<instance>_<name>" (camera / light target refs inside the subtree renamed too). Instance subtrees gather no assets of their own, and global sections ( actuator / sensor / tendon / equality / contact ) are not duplicated per instance — don't reference instance-link-internal elements from them. A marked link nested inside a template subtree is never copied as a <body> either — its content still only exports through the placeholders referencing it. MCP: forge_set_instance_idname .
docs.title: forge.set_instance_idname()

docs.text: Requires: object mode. Adds every scene object whose name contains the main scene's Forge_Props.select_tag to the current selection — it does not clear first, so pre-selected objects stay selected. An empty select_tag matches every object name ( "" is contained in any string) and therefore selects the whole scene. MCP: forge_select_by_tag .
docs.title: forge.select_by_tag()

docs.text: Requires: Object Mode. Adds selectable objects whose Forge type matches the main scene's Forge_Props.select_model_type to the current selection; existing selection is preserved. No dedicated MCP wrapper. Set Forge_Props.select_model_type and invoke the documented operator through forge_execute when needed.
docs.title: forge.select_by_model_type()

docs.text: Requires: object mode. Selects every scene object whose full name matches the addon preference coacd_name_template interpreted as a pattern ( ? → any name segment, # → digits) — the same template CoACD uses to name hulls. MCP: forge_select_hulls .
docs.title: forge.select_hulls()

docs.text: No poll. Sets gizmo display of selected objects — or all objects in the blend file when nothing is selected — using the main scene's Forge_Props.gizmo_scale relative to each object's stored base size: modifier Socket_0 for JOINT / CONTACT / EQUALITY / TENDON / ACTUATOR / SENSOR , empty_display_size for LINK / FRAME / ATTACH . INERTIAL display is determined by mass and inertia and is excluded. MCP: forge_scale_gizmo_size .
docs.title: forge.scale_gizmo_size()

docs.text: Requires: selection all in [LINK, FRAME, REPLICATE] . Parentless objects are marked with obj["Root Link"] = True ; objects that have a parent are first unparented while preserving world transform, then marked. MCP: forge_mark_root_link .
docs.title: forge.mark_root_link()

docs.text: Requires: selection all LINK . Toggles obj["INSTANCE_LINK"] = True per selected link (run again to unmark); reports how many links were marked / unmarked. A marked instance link never exports as a <body> ; its children are written under every INSTANCE_IDNAME link. A referenced marked link feeds the <asset> section with its subtree's meshes / materials; an unreferenced one exports nothing at all (warned). Forge_Props.instance_body 's picker only lists marked links. MCP: forge_mark_instance_link .
docs.title: forge.mark_instance_link()

docs.text: Requires: selection all VISUAL . Reports self- and pairwise intersections (boundary-only contact and separating coplanar faces are valid — details in the modify skill). Run before create_inertial / export. MCP: forge_mesh_check .
docs.title: forge.mesh_check()

docs.text: Requires: the active object is TENDON . Appends an item to obj.Forge_Tendon.targets.items and sets active_index to the new last entry (fill target / coef afterwards via property access). No MCP wrapper — prefer forge_set_tendon_targets(name, [...]) which replaces the whole ordered path.
docs.title: forge.add_tendon_target_item()

docs.text: Requires: the active object is TENDON . Removes the item at Forge_Tendon.targets.active_index and clamps the index. No MCP wrapper — prefer forge_set_tendon_targets .
docs.title: forge.remove_tendon_target_item()

docs.text: Modal ( BaseProgressOperator ). filepath argument wins, else the main scene's Forge_Props.import_file_path ; missing file cancels. Destructive : clears scene objects, collections, non-main scenes and orphaned data before rebuilding the model (stage order: compiler → option → statistic → visual → asset → worldbody → contact → equality → tendon → actuator → sensor → replicates). Requires the Forge Library asset library (auto-recreated from the addon's lib/assets when missing). MCP: forge_import_mjcf (sets import_file_path / import_material , invokes, waits for is_importing to clear).
docs.title: forge.import_mjcf(filepath)

docs.text: Modal . No filepath parameter — always writes the main scene's Forge_Props.export_path (resolved against the blend file when rel_path is set). Stage order: gather assets → export images / hfields / visual meshes / collider meshes → XML sections (include, compiler, option, statistic, visual, asset, world, contact, equality, tendon, actuator, sensor) → write file. update_forge_only skips asset file writes; use_glb switches visual mesh format. Empty mesh visuals/colliders (zero vertices or triangles) are skipped, so no mesh asset or <geom mesh="..."> reference is emitted. A World environment image connected through an Environment Texture is exported as <texture type="envhdr"> and restored to the main scene World on import. MCP: forge_export_mjcf (sets export_path + rel_path=False and the two flags, refuses existing destinations without overwrite=True , waits for is_exporting to clear).
docs.title: forge.export_mjcf()

docs.text: Modal . Requires: exactly 1 selected [LINK, REPLICATE, FRAME] object (becomes the attach parent), or nothing selected. Reads the main scene's Forge_Temp_Props : tmp_file , tmp_model , tmp_prefix , tmp_link — all must be non-empty (file must exist). Imports the external model into its own scene / collection, then creates the attach reference. A file already include d in the scene yields an empty attach task list and reports Attach fail: list index out of range ; attach and include take separate files. MCP: forge_create_attach (sets Forge_Temp_Props directly from the file / model / prefix / link arguments and waits).
docs.title: forge.create_attach()

docs.text: Modal . Requires: nothing selected. Reads Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include ; imports the file's collections into the scene but only an <include> tag is written on export (file content never exported). MCP: forge_create_include (sets tmp_include directly).
docs.title: forge.create_include()

docs.text: UI file browser ( *.xml ) feeding create_attach . On execute stores Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file , derives tmp_model (basename) and tmp_prefix ( model + "_" ), resets tmp_link to "None" . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props directly (what forge_create_attach does); drivable via EXEC_DEFAULT with filepath=... .
docs.title: forge.temp_file(filepath)

docs.text: UI enum dialog listing the <body> links parsed from Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_file ( get_link_names identifiers); stores the choice in tmp_link . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_link directly with the link identifier.
docs.title: forge.temp_link(tmp_link)

docs.text: UI file browser ( *.xml ) feeding create_include ; stores Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include . Agent path: assign Forge_Temp_Props.tmp_include directly.
docs.title: forge.temp_include(filepath)

docs.text: UI file browser; stores the chosen path in Forge_Props.import_file_path (used by import_mjcf invoke). Agent path: assign Forge_Props.import_file_path directly.
docs.title: forge.file_path(filepath)

docs.text: UI file browser; appends .xml when missing and stores Forge_Props.export_path ; sets rel_path=True when the path lies under the blend file's directory (stores a blend-relative path), else rel_path=False . Agent path: assign Forge_Props.export_path (+ rel_path ) directly.
docs.title: forge.export_path(filepath)

docs.text: Requires: object mode with one or more selected VISUAL objects; needs the coacd python package (install via addon preferences pip). Decomposes triangle faces from the evaluated mesh without applying a Triangulate modifier to or deleting the source object; processing can take minutes. Creates one mesh object per convex hull in the source object's first collection, named from the add-on preference coacd_name_template ( ? → source object name, # → 1-based zero-padded hull index). Each hull has Forge_Model_Type='COLLIDER' , geometry type MESH , the source's world transform, and the same parent as the source. Key parameters: threshold (concavity termination), max_convex_hull (only with merge ), preprocess_mode in [Auto, On, Off] , sampling / MCTS controls, decimate + max_ch_vertex , extrude + extrude_margin , seed . MCP: forge_coacd (single object by name).
docs.title: forge.coacds(threshold=0.05, max_convex_hull=-1, preprocess_mode='Auto', preprocess_resolution=50, resolution=2000, mcts_nodes=20, mcts_iterations=100, mcts_max_depth=3, pca=False, merge=True, decimate=False, max_ch_vertex=128, extrude=False, extrude_margin=0.01, apx_mode='CH', seed=0)

docs.text: All 16 open invoke_props_dialog windows whose edits happen through the live UI; their execute is a no-op for agents. Every value they expose is reachable by direct property assignment — see the parameter reference in the modify skill. Never call them from scripts. forge.properties_global — scene Forge_GlobalConfig ( compiler / option / statistic ). forge.properties_visual — scene Forge_VisualConfig ( <visual> section groups). forge.properties_link , forge.properties_shape , forge.properties_shape_site , forge.properties_hfield , forge.properties_plane , forge.properties_joint , forge.properties_actuator , forge.properties_tendon , forge.properties_equality , forge.properties_contact , forge.properties_sensor , forge.properties_light , forge.properties_camera , forge.properties_replicate — per-object Forge_<Type> property groups.
docs.title: UI-only popup operators

docs.text: Not model-authoring; manage the environment and the MCP bridge itself. No MCP wrappers. forge.pip_install(package) — install / upgrade a python package into Blender's environment (addon preferences dependency rows). forge.ensure_pip() — bootstrap pip / setuptools / wheel when missing. forge.mcp_server_start — start the in-Blender TCP bridge the MCP server connects to; refuses in --background mode (use blender --background --command forge_mcp instead). forge.mcp_server_stop — stop the bridge and unregister its polling timer.
docs.title: Addon infrastructure operators
